Text in another language with few or no accented letters cannot be told apart from English, so name a multilingual model for it. Pin `hexgrad/kokoro-82m` to never switch: an unknown voice is then `validation_failed` and an outage `provider_error`. While it is not listed, `hexgrad/kokoro-82m` and its `af_`/`am_`/`bf_`/`bm_` voices are refused.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/audio/speech \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: 9c7e…" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "text": "Your order has shipped and arrives Thursday." }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const speech = await naive.media.audio.speak({ text: "Your order has shipped and arrives Thursday." });
const wav = await naive.files.downloadBytes(speech.file.id);
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media speak "Your order has shipped and arrives Thursday." | jq -r .file.id | xargs naive file download > shipped.wav
```

```json 200 OK theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "speech_generation",
  "model": "openai/gpt-audio-mini",
  "file": {
    "id": "fil_01j9x3d7k2m4n6p8q0r2s4t6u8",
    "object": "file",
    "name": "fil_01j9x3d7k2m4n6p8q0r2s4t6u8.wav",
    "content_type": "audio/wav",
    "size_bytes": 134444,
    "scope": "published",
    "session_id": null,
    "sha256": "3f…",
    "created_at": "2026-09-06T10:00:01Z"
  },
  "duration_seconds": 2.8,
  "cost_micro_usd": 640
}
```

On `hexgrad/kokoro-82m`, the cost is its seconds of audio at the rate above, rounded up to a whole micro-dollar. Another model's cost is settled from the provider's usage record after the audio is returned. When that record is not yet available, the call is billed at the `media` component's floor rather than held.

## Converse

`POST /v1/media/audio/conversations` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) required

Synchronous, like speech: one spoken turn in, the spoken reply out, as a stored file. The input is a stored file only — [upload](/docs/api/files#upload-a-file) or [import](/docs/api/files#import-a-file-from-a-url) a recording first; the CLI does both for you.

**file\_id** `string` *required*

A stored audio file, `fil_…`, holding the turn to answer.

**model** `string` (default: s2s/auto)

A model from [`GET /v1/media/models?kind=s2s`](#the-catalogues).

**voice** `string`

One of the voices the model offers. Omitted, the model's default.

**format** `string` (default: mp3)

`mp3` · `wav` · `ogg`, a preference: the catalogue's conversation models reply in WAV whatever is asked, and the file's `content_type` says so.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/audio/conversations \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: b81d…" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "file_id": "fil_01j9x3f0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8j9", "format": "wav" }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const reply = await naive.media.audio.converse({ file_id: turn.id, format: "wav" });
const wav = await naive.files.downloadBytes(reply.file.id);
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media converse ./question.wav | jq -r .file.id | xargs naive file download > reply.wav
```

The reply is a `speech_generation`, the same object [Speak](#speak) answers, with `model` naming the conversation model or alias that ran.

## Sound effects

`POST /v1/media/sound-effects` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) required

Synchronous, like speech: a text prompt in, a short generated clip out, saved to [Files](/docs/api/files) as a `fil_`. This is not speech — it turns a description (`"a heavy wooden door slamming shut, echoing"`) into an effect — so it takes no `voice` and no `model`; the reply names none. Inside a session it is the [`generate_sound_effect`](/docs/capabilities/tools#audio-tools) tool.

**prompt** `string` *required*

What to generate, 1–500 characters.

**duration\_seconds** `number`

How long the clip should be, 0.5–30. Omitted, the generator picks a length to fit the prompt.

**loop** `boolean` (default: false)

Make the clip loop seamlessly — for ambience and backgrounds.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/sound-effects \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: 2d6a…" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "prompt": "a heavy wooden door slamming shut, echoing", "duration_seconds": 3 }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const sound = await naive.media.soundEffects.generate({
  prompt: "a heavy wooden door slamming shut, echoing",
  duration_seconds: 3,
});
const mp3 = await naive.files.downloadBytes(sound.file.id);
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media sound-effect "a heavy wooden door slamming shut, echoing" | jq -r .file.id | xargs naive file download > door.mp3
```

```json 200 OK theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "sound_generation",
  "file": {
    "id": "fil_01j9x3g4m6p8q0r2s4t6u8v0w2",
    "object": "file",
    "name": "fil_01j9x3g4m6p8q0r2s4t6u8v0w2.mp3",
    "content_type": "audio/mpeg",
    "size_bytes": 48192,
    "scope": "published",
    "session_id": null,
    "sha256": "7a…",
    "created_at": "2026-09-06T10:00:02Z"
  },
  "duration_seconds": 3,
  "cost_micro_usd": 7800
}
```

The cost is settled from the clip the generator returns — its length in seconds, never more than 30 — after the audio lands, billed once on the `media` component under the `Idempotency-Key`.

## Music

`POST /v1/media/music` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) required

Synchronous, like sound effects: a text prompt in, an original song out, saved to [Files](/docs/api/files) as a `fil_`. Describe the genre, mood, instrumentation and any lyrics (`"an upbeat synthwave track with driving bass and bright arpeggios"`); it takes no `voice` and no `model`, and the reply names none. Inside a session it is the [`generate_music`](/docs/capabilities/tools#audio-tools) tool.

**prompt** `string` *required*

What to generate, 1–2 000 characters.

**length\_seconds** `number`

How long the song should be, 3–300. Omitted, 30.

**instrumental** `boolean` (default: false)

Force an instrumental track with no vocals.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/music \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: 4f8c…" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "prompt": "an upbeat synthwave track with driving bass and bright arpeggios", "length_seconds": 30 }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const song = await naive.media.music.generate({
  prompt: "an upbeat synthwave track with driving bass and bright arpeggios",
  length_seconds: 30,
});
const mp3 = await naive.files.downloadBytes(song.file.id);
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media music "an upbeat synthwave track with driving bass and bright arpeggios" | jq -r .file.id | xargs naive file download > track.mp3
```

```json 200 OK theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "music_generation",
  "file": {
    "id": "fil_01j9x3g4m6p8q0r2s4t6u8v0w2",
    "object": "file",
    "name": "fil_01j9x3g4m6p8q0r2s4t6u8v0w2.mp3",
    "content_type": "audio/mpeg",
    "size_bytes": 481920,
    "scope": "published",
    "session_id": null,
    "sha256": "9c…",
    "created_at": "2026-09-06T10:00:30Z"
  },
  "duration_seconds": 30,
  "cost_micro_usd": 97500
}
```

The cost is settled from the song the generator returns — its length in seconds, never more than 300 — after the audio lands, billed once on the `media` component under the `Idempotency-Key`.

## The catalogues

[`GET /v1/media/models`](/docs/api/media) answers the audio models too: `kind=stt`, `kind=tts` and `kind=s2s` each list the managed alias for that direction first, then the pinned models cheapest-first where a published price exists. Each row's `description` carries the published price per second or per request where there is one. Voices are the model's own: a speech or conversation model accepts the voice names its maker publishes, and the managed aliases pick a voice when none is named.

## Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| - | - | - |
| `402` | `insufficient_credits` | The prepaid balance is empty. Nothing is sent to the provider. |
| `404` | `not_found` | `file_id` names no file of yours; `GET` names no transcription of yours. |
| `400` | `validation_failed` | Both or neither of `file_id`/`url`; a `file_id` or `url` that is not an audio or video recording (an image, a page, a document), refused before any model hears it; a `url` at a private host, over 100 MiB or that does not answer `2xx`; `text` over 4 096 characters; a sound-effect `prompt` over 500 characters or a `duration_seconds` outside 0.5–30; a music `prompt` over 2 000 characters or a `length_seconds` outside 3–300; a `voice` the model does not offer; a `model` the catalogue does not have; audio the model cannot read. `param` names the field. |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | The provider is throttling. Retry after a moment with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `501` | `feature_not_configured` | This deploy has no audio provider configured, or its account can no longer be billed. |
| `502` | `provider_error` | The provider failed. Retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |


# Audit logs
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/audit-logs

A queryable, principal-attributed record of control-plane actions.

The **audit log** is an append-only record of who did what on the control plane. Every sensitive mutation — an [agent](/docs/api/agents) update, a key rotation, a role change, a denied policy, a credit top-up — is captured as an immutable entry attributed to the acting **principal** (a member or an API key). Use it to answer "who changed this, when, and from which request?" for security review, incident response, and compliance.

Reads require the `audit:read` [scope](/docs/api/authentication#scopes). Entries are never modified or deleted; the log only grows.

## The audit entry object

**id** `string`

Entry id (e.g. `aud_01H...`).

**actor** `object`

The principal that performed the action.

**actor**

**type** `string`

`user` (a member acting in the dashboard) or `key` (an API key acting programmatically).

**id** `string`

Id of the member (`usr_…`) or API key (`key_…`).

**action** `string`

The audited action (see [Audited actions](#audited-actions)).

**resource\_type** `string`

The kind of resource affected (e.g. `agent`, `api_key`, `member`, `webhook_endpoint`, `session`, `credits`).

**resource\_id** `string | null`

Id of the affected resource, when the action targets one.

**request\_id** `string`

The `x-request-id` of the request that produced the entry — join this to your own logs and to the [error envelope](/docs/api/errors).

**metadata** `object`

Action-specific detail (e.g. the before/after role on a role change, the `to_version` on a rollback, the denied tool on a policy denial).

**created\_at** `string`

When the action occurred.

## List audit logs

`GET /v1/audit_logs` returns entries newest-first. Cursor-paginated — see [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

### Filters

**actor** `string`

Filter to a single principal id (a member `usr_…` or key `key_…`).

**resource** `string`

Filter to a single resource id (e.g. a specific `agt_…`).

**action** `string`

Filter to one action string (e.g. `api_key.rotated`).

**request\_id** `string`

Filter to the entries one request wrote, by the `request_id` it carried.

**from** `string`

Lower bound (inclusive) on `created_at`: a date like `2026-08-01` or a timestamp like `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z` (send an offset's `+` as `%2B`). Anything else is `400 validation_failed` with `param: "from"`.

**to** `string`

Upper bound (exclusive) on `created_at`: a date like `2026-08-01` or a timestamp like `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z` (send an offset's `+` as `%2B`). Anything else is `400 validation_failed` with `param: "to"`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/audit_logs?action=member.role_changed&from=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "aud_01H9MM...",
      "object": "audit_entry",
      "actor": { "type": "user", "id": "usr_01H8AA..." },
      "action": "member.role_changed",
      "resource_type": "member",
      "resource_id": "mem_01H9JJ...",
      "request_id": "req_01H9MM...",
      "metadata": { "from_role": "member", "to_role": "admin" },
      "created_at": "2026-08-20T18:02:11Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "aud_01H9ML...",
      "object": "audit_entry",
      "actor": { "type": "key", "id": "key_01H8XK..." },
      "action": "api_key.rotated",
      "resource_type": "api_key",
      "resource_id": "key_01H8XK...",
      "request_id": "req_01H9ML...",
      "metadata": { "reason": "scheduled_rotation" },
      "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:59:40Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "aud_01H9ML..."
}
```

## Audited actions

The following control-plane actions are captured in the initial release. The list grows over time; treat `action` as an open string and branch on the prefixes you care about.

| Action | Resource | Recorded when |
| - | - | - |
| `agent.updated` | `agent` | An [agent](/docs/api/agents) configuration is changed (new version). |
| `agent.rolled_back` | `agent` | An agent is rolled back to a prior version. `metadata.to_version` carries the target. |
| `api_key.created` | `api_key` | A new [API key](/docs/api/authentication) is issued. |
| `api_key.rotated` | `api_key` | A key's secret is rotated. |
| `api_key.revoked` | `api_key` | A key is revoked. |
| `member.role_changed` | `member` | A [member's](/docs/api/organizations) role changes. `metadata` carries `from_role`/`to_role`. |
| `member.removed` | `member` | A member is removed (triggering the removal cascade). |
| `policy.denied` | `session` | A [permission policy](/docs/api/agents) blocks a tool call (the persisted trace of a `403 forbidden`). |
| `credits.topped_up` | `topup` | A [top-up](/docs/api/credits) succeeds, or free credit is granted to your balance. `metadata.source` says which kind of grant it was. |
| `credits.adjusted` | `ledger_entry` | Support corrects your balance downward. `metadata.amount_micro_usd` is the (negative) amount and `metadata.note` the reason. |
| `webhook.secret_rotated` | `webhook_endpoint` | A [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) signing secret is rotated. |
| `session.interrupted` | `session` | A running [session](/docs/api/sessions) is interrupted. |
| `app.db_rest` | `app` | A [database REST](/docs/api/database) call runs as the service role. `metadata` carries the method and path. |
| `app.db_migrated` | `app` | A [migration](/docs/api/database) is applied to an app's database. |
| `app.bucket_created` | `app` | A [storage](/docs/api/storage) bucket is created. `metadata.bucket` names it. |
| `app.bucket_deleted` | `app` | A storage bucket is deleted (with `metadata.force` when it was emptied first). |
| `app.storage_put` | `app` | An object is written — inline, through a signed upload URL (`metadata.signed`), or by an agent's `storage_put`. `metadata` carries `bucket` and `key`, never the bytes. |
| `app.storage_get` | `app` | An object is read, or a signed download URL issued (`metadata.signed`). |
| `app.storage_deleted` | `app` | An object is deleted. |
| `file.imported` | `file` | A [URL import](/docs/api/files#import-a-file-from-a-url) lands. `metadata.url` is the address fetched. |
| `browser.session_opened` | `browser_session` | A [browser](/docs/api/browser) is opened over REST — lazily, on the first action. An agent's `browser` tool emits a `browser.session.opened` [event](/docs/api/events) instead. |
| `browser.session_closed` | `browser_session` | A REST-opened browser is closed and its minutes settled. |
| `browser.live_view_opened` | `browser_session` | A [live view](/docs/api/browser-sessions#open-a-live-view) is minted for a browser session. `metadata` carries `computer_id` and `expires_at`, never the URL. |
| `browser.context_saved` | `browser_context` | A [saved login](/docs/api/browser#save-a-login) is saved from a browser. |
| `browser.context_granted` | `browser_grant` | A saved login is [granted](/docs/api/browser#grant-a-saved-login) to an agent or role. |
| `browser.context_revoked` | `browser_context` | A saved login is [deleted](/docs/api/browser#revoke-a-saved-login), with every grant on it. `metadata.context_id` names it. |
| `browser.credential_stored` | `vault_credential` | A login [credential is saved](/docs/api/browser#save-a-credential) to a vault. `metadata` carries `service` and `identity_id`, never the secret. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Each entry pins the exact `request_id`, so an audited action, its [error envelope](/docs/api/errors) (if it failed), and your own request logs all correlate on one id. Money movements additionally carry an `actor` on the [ledger](/docs/api/credits#ledger), so spend is attributable without cross-referencing the audit log.


# Authentication
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/authentication

Organization-scoped API keys and the Bearer scheme.

The Naive Managed Agents API authenticates with **organization-scoped API keys**. Every key belongs to a single [organization](/docs/api/organizations) and can act only on that org's resources and credit balance.

## The Bearer scheme

Send your key in the `Authorization` header on every request:

```bash theme={"system"}
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
```

A missing or invalid key returns `401 unauthorized`. A valid key acting outside its scopes returns `403 forbidden`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Live keys are prefixed `sk_live_` and are shown **once** at creation. Store them in a secret manager — they cannot be retrieved again, only rotated.

## Scopes

Keys carry scopes that limit what they can do. Scopes follow a `resource:action` grammar (e.g. `agents:write`, `sessions:read`). Every key names at least one; grant `admin` for full access to the organization.

| Scope | Grants |
| - | - |
| `agents:read` / `agents:write` | Read or manage [agents](/docs/api/agents). |
| `sessions:read` / `sessions:write` | Read or run [sessions](/docs/api/sessions). |
| `computers:write` | Manage [computers](/docs/api/computers), and read what commands run on them printed ([command history](/docs/api/computers#command-history)). |
| `proxy:write` | Call the [model proxy](/docs/api/proxy) and [choose a model](/docs/api/models#choose-a-model-for-a-conversation) for it — nothing else. |
| `files:read` / `files:write` | Read or upload [files](/docs/api/files). |
| `billing:read` / `billing:write` | Read the [credits](/docs/api/credits) balance and ledger / charge a payment method to top up. |
| `webhooks:*` | Manage [webhook endpoints](/docs/api/webhooks), rotate secrets, and read delivery logs. |
| `audit:read` | Read the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs). |
| `admin` | Manage members, keys, and organization settings. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `proxy:write` is deliberately narrow. The proxy routes accept it **or** `sessions:write`, so a key that reaches them today keeps working — but a credential that holds only `proxy:write` can make model calls and cannot start, cancel or read sessions. That is what makes it safe to hand to a sandbox: a harness that runs as a process inside a micro-VM needs a credential to reach the door, and one that leaked should not be able to run sessions for your organization.
>
> `webhooks:*` is one scope, spelled with the star: it is the only webhook scope, and it covers both reading and managing endpoints. `billing:write` gates the card-charging top-up endpoint and is deliberately separate from read-only `billing:read`.

## Who is this credential?

`GET /v1/me` answers from the credential alone — no scope, no organization id in the request. It is
the first call any client should make, and it is how the CLI and the dashboard learn which
organization a key belongs to instead of asking you to paste an `org_` id you have no way to look
up.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "identity",
  "principal": { "type": "key", "id": "key_01H8AA..." },
  "organization": { "id": "org_01H8AA...", "name": "Acme", "mode": "live" },
  "scopes": ["admin"],
  "user": null
}
```

`organization` is `null` only for a signed-in person who does not belong to one yet; `user` is
`null` whenever the caller is an API key rather than a person.

`GET /v1/organizations` is the list form. An API key reaches exactly the one organization it is
bound to — a one-row page, never another tenant's row. A signed-in person reaches every
organization they are a member of. Cursor-paginated, see [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

## Signing a person in

A **person** authenticates with an email address and password and receives a short-lived bearer
session token prefixed `vt_`. It is accepted anywhere an `sk_` key is, on the same
`Authorization: Bearer` header, and its scopes are derived from the member's role.

```bash theme={"system"}
POST /v1/auth/session
```

**email** `string`

The account's email address. Required with `password` when signing in fresh; omitted when re-scoping an existing `vt_` token.

**password** `string`

The account's password. Paired with `email`.

**provider\_token** `string`

The access token an external provider sign-in came back with. Verified against the provider on every call; never decoded here. Used instead of `email`/`password`.

**organization\_id** `string`

The organization to scope the session to. With an existing `vt_` token this re-scopes the session — the org switcher. Must be an organization the person belongs to.

```json Request theme={"system"}
{ "email": "ada@acme.test", "password": "..." }
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "auth_session",
  "token": "vt_...",
  "expires_at": "2026-08-22T09:00:00Z",
  "organization": { "id": "org_01H8AA...", "name": "Acme", "mode": "live" }
}
```

Presenting an existing `vt_` token to the same route with an `organization_id` re-scopes the session
to another organization you belong to — that is what an organization switcher is. Passing an
`organization_id` you are not a member of returns `404 not_found`. The new token keeps the presented
token's `expires_at`: re-scoping never extends a session. Sign in again to start a new 30 days.

### Signing in with Google

The dashboard offers "Continue with Google" wherever the deployment has the provider turned on. It
is the same route and the same session at the end of it: the provider hands back an access token,
and that token is exchanged for a `vt_`.

```json Request theme={"system"}
{ "provider_token": "..." }
```

The token is **verified against the provider on every call** — it is never decoded or taken at face
value, so a forged, expired or revoked one is `401 unauthorized`, phrased exactly as a wrong
password is.

Two things are worth knowing before you build against it:

* **The address must be one your provider has verified.** You are matched to your organizations by
  email address, so an unverified address is refused rather than signed in. Google verifies the
  addresses it asserts, so this is invisible in practice.
* **It signs you in; it does not enrol you.** Signing in with Google as somebody who belongs to no
  organization gives you the same session a password sign-in would: `organization_id: null`, no
  scopes, and the choice of joining one or creating one. Your role and scopes always come from your
  membership — never from how you signed in, and never from anything the caller asks for.

`POST /v1/auth/users` registers a person:

**email** `string` *required*

The address to register. Must be confirmed by mail before sign-in succeeds.

**password** `string` *required*

At least 8 characters.

**return\_to** `string`

Which app the confirmation link opens. `creator` sends it to the creator platform; omitted, it opens the dashboard.

```json Request theme={"system"}
{ "email": "ada@acme.test", "password": "..." }
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "auth_user",
  "email": "ada@acme.test",
  "confirmation_required": true,
  "hint": "If no email arrives, this address may already have an account: sign in or reset your password."
}
```

`confirmation_required: true` means the address must be confirmed by mail before
`POST /v1/auth/session` will succeed — the response never pretends the person is signed in.

The answer is the same whether or not the address already has an account, so it never tells anyone who has one. An address whose account is already confirmed is sent nothing. `hint` says so on every answer: if no email arrives, sign in, or [reset the password](#password-reset-and-confirmation).

Registering the same address more than five times in a minute answers `429 rate_limited`, as do more than 60 registrations a minute from one connecting address.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Session tokens are for interactive clients. Machine-to-machine callers should hold a scoped API key:
> a token expires and a key does not.

## Password reset and confirmation

`POST /v1/auth/recover` starts a password reset:

**email** `string` *required*

The address to send the reset link to.

`POST /v1/auth/confirmations` re-sends the
confirmation for an address that has not been proved yet:

**email** `string` *required*

The address to re-send the confirmation to.

Both answer `202` with the same body **whether or not that address has an account** — an endpoint that
answered differently would be a way to discover who your users are. Do not branch on it; there is
nothing to branch on.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "object": "auth_recovery", "delivery": "sent" }
```

`delivery` is `sent` when the message was handed to a mailer and `undeliverable` when the deployment
has none attached. It describes the *deployment*, never the address, which is why it is safe to show
a caller: it lets a sign-in screen say "check your inbox" or "nothing will arrive, ask an operator"
truthfully, without either state being hard-coded.

`POST /v1/auth/password` finishes a reset with the token the emailed link carried:

**token** `string` *required*

The single-use token from the emailed link.

**password** `string` *required*

The new password. At least 8 characters.

```json Request theme={"system"}
{ "token": "...", "password": "..." }
```

It answers `200` with `{ "object": "auth_password", "updated": true }`, or `401` when the token is
expired or already spent. This one *is* allowed to refuse out loud — the caller already holds the
credential, so saying it is dead discloses nothing.

Both mailed routes are rate limited per address.

## Create an API key

`POST /v1/api_keys` → `201 Created`. Creates a new key for the caller's organization. The plaintext `secret` is returned only in this response.

**name** `string` *required*

Human-readable label for the key.

**scopes** `string[]` *required*

Scopes to grant. At least one; `admin` for full org access.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/api_keys \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{ "name": "ci", "scopes": ["agents:write", "sessions:write"] }'
```

**id** `string`

The key id (e.g. `key_01H...`).

**name** `string`

The label you supplied.

**secret** `string`

The plaintext key. Returned only once.

**scopes** `string[]`

Granted scopes.

**prefix** `string`

The non-secret prefix, shown in listings for identification.

**created\_by** `object`

The principal that created this key — `{ "type": "user" | "key" | "system", "id": "..." }`, the same shape the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) records.

**last\_used\_at** `string | null`

When the key was last used to authenticate a request, to within about a minute; `null` until first use.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**org\_id** `string`

The organization this key opens. Returned only at create and rotate.

**mode** `string`

`live` or `test` — the tier the key spends on. Returned only at create and rotate.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "key_01H8XK2M...",
  "object": "api_key",
  "name": "ci",
  "secret": "sk_live_9f2c...redacted",
  "prefix": "sk_live_9f2c",
  "scopes": ["agents:write", "sessions:write"],
  "created_by": { "type": "user", "id": "usr_01H8AA..." },
  "last_used_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z",
  "org_id": "org_01H8A0...",
  "mode": "live"
}
```

## List API keys

`GET /v1/api_keys` returns key metadata (never the secret). Cursor-paginated — see [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "key_01H...", "name": "ci", "prefix": "sk_live_9f2c", "scopes": ["agents:write"], "created_by": { "type": "user", "id": "usr_01H8AA..." }, "last_used_at": "2026-08-20T17:22:10Z", "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z" }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Rotate & revoke

Rotation issues a new secret and invalidates the old one. Revocation deletes the key immediately.

```bash theme={"system"}
POST   /v1/api_keys/{id}/rotate   # returns a new secret
DELETE /v1/api_keys/{id}          # revoke
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Rotate on a schedule and on any suspected exposure. Because keys are org-scoped, revoking one never affects another org's access.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Key creation, rotation, and revocation are recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `api_key.created`, `api_key.rotated`, and `api_key.revoked`, attributed to the acting principal.


# Company board
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/board

The durable coordination surface of a team: cards and comments on one board owned by the coordinator and shared by its roster.

The [company board](/docs/team/board) is the durable half of a [team](/docs/team/overview) — a coordinator's transcript scrolls away, the card that says who holds what does not. These are the routes a person, a script or a dashboard reads and writes it through; the agents themselves use the `board_read` and `board_write` tools, against the same rows. A card's `assignee` is an agent's **name**, and assigning a `todo` card with no open blocker is what [starts that agent on it](/docs/team/board#assigning-a-card-starts-the-teammate-on-it). Through these routes it starts in the same request, and the response carries `woken_session_id`; through the tool — a `create`, an `assign`, or a move that frees the card — as soon as the write lands.

## Addressing a board

A board is addressed by its `brd_` id **or** by the `agt_` id of the agent that owns it — the coordinator. That is not a convenience. A board is **minted on first write**, one per agent, and a board with no cards has never told anyone its `brd_` id — so on a brand-new team the agent id is the only reference a caller can have.

One board per agent — `unique (org_id, agent_id)` — so `POST /v1/boards` is an **ensure**, not a create that can conflict. It is also not the only way a board comes into being: the first card created against the `agt_` spelling mints one too. A read never does. Every agent on the owner's current roster reads and writes this board through the tools; a roster member has no board of its own to address here unless its own `multiagent.board` is on.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **There is no delete call.** A card is never removed: a finished card is the record of what the team was asked to do, and a task that vanishes takes the answer to "what happened here" with it. Move it to `done` instead.
>
> A board and its cards and comments are kept for the life of the organization; no sweep or expiry removes them. The one exception is [removing a template](/docs/sdk/apps#installsremove): its seed cards that are not `done` and that no person commented on go with it.

Every route here is gated by `agents:read` for reads and `agents:write` for writes: a board belongs to an agent, and the scope grammar is fixed.

## The board object

**id** `string`

Unique id (`brd_…`).

**object** `string`

Always `board`.

**agent\_id** `string`

The agent that owns the board (`agt_…`). One board per agent.

**cards** `object`

How many cards stand in each column: `{ "todo": n, "doing": n, "blocked": n, "done": n }`. All four keys are always present, so `0` and "absent" never read the same. This is a real aggregate over the board, not the length of a page — which is the one fact a page of cards cannot state, because a page is truncated and a count is not.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## The card object

**id** `string`

Unique id (`crd_…`). Derived rather than minted — from the board and the tool call for a card an agent wrote, from the board and the `key` for a card created here with one — so a retried write collides with the row it already made rather than duplicating it.

**object** `string`

Always `board_card`.

**board\_id** `string`

The board this card is on (`brd_…`).

**title** `string`

Short label, 1–200 characters.

**body** `string`

The brief — what was asked, written by whoever created the card.

**note** `string | null`

What the holder wrote back — what was done and what is left. A member cannot see another member's conversation, so this is the hand-off; `board_write update` writes it, and a `done` must carry one.

**status** `string`

One of `todo`, `doing`, `blocked`, `done`. Fixed — not configurable columns. `done` is terminal for the agents' tool; this route can still change it.

**assignee** `string | null`

An agent's **name**, not an id. `null` is unclaimed. A `todo` card with an assignee and no open blocker is due to be worked: the board's clock starts a session of that agent on it.

**blocked\_by** `string[]`

The `crd_` ids this card waits on. A `blocked` card with an empty list is stuck on the world. When every card in the list reaches `done`, this card is promoted back to `todo` — on the next read, on the next tick, and at once when a teammate's `board_write` finishes the last one on the same board.

**woken\_session\_id** `string | null`

The session (`ses_…`) the board's clock started on this card, or `null`. Set when the assignee is woken; cleared when the card is reassigned or healed back to `todo`, so the new hand is woken in turn. Read-only: it is not accepted in any request body.

**reported\_status** `string | null`

The last `done` or `blocked` status the board's owner was told about in a digest, or `null`. A card whose `status` differs from this is unreported and goes into the owner's next digest. Read-only.

**wake\_count** `integer`

How many sessions the board's clock has started for this card. A card is started at most three times; the next time it would be due it is parked `blocked` for the owner instead. A schedule's standing card is the exception: the clock never starts it — its own fire does — so the count climbs with the schedule and the cap does not apply while the card is the schedule's.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**updated\_at** `string`

Last modification timestamp.

## The comment object

**id** `string`

Unique id (`bcm_…`).

**object** `string`

Always `board_comment`.

**card\_id** `string`

The card commented on (`crd_…`).

**author** `string`

Who wrote it, as an id **the server derived** — never a name the caller supplied. A person's comment carries their `usr_` or `key_` principal; a member's, written through `board_write`, carries the `ses_` id of the thread. The prefix is what lets a reader tell an agent's comment from a person's.

**body** `string`

The comment text.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Ensure a board

`POST /v1/boards` → the board object. `201 Created` when this call minted the row, `200 OK` when it found one already there.

**agent\_id** `string` *required*

The agent that owns the board (`agt_…`). `404 not_found` if this organization has no such agent.

Calling it twice is not a conflict. There is one board per agent, so the second call answers the same board and the status code is the only difference between the two outcomes — a caller that does not care ignores it and reads the same board either way.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/boards \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "agent_id": "agt_9f2c..." }'
```

```json 201 Created theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "brd_mgng...",
  "object": "board",
  "agent_id": "agt_9f2c...",
  "cards": { "todo": 0, "doing": 0, "blocked": 0, "done": 0 },
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:02Z"
}
```

## Get a board

`GET /v1/boards/{id}` → the board object. `{id}` is a `brd_` id or the owning `agt_` id. An agent whose board has not been minted yet answers `404 not_found`; a read never creates one.

This is the read that answers a board's own id, its owner and how much work stands on it. The cards routes answer cards.

## Read an agent's board

`GET /v1/agents/{id}/board` → the agent's cards, in **column order** (`todo`, `doing`, `blocked`, `done`) and then oldest first. A team that has not started answers an empty page rather than a 404, and no board is created. `GET /v1/boards/{agt_id}/cards` answers the same empty page. This is the owner's board: a roster member has no board of its own, and its cards are on its coordinator's.

The response is the standard [pagination](/docs/api/pagination) envelope of card objects.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/agents/agt_9f2c.../board \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json 200 OK theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "crd_8k12...",
      "object": "board_card",
      "board_id": "brd_mgng...",
      "title": "Verify the Q3 numbers",
      "body": "Cross-check the filing against the model.",
      "note": "Revenue and expenses reconcile; the tax line is off by 2%, chasing it.",
      "status": "doing",
      "assignee": "fact-checker",
      "blocked_by": [],
      "woken_session_id": "ses_01j9...",
      "reported_status": null,
      "created_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:02Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:31:44Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## List a board's cards

`GET /v1/boards/{id}/cards` → the same cards, addressed by board reference. `{id}` is a `brd_` id or the owning `agt_` id. Same envelope, same column order.

## Add a card

`POST /v1/boards/{id}/cards` → `201 Created` with the card object — or, under a `key` the board has seen before, `200 OK` with the card that key already made.

**title** `string` *required*

1–200 characters.

**body** `string`

The brief, up to 20,000 characters.

**status** `string`

`todo` (default), `doing`, `blocked` or `done`. A card created with a non-empty `blocked_by` starts `blocked` unless this says otherwise.

**assignee** `string | null`

An agent's name, up to 128 characters, and it must be one a **live agent in this organization carries** — a name nobody answers to is refused (see [Refusals](#refusals)). Defaults to `null`. With an assignee and no open blocker, the card is due and the agent is started on it in this request — unless it is busy with another card on this board, when the card waits its turn. A create with a `key` is a seed, as a template's are, and is left to the board's clock.

**blocked\_by** `string[]`

Up to 50 `crd_` ids this card waits on, each a card **on this board** — any other id is refused (see [Refusals](#refusals)).

**key** `string`

An idempotency key, 1–128 characters, unique within the board. The card's id is derived from it, so a second `POST` under the same key answers the **existing** card with `200 OK` and writes nothing — the rest of the body is ignored on a replay. Without it every request writes its own card. This is what lets a [template](/docs/concepts/templates) seed a board on every apply without doubling its cards.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/boards/agt_9f2c.../cards \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "key": "q3-report:verify", "title": "Verify the Q3 numbers", "assignee": "fact-checker" }'
```

```json 201 Created theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "crd_8k12...",
  "object": "board_card",
  "board_id": "brd_mgng...",
  "title": "Verify the Q3 numbers",
  "body": "",
  "note": null,
  "status": "todo",
  "assignee": "fact-checker",
  "blocked_by": [],
  "woken_session_id": null,
  "reported_status": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:02Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:02Z"
}
```

```json 200 OK (same key again) theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "crd_8k12...",
  "object": "board_card",
  "board_id": "brd_mgng...",
  "title": "Verify the Q3 numbers",
  "body": "",
  "note": null,
  "status": "doing",
  "assignee": "fact-checker",
  "blocked_by": [],
  "woken_session_id": "ses_01j9...",
  "reported_status": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T09:14:02Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-20T09:31:44Z"
}
```

The replay answers the card as it stands now — here already claimed and being worked — not as the request described it. The status code is how a seeding script tells `created` from `unchanged`.

## Get one card

`GET /v1/boards/{id}/cards/{cid}` → the card object. A card that is not on the named board answers `404 not_found`, even if the id exists elsewhere in your organization.

## Update a card

`PATCH /v1/boards/{id}/cards/{cid}` → `200 OK` with the updated card object. Every field of the create body but `key` is accepted and every one is optional, so a move is `{"status": "doing"}` and nothing else.

**title** `string`

1–200 characters.

**body** `string`

Replaces the brief, up to 20,000 characters.

**note** `string`

Replaces the holder's note, up to 20,000 characters — the same field a member's `board_write update` writes.

**status** `string`

`todo`, `doing`, `blocked` or `done`. No race guard: a card in `done` can be moved here. A move to `done` still needs a `note` — on the call or already on the card.

**assignee** `string | null`

Hand the card to an agent by name — one a live agent in this organization carries, or the write is refused (see [Refusals](#refusals)) — or `null` to unclaim it. **Omitting the key leaves the current holder alone; sending `null` does not.** Writing this field clears `woken_session_id`, so a `todo` card handed to someone new is due again and the new assignee is started on it in this request, or after their current card if they are busy.

**blocked\_by** `string[]`

Replaces the list of `crd_` ids this card waits on, up to 50, each a card on this board. A list that names the card itself, or a card that already waits on it (directly or through others), is refused.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/boards/agt_9f2c.../cards/crd_8k12... \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "assignee": "writer" }'
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> This is an **operator's override**, and it is deliberately more powerful than the agents' own `board_write`. A person has the card on screen and outranks the claim guards, which exist only to stop two members stepping on each other — so this route never answers a refusal, and this is the only way to retitle or re-block a card after it is created.

## Refusals

The routes on this page fail the ordinary ways — `400 invalid_request` for a body the schema rejects, `404 not_found` for a board or card that is not there. The `PATCH` refuses exactly one move: `{ status: "done" }` with no `note` on the call and none on the card is `409 state_conflict`, its message opening with `missing_note`.

Both the `POST` and the `PATCH` also refuse an `assignee` that is not a live agent's name in the organization: `400 validation_failed`, `param: "assignee"`, its message opening with `unknown_member`. The clock joins `assignee` to a live agent, so a card handed to a name nobody carries would never be due and never worked — it would sit in `todo` reading "waiting to start" indefinitely. Sending `null` unclaims and is never refused. The check happens at the write: an agent renamed or deleted afterwards leaves the card holding a name nothing answers to, which the board shows as a stalled card.

Both also refuse a `blocked_by` id that is not a card on this board, and the `PATCH` one that would make the card wait on itself, directly or around a cycle: `400 validation_failed`, `param: "blocked_by"`. A card waiting on a card that does not exist could never be told it was free, and a cycle can never reach `done`.

Every other compare-and-set guard lives in the agents' `board_write`, where a lost race comes back as a named tool result rather than an error:

| Refusal | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `already_claimed` | The card is held by another teammate (on a claim), or someone is `doing` it (on an `assign`). |
| `already_working` | The writer already holds a `doing` card on this board. |
| `blocked` | The card's `blocked_by` names cards that are not `done`. |
| `already_resolved` | The card is `done`; it is not reopened or reassigned. |
| `missing_note` | A move to `done` with nothing written on the card. |
| `unknown_member` | `assign` named an agent that does not exist in the organization. The `POST` and `PATCH` above refuse the same name as a `400 validation_failed`. |
| `missing_assignee` | `assign` without an `assignee` (a name, or `null`). |
| `unknown_card` | No such card on this board. |

They are described in full on the [board page](/docs/team/board#a-write-can-be-refused-and-that-is-normal). An operator who needs the same outcome the tool refused — reopening a `done` card, say — has the `PATCH` above.

## Read a card's comments

`GET /v1/boards/{id}/cards/{cid}/comments` → the card's comments, **oldest first**, in the standard [pagination](/docs/api/pagination) envelope. A card's comments are a conversation, so they are not reversed the way a feed is.

A `cid` that is not on the named board answers `404 not_found`, the same guard the card read sits behind.

## Comment on a card

`POST /v1/boards/{id}/cards/{cid}/comments` → `201 Created` with the comment object.

**body** `string` *required*

The comment text, 1–20,000 characters.

**There is no `author` field, and sending one is a `400 invalid_request`.** The server signs the comment with the principal behind your key, so nobody has to invent a name for themselves — or for anyone else. Nothing used to stop an operator signing a comment `fact-checker`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/boards/agt_9f2c.../cards/crd_8k12.../comments \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "body": "Filing arrived; unblocked." }'
```

> [card] [The board, in concept](/docs/team/board)
>
> The four statuses, the two tools agents call, how a card starts its assignee, and how the board composes with delegation.


# Browser
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/browser

Drive a computer's managed browser over REST — actions, session state, saved logins and who may reopen them.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The option object, guards and lifetime are in the [Browser](/docs/computer/browser) guide. This page is the routes.

A [computer](/docs/api/computers) created with a `browser` block carries one **browser session**. The
first action opens it; `DELETE` closes it. Every route below takes the `computers:write` scope
unless it says otherwise. Three routes — live view, granting and revoking a saved login — answer
only a signed-in dashboard session: an API key gets `403 forbidden` whatever its scopes.

## The browser session object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `brw_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `browser_session`.

**computer\_id** `string | null`

The computer the browser runs on.

**session\_id** `string | null`

The [agent session](/docs/api/sessions) whose `browser` tool opened it; `null` for a browser opened over the API.

**status** `string`

`creating`, `active`, `closed` or `error`.

**allowed\_domains** `string[]`

The allow-list every action is checked against.

**region** `string`

`us-west`, `us-east`, `eu-central` or `ap-southeast`.

**context\_id** `string | null`

The saved login (`bct_`) this session reopened, if any.

**context\_backed** `boolean`

`true` when the session carries a saved login — `extract`, `observe`, `links` and `screenshot` then need `allow_extract`.

**timeout\_at** `string`

When the session closes on its own (`timeout_minutes` after it opened). A sweep on the platform clock closes and bills any session past it within a minute; the row is then `closed` like one you deleted.

**opened\_at** `string`

When the browser came up.

**closed\_at** `string | null`

When it closed; `null` while open.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

The live-view URL and the upstream connect URL are bearer credentials. Neither is a field on this
object, and neither appears in a tool result, an event or a log.

## Perform an action

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser/actions` — opens the browser lazily on the first call.

The body is **one action**, discriminated on `action`. `Idempotency-Key` is **required** for `goto`
and `act` and optional elsewhere.

| `action` | body | how it runs |
| - | - | - |
| `goto` | `{ url }` | deterministic |
| `click` | `{ selector }` | deterministic |
| `type` | `{ selector, text }` | deterministic; credential-shaped `text` is refused |
| `extract` | `{ instruction?, selector?, schema? }` | selector only → the element's text; with `instruction`/`schema` → model-driven, shaped to `schema` |
| `act` | `{ instruction, variables? }` | model-driven; `%name%` placeholders are filled from `variables` |
| `observe` | `{ instruction }` | model-driven → candidate elements |
| `links` | `{ contains?, limit? }` | deterministic; `limit` defaults to 50, max 200 |
| `screenshot` | `{}` | deterministic → a `fil_` file |

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H.../browser/actions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 5f3b0e2e-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "action": "act", "instruction": "search for %term%", "variables": { "term": "naive" } }'
```

Every action answers the same object:

**object** `string`

Always `browser_action`.

**action** `string`

The action that ran.

**url** `string`

The page URL after the action.

**text** `string | null`

`extract` without a schema: the text read.

**data** `unknown | null`

`extract` with a schema: the data, in that shape.

**links** `object[] | null`

`links`: `[{ href, text }]`.

**elements** `object[] | null`

`observe`: `[{ selector, description }]`.

**file\_id** `string | null`

`screenshot`: the `fil_` id of the PNG. Never the bytes.

**performed** `boolean`

Always `true` on a `200`. An `act` that did nothing is a `502 provider_error`, not a `200` with `false`.

`variables` values are never echoed — not in the result, not in the event, not in the audit row.

### What is refused

| Guard | Error |
| - | - |
| Page URL off the allow-list, or a private, loopback or metadata host — checked before **and** after every action | `403 forbidden`, `param: url` |
| Write-looking `act`, `click` or `type` (submit, purchase, delete, send, pay, confirm) without `allow_writes` | `403 forbidden`, `param: allow_writes` |
| Credential-shaped `type.text` or `act.instruction` (password, token and key patterns; vault values are sealed and never compared) — credentials travel only through [login](#log-in-with-a-saved-credential) | `400 validation_failed`, `param: text` / `instruction` |
| `extract`, `observe`, `links` or `screenshot` on a context-backed session without `allow_extract` | `403 forbidden`, `param: allow_extract` |
| An `act` the automation could not perform | `502 provider_error` |
| A `context_name` the calling agent has no grant for | `403 forbidden`, `param: context_name` |
| A `context_name` that names a saved login on more than one identity — the lookup is organization-wide by name, and a computer's options carry no identity to pick one | `400 validation_failed`, `param: context_name` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Name saved logins uniquely across the organization if more than one identity will hold them: `shop-ava` rather than two `shop`s. A name is unique per identity at save time, so the collision only arises across identities.

## Read the session

`GET /v1/computers/{id}/browser` → the [browser session](#the-browser-session-object), or `404 not_found` when none is open.

## Close the session

`DELETE /v1/computers/{id}/browser` — idempotent. The closed [browser session](#the-browser-session-object)
(`status: closed`, `closed_at` set), or `204` when nothing was open. Closing settles the session's
minutes on the `browser` line item, capped at `timeout_at`, and, on a session opened with `persist_context` or `human_login`,
writes its cookies and storage into the saved login.

## Live view

`GET /v1/computers/{id}/browser/live-view` — **dashboard session only.** A `browser_live_view`
(`{ object, url, expires_at }`) for the one browser currently open; the URL is a bearer credential
and is never logged or put in an event. An API key gets `403 forbidden`.

The dashboard's Browser tab on a computer renders it, and lists every browser the computer ever
drove — see [Browser sessions](/docs/api/browser-sessions). Never hand the URL to an agent or store it.

## Save a login

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser/context` → `201 browser_context`

A saved login is **bound when a browser opens**: the engine attaches it at session start and flushes
cookies and storage into it at close. This call therefore has two moments:

1. **No browser open on the computer** — creates the empty saved login under `name`, owned by an
   [identity](/docs/api/identities). Open the next browser with `context_name` (and `human_login` or
   `persist_context`) to fill it.
2. **A browser open with that `context_name`** — marks the login saved and releases the
   `human_login` lock; the same `bct_` comes back and the close persists the login.

On a browser open without that context the call is `400 validation_failed` (`param: context_name`):
nothing that browser holds can reach the saved login.

**name** `string` *required*

1–64 characters; unique per identity.

**identity\_id** `string` *required*

The `idn_` that owns the saved login.

**service** `string`

What the login is for, e.g. `figma.com`.

**id** `string`

`bct_` id.

**object** `string`

Always `browser_context`.

**identity\_id** `string`

The owning identity.

**name** `string`

The name a later `context_name` reopens.

**service** `string | null`

As given.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**last\_used\_at** `string | null`

When a session last reopened it.

## Grant a saved login

`POST /v1/browser/contexts/{name}/grants` — **dashboard session only** → `201 browser_grant`

A saved login is default-deny: a session may reopen it only when its agent — or the agent's member
role — holds a grant. The same grantee twice is a `200` replay of the existing grant; a new one
reaches your [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) as `browser.context.granted`. Over the REST
API, an **owner or admin** dashboard session — or an API key holding the `admin` scope — opens every
saved login of the organization without a grant; a **member** session, and any other API key, needs
the `member` role grant; an agent's `browser` tool needs a grant by its `agt_` id or by role.

**identity\_id** `string` *required*

The identity that owns `{name}`.

**grantee\_type** `string` *required*

`agent` or `role`.

**grantee\_id** `string` *required*

An `agt_` id, or `owner` / `admin` / `member`.

**id** `string`

`bgr_` id.

**object** `string`

Always `browser_grant`.

**context\_id** `string`

The `bct_` granted.

**grantee\_type** `string`

`agent` or `role`.

**grantee\_id** `string`

As given.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Revoke a saved login

`DELETE /v1/browser/contexts/{name}?identity_id=idn_...` — **dashboard session only.** Deletes the
saved login and every grant on it. `identity_id` is required. Webhooks receive
`browser.context.revoked { context_id }`.

## Log in with a saved credential

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser/login` → `browser_action`

Reads the identity's vault credential `login:<service>` and fills the form through `%username%` and
`%password%` placeholders. The plaintext never enters the model or a result.

**service** `string` *required*

The credential's service, e.g. `figma.com`.

**url** `string` *required*

The sign-in page.

**identity\_id** `string` *required*

Whose vault to read.

## Sign up

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser/signup` → `browser_action`

Generates a password, stores it as `login:<service>` in the identity's vault, then runs the sign-up
flow with it. When an agent's `browser` tool does this, the session **always pauses for a person to
confirm** — see [Tools](/docs/capabilities/tools).

**service** `string` *required*

The service being joined.

**url** `string` *required*

The sign-up page.

**identity\_id** `string` *required*

Whose vault receives the credential.

**email** `string` *required*

The address to register.

## Save a credential

`POST /v1/browser/credentials` → the [vault credential](/docs/api/vaults)'s metadata

Seals `login:<service>` into the identity's vault so `login` can use it. The reply is metadata —
no route ever returns the value.

**identity\_id** `string` *required*

Whose vault.

**service** `string` *required*

The service, e.g. `figma.com`.

**email** `string` *required*

The account's email.

**password** `string` *required*

Write-only.

**username** `string`

When the site signs in by username rather than email.

## Errors

`forbidden`, `validation_failed`, `not_found`, `context_locked` (`409` — a `human_login` flow holds
the saved login for 15 minutes), `provider_error` (`502`), `computer_unavailable`, `rate_limited`,
`feature_not_configured`. See [Errors](/docs/api/errors).


# Browser sessions
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/browser-sessions

The history of managed browsers driven beside a computer, and a view-only live view of one.

> [!NOTE]
>
> See [Browser](/docs/api/browser) for driving the browser itself — actions, close, saved logins. This page is the dashboard's read of what ran.

Every browser opened beside a computer — by an agent's `browser` tool or by `POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser/actions` — is a [browser session](/docs/api/browser#the-browser-session-object) row. These routes list a computer's rows, closed ones included, and mint a live view of one that is still open.

## The browser session object

The same object [Browser](/docs/api/browser#the-browser-session-object) returns: `id` (`brw_…`), `object: "browser_session"`, `computer_id`, `session_id` (the [agent session](/docs/api/sessions) that opened it, or `null` for one opened over the API), `status` (`creating`, `active`, `closed`, `error`), `allowed_domains`, `region`, `context_id`, `context_backed`, `timeout_at`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`, `created_at`. It never carries a provider reference.

## List browser sessions

`GET /v1/computers/{id}/browser_sessions` — any API key, the same read gate as `GET /v1/computers`

Every browser session opened beside the computer, newest first, closed sessions included. The list is **not paginated** — a computer drives a handful — so `has_more` is always `false`. `404 not_found` for a computer that is not yours.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H.../browser_sessions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
const { data } = await naive.browserSessions.list("cmp_01H...");
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "brw_3f9c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
      "object": "browser_session",
      "computer_id": "cmp_01H...",
      "session_id": "ses_01H...",
      "status": "active",
      "allowed_domains": ["docs.example.com"],
      "region": "us-west",
      "context_id": null,
      "context_backed": false,
      "timeout_at": "2026-09-08T10:15:00Z",
      "opened_at": "2026-09-08T10:00:00Z",
      "closed_at": null,
      "created_at": "2026-09-08T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Open a live view

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser_sessions/{bid}/live_view` — **dashboard session only**

Mints a short-lived URL that shows the remote browser as it runs. Takes no body. On an API key: `403 forbidden` — the same rule as [`GET /v1/computers/{id}/browser/live-view`](/docs/api/browser#live-view), which returns the same object for the one browser currently open.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The URL is a **bearer credential**: anyone holding it controls the browser until it expires, with no further authentication. It is minted on demand for the person looking at the dashboard, never stored, never written to the audit trail, never returned inside any other object, and withheld from the [MCP catalogue](/docs/api/mcp) — the agent that drives the browser never sees its own live view. Hold it in memory, render it, and let it expire.

`404 not_found` once the session has closed, or for a session that was not opened beside this computer. Audited as `browser.live_view_opened` — who, when, and for which session, never the URL.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "browser_live_view",
  "url": "https://...",
  "expires_at": "2026-09-08T10:15:00Z"
}
```


# Cards
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/cards

Prepaid virtual cards an identity buys with organization credits, with a single audited credential reveal.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Not available yet.** Card issuing is not configured on the hosted service yet, so quoting, issuing, retrying and revealing a card answer `501 feature_not_configured` ("card issuing is not configured") and no credit moves. The reference below describes the surface for when issuing is turned on; do not build on it yet.

Every route is nested under an identity. `{identity}` accepts an `idn_…` id or the identity's name.
An identity may hold any number of cards. A card is `prepaid`: bought once for `load_micro_usd`,
never reloaded. Amounts are integer micro-USD (`1 USD = 1000000`). An agent reaches a card through
the identity its session selected; there is no card-to-agent assignment to manage.

> [!NOTE]
>
> On a deployment with no card issuer bound, quoting, issuing, retrying and revealing answer `501 feature_not_configured` before any credit moves; reads return what the identity already holds.

## The card object

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "vcd_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "object": "card",
  "identity_id": "idn_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "kind": "prepaid",
  "status": "active",
  "label": "Ads",
  "brand": "Visa",
  "last4": "4242",
  "load_micro_usd": 50000000,
  "spent_micro_usd": 1299000,
  "currency": "usd",
  "expires_at": "2027-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  "failure_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-01T10:00:04Z"
}
```

`status` is one of `pending_payment`, `issuing`, `active`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `refunded`. This
object never carries a number, PIN, CVV or redemption link — those live only in the
[credential reveal](#reveal-credentials).

## List cards

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/cards` — scope `agents:read`

A [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of `card` objects. Filter with `?status=active`.

## Price a load

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/quote` — scope `agents:read`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "load_micro_usd": 50000000 }
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "card_quote",
  "load_micro_usd": 50000000,
  "price_micro_usd": 50500000,
  "brand": "Visa",
  "min_load_micro_usd": 1000000,
  "max_load_micro_usd": 150000000
}
```

`price_micro_usd` is what issuing will debit from credits — the load plus the issuer's fee. A load
outside the bounds answers `validation_failed`. Zero side effects.

## Issue a card

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "label": "Ads", "load_micro_usd": 50000000 }
```

The price is debited from the organization's credits **before** the issuer is asked; a short
balance answers `402 insufficient_credits` and nothing is ordered. Answers `201` with the card in
status `issuing` (the issuer is still fulfilling; read it again) or `active`. If the issuer refuses
the order the card is `failed` with a provider-neutral `failure_reason`, its debit is held, and
[retry](#lifecycle) or [refund](#lifecycle) settles it. Honours `Idempotency-Key`; the same key
replays the same card without a second debit.

## Read a card

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}` — scope `agents:read`

Reading an `issuing` card reconciles it with the issuer, so the status you see is current.

## Reveal credentials

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/credentials` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "card_credentials",
  "card_id": "vcd_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "number": "4242424242424242",
  "pin": "1234",
  "cvv": null,
  "expiry": "09/27",
  "url": "https://redeem.example/abc",
  "instructions": "Enter the number and PIN at checkout.",
  "revealed_at": "2026-09-01T10:05:00Z"
}
```

The only route that answers a `card_credentials` object. Every reveal writes an audit event
(`card.credentials_revealed` — the event names the card, never the credential) and the response is
`Cache-Control: no-store`. A card that is not `active`, or that the caller cannot see, answers
`404 not_found` — never a `403` that confirms it exists.

## Lifecycle

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/retry` — scope `billing:write` — re-runs issuance from `failed`, reusing the held debit.

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/cancel` — scope `billing:write` — marks an `active` card `cancelled`. The prepaid balance stays on the card.

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/refund` — scope `billing:write` — returns the credits of a `pending_payment` or `failed` card and marks it `refunded`.

A lifecycle action from any other status answers `409 state_conflict`. A prepaid card has no
top-up: buy another card.

## Transactions

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/transactions` — scope `agents:read`

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/cards/{card}/transactions` — scope `sessions:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "amount_micro_usd": 1299000, "merchant": "Example Ads", "description": "Campaign #4" }
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "vct_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w3",
  "object": "card_transaction",
  "card_id": "vcd_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "amount_micro_usd": 1299000,
  "merchant": "Example Ads",
  "description": "Campaign #4",
  "session_id": "ses_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w4",
  "metadata": {},
  "created_at": "2026-09-01T11:00:00Z"
}
```

Logging a spend increments `spent_micro_usd` and is refused (`validation_failed`) when it would
exceed the load. A prepaid card has no live authorization feed; this ledger is what the identity
and its agents record. The list is paginated (`limit` default 50, max 200).

## Errors

`insufficient_credits` before any issuer call; `validation_failed` for a load outside the quote's
bounds or an over-load spend; `state_conflict` for a lifecycle action from the wrong status;
`not_found` for the credentials of a card that is not active; `feature_not_configured`. See
[Errors](/docs/api/errors).


# Characters
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/characters

Train a reusable on-screen persona from reference photos, then render images as it — the same face, hair and build across a whole channel.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A character is the media sibling of an [identity](/docs/api/identities): an identity is *who an agent is being* to the world (an inbox, a number); a character is *who it renders as* on screen.

Two renders of "a young woman with freckles" are two different women, so a channel of shorts has no recurring host. A **character** fixes that: it is trained once from a handful of reference stills and then pinned into every later [image](/docs/api/images), so the same face carries across every render — the AI-influencer primitive. Training takes minutes, so `POST /v1/characters` does not wait: it answers `202` with the character in `training`, and you read it back until it is `ready`. An agent does the same with the [`create_character`](/docs/capabilities/tools#characters) family of tools; a character made here is one a session can render as, and the other way round.

## The character object

**id** `string`

`chr_…`.

**object** `string`

Always `character`.

**name** `string`

How a person and an agent address it, up to 100 characters. Unique among the organization's live characters, ignoring case.

**description** `string | null`

Who the character is — looks, age, vibe, wardrobe — up to 1,024 characters. Read by the model when it renders as them.

**status** `string`

`training` → `ready` | `failed`. `ready` is the only state a render can pin.

**source\_images** `string[]`

The reference stills it was trained from, **as you gave them**: a `fil_` id or a public URL. Never the short-lived signed link the trainer was handed.

**thumbnail\_url** `string | null`

Reserved for a trained preview. Always `null` today: render a still with the character to see it.

**reason** `string | null`

Why a `failed` training failed; `null` otherwise.

**scope** `string`

`organization` — your own, trained from your photos — or `platform`: a **prebuilt** character every organization can render as, ready with no training. A prebuilt character cannot be deleted.

**persona** `object | null`

Who the character is, as up to five lines (`niche`, `bio`, `voice`, `wardrobe`, `hooks`, each up to 500 characters), read by your agents when they write as them. `null` when none was given.

**style\_pack** `string[]`

The [looks](/docs/api/images#looks) the character is usually drawn in, by name. A trained character given none gets Phone snap, Realistic and Everyday.

**sheet** `string[]`

A prebuilt character's sample stills, as paths on the dashboard. Empty for your own.

**metadata** `object`

Arbitrary key/value pairs. A character you trained carries `consent` here: `attested`, `by` (the member or API key that confirmed it, or the session whose approved call trained it), `at` and the `statement` that was confirmed.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**updated\_at** `string`

When its status or fields last changed.

## Create a character

`POST /v1/characters` → `202 Accepted` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) **required**.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Train only your own face, or the face of someone who has agreed to an AI likeness of them. Every training records who confirmed that and when, and photos of a recognizable public figure are refused. Using someone's likeness without their permission breaks the [Terms](https://usenaive.ai/terms).

**name** `string` *required*

A short, unique name, such as `Ava`. 1–100 characters. A name a live character already holds is `validation_failed` before anything is trained or billed.

**description** `string`

Who the character is. Up to 1,024 characters. Left out, it is a one-line description of how the person in the photos looks (apparent gender, age, hair), read from the photos when they are checked: every render as the character uses it to keep the person the same.

**persona** `object`

Who they are: any of `niche`, `bio`, `voice`, `wardrobe`, `hooks`, each up to 500 characters.

**style\_pack** `string[]`

Up to 12 [look](/docs/api/images#looks) names they are usually drawn in. An unknown look is `validation_failed`. Omitted or empty, they are Phone snap, Realistic and Everyday.

**consent** `object` *required*

`{ "attested": true }` — you confirm: *"I confirm the person in these photos is me, or has given me permission to create an AI likeness of them, and is not a public figure."* Anything else is `validation_failed` before anything is checked, trained or billed. Kept on the character as `metadata.consent`, with who confirmed it and when. An agent's `create_character` always waits for a person to approve the call, whatever its tool policy says: approving it is that person's confirmation of this statement.

**image\_urls** `string[]` *required*

One to **sixteen** reference photos of the *same* person, each a stored file's `fil_` id (an upload, or an image a [render](/docs/api/images) filed) or a public `http(s)` URL. More, varied angles train a stronger likeness. A `fil_` this organization does not hold is `not_found`; one that is not an image, a private or loopback host, and a `data:` or `file:` URL are `validation_failed`. The first two photos are checked for a recognizable public figure before anything is billed; if they show one, the request is `validation_failed` on `image_urls` with the reason.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/characters \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Ava",
    "description": "Late twenties, freckles, copper bob, oversized denim jacket",
    "image_urls": ["fil_01J9A...", "fil_01J9B...", "https://example.com/ava-profile.jpg"],
    "persona": { "niche": "Fashion · fit checks", "voice": "Dry, quick, never salesy" },
    "style_pack": ["Phone snap", "Quiet luxury"],
    "consent": { "attested": true }
  }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const ava = await client.characters.create({
  name: "Ava",
  description: "Late twenties, freckles, copper bob, oversized denim jacket",
  image_urls: ["fil_01J9A...", "fil_01J9B...", "https://example.com/ava-profile.jpg"],
  persona: { niche: "Fashion · fit checks", voice: "Dry, quick, never salesy" },
  style_pack: ["Phone snap", "Quiet luxury"],
  consent: { attested: true },
});
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive character create --name Ava --consent --image fil_01J9A... --image fil_01J9B... --image https://example.com/ava-profile.jpg \
  --persona '{"niche":"Fashion · fit checks","voice":"Dry, quick, never salesy"}' --style-pack "Phone snap" --style-pack "Quiet luxury"
```

```json 202 Accepted theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "chr_01J9CD...",
  "object": "character",
  "name": "Ava",
  "description": "Late twenties, freckles, copper bob, oversized denim jacket",
  "status": "training",
  "source_images": ["fil_01J9A...", "fil_01J9B...", "https://example.com/ava-profile.jpg"],
  "thumbnail_url": null,
  "reason": null,
  "scope": "organization",
  "persona": { "niche": "Fashion · fit checks", "voice": "Dry, quick, never salesy" },
  "style_pack": ["Phone snap", "Quiet luxury"],
  "sheet": [],
  "metadata": {
    "consent": {
      "attested": true,
      "by": "usr_01J8ZX...",
      "at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "statement": "I confirm the person in these photos is me, or has given me permission to create an AI likeness of them, and is not a public figure."
    }
  },
  "created_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

A replay under the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the character the first request made — it is not trained or billed twice. Once that character is deleted, a replay of its key is `409 idempotency_conflict`; send a new key to train another.

## Retrieve a character

`GET /v1/characters/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. `{id}` is the `chr_` id **or** the name; an exact id wins over a name. Poll it after a create: each read advances the status from the trainer, so `training` turns into `ready` or `failed` on the read that sees it. A training takes a few minutes.

## List characters

`GET /v1/characters` → `200 OK`, [cursor-paginated](/docs/api/pagination), newest first — scope `agents:read`. `{ data: Character[], has_more, next_cursor }`.

Your own characters come first, then the prebuilt ones.

**status** `string`

`training`, `ready` or `failed`.

**scope** `string`

`organization` for your own only, `platform` for the prebuilt ones only.

**limit** `number`

Page size, 1–100.

**after** `string`

The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

## Update a character

`PATCH /v1/characters/{id}` changes who a character is, by `chr_` id or name: `name`, `description`, `persona` and `style_pack`. A `persona` is merged line by line, so lines you leave out stay. The face can't change: that's a new training. A prebuilt character is `409 state_conflict`, and a name another character holds is `validation_failed`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/characters/Ava \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "persona": { "wardrobe": "Linen shirts and old denim" } }'
```

## Delete a character

`DELETE /v1/characters/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:write`. `{id}` is the `chr_` id or the name. A soft delete: the character can no longer be rendered as and its name is free for a new one, while every file it rendered keeps its `source.character_id`. A prebuilt character (`scope: "platform"`) cannot be deleted: `409 state_conflict`.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "chr_01J9CD...", "object": "character", "deleted": true }
```

## Rendering as a character

Pass `character` — the `chr_` id or name of a `ready` character — to [`POST /v1/media/images`](/docs/api/images#generate-images). The render is routed to a model that pins one, and the same face carries across every image. Add `style` to draw it in a [look](/docs/api/images#looks).

To keep a scene's room, props and outfit across shots, pass `character` together with `image_urls` naming a still of that character: the render is an edit of that still in a new pose or framing, and it is a still of the character too, so it can be the first frame of the next video.

A character carries into video through the **still** it renders: generate an image as the character, then pass `character` and the still's `fil_` id as the `image_urls` first frame of [`POST /v1/media/videos`](/docs/api/video#generate-a-video). The first frame must be a still rendered as that character, or the request is `validation_failed`, and only a model that animates a still is used.

```ts theme={"system"}
const still = await client.media.images.generate({ prompt: "Ava waves at the camera on a rooftop at golden hour", character: "Ava", style: "Phone snap" });
const job = await client.media.videos.generate({ prompt: "she waves, the camera pushes in slowly", character: "Ava", image_urls: [still.files[0].id] });
```

A post that attaches a file rendered as a character is not labelled AI-generated on its own: the label is opt-in, so set `ai_generated: true` on the post to add it. See [AI-generated posts](/docs/api/social#ai-generated-posts).

## Billing

A training costs dollars, not cents, so unlike a render it is **admitted first**: the organization's prepaid balance must cover one training, else `402 insufficient_credits` before anything is bought. It is then billed once, on the media tier, when the trainer accepts the photos — under the character the request's idempotency key names, so a replay charges nothing. A request refused before training (a taken name, no consent, a public figure, an unreadable photo) is not billed. A training that later ends `failed` is refunded — credited back to the organization on the read that sees it fail. Reads, lists and deletes are free. See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#media-generation--per-finished-job-media-component).

**Price.** There is no fixed list price: a training is billed at what the trainer charges for it when it accepts the photos. That has been about \*\*$2.50** (`2500000` micro-USD) per training; when the trainer's live figure cannot be read, $2.50 is what is billed, and it is also the balance a create needs to start.
