There is no quote call for a training; the charge shows as one `media` line item in the [ledger](/docs/api/credits), and on the session's cost when an agent trained it.

## Errors

| Code | When |
| - | - |
| `validation_failed` | Missing `Idempotency-Key`; no `consent` or `consent.attested` not `true`; photos that show a recognizable public figure (`image_urls`, with the reason); `name` empty, over 100 characters or already held by a live character; zero or more than sixteen `image_urls`; a stored file that is not an image; a private-host, `data:` or `file:` URL. On a render: a `character` still `training` or `failed`, or with `image_urls` that are not all stills of it. |
| `insufficient_credits` | `402`: the prepaid balance cannot cover a training. Nothing is trained or billed. |
| `not_found` | No such `chr_` id or name in this organization, or it was deleted; an `image_urls` `fil_` this organization does not hold. |
| `provider_error` | The trainer refused the photos, or could not be reached. On a create nothing is created or billed; on a read the character is answered as it stood once the trainer answers again. |
| `idempotency_conflict` | `409`: the `Idempotency-Key` already created a character that has since been deleted. |
| `feature_not_configured` | This deploy has no media backend that trains characters. |

> [card] [In a session](/docs/capabilities/tools#characters)
>
> `create_character`, `get_character`, `list_characters` and `delete_character` — the same lifecycle as agent tools.


# Clips
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/clips

Cut a long video into short, captioned, vertical clips — as a job you submit, poll and collect.

Clipping is asynchronous: a submit is answered `202` with a `media_job` you poll (or receive by [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks)). When it completes, every clip is a published [file](/docs/api/files) in your library, scored for virality by the same pipeline the [`clip_video`](/docs/capabilities/tools) tool uses in a session.

## The media job object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `med_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `media_job`.

**kind** `string`

Always `clip` here.

**status** `string`

`queued` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`.

**model** `string | null`

Always `null` for clipping; the pipeline is not model-selectable.

**input** `object`

The request as accepted, defaults filled in. Fields you did not send are `null`.

**result** `object | null`

`{ clips: [...] }` once `completed`, otherwise `null`. Each clip: `file_id`, `title`, `start_seconds`, `end_seconds`, `duration_seconds`, and `virality` — `total`, `shareability`, `hook_strength`, `story_quality`, `emotional_impact`, each an integer 0–100.

**error** `object | null`

`{ code, message }` once `failed`, otherwise `null`.

**cost\_micro\_usd** `integer | null`

What the job actually cost, settled on completion. `null` until then and for a failed job — a failure is not billed.

**session\_id** `string | null`

Always `null` for a job submitted here; set when the `clip_video` tool queued it.

**created\_at** `string`

Submission timestamp.

**completed\_at** `string | null`

When the job reached a terminal status.

## Submit a clipping job

`POST /v1/media/clips` — scope `agents:write`. An [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) header is **required** — a submit without one is refused with `validation_failed` — so a retried submit replays the job instead of queueing (and billing) a second one; the same key with a different body is `idempotency_conflict`.

**video\_url** `string` *required*

A public `http(s)` URL of the source video. Private, loopback and link-local hosts are refused with `validation_failed`.

**aspect\_ratio** `string` (default: 9:16)

`9:16` (reframed to the speaker) or `16:9` (kept as shot).

**remove\_silence** `boolean` (default: false)

Tighten pauses inside each clip.

**caption\_preset** `string` (default: none)

`none`, `clean`, `bold` or `karaoke`. `none` burns no captions.

**language** `string`

BCP-47 hint for transcription (e.g. `de`, `pt-BR`). Omit to detect.

**min\_seconds** `integer` (default: 15)

Shortest clip to keep, 5–180.

**max\_seconds** `integer` (default: 60)

Longest clip to keep, 5–180; must not be below `min_seconds`.

**title** `string`

A title for clips the scorer does not name itself.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/clips \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: 6f1c...ab" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "video_url": "https://cdn.example.com/keynote.mp4", "caption_preset": "bold", "language": "en", "max_seconds": 45 }'
```

```json 202 Accepted theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01H9HH...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "clip",
  "status": "queued",
  "model": null,
  "input": {
    "video_url": "https://cdn.example.com/keynote.mp4",
    "aspect_ratio": "9:16",
    "remove_silence": false,
    "caption_preset": "bold",
    "language": "en",
    "min_seconds": 15,
    "max_seconds": 45,
    "title": null
  },
  "result": null,
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": null,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-06T18:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": null
}
```

A submit is refused with `402 insufficient_credits` when the organization's prepaid balance is empty. There is no per-tenant concurrency cap on this route — your balance bounds you, not a turn — unlike the `clip_video` tool, which keeps one active job per session.

## Retrieve a job

`GET /v1/media/clips/{id}` — scope `agents:read`

```json 200 OK theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01H9HH...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "clip",
  "status": "completed",
  "model": null,
  "input": { "video_url": "https://cdn.example.com/keynote.mp4", "aspect_ratio": "9:16", "remove_silence": false, "caption_preset": "bold", "language": "en", "min_seconds": 15, "max_seconds": 45, "title": null },
  "result": {
    "clips": [
      {
        "file_id": "fil_01H9HJ...",
        "title": "The one metric that changed our roadmap",
        "start_seconds": 812.4,
        "end_seconds": 851.0,
        "duration_seconds": 38.6,
        "virality": { "total": 87, "shareability": 82, "hook_strength": 91, "story_quality": 85, "emotional_impact": 90 }
      }
    ]
  },
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": 412000,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-06T18:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-09-06T18:06:31.000Z"
}
```

A failed job reads back with `status: "failed"`, `result: null`, `cost_micro_usd: null` and `error: { "code": "provider_error", "message": "..." }`.

## List jobs

`GET /v1/media/clips` — scope `agents:read`

**status** `string`

`queued`, `processing`, `completed` or `failed`.

**limit** `number`

Page size, 1–100.

**after** `string`

The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

Newest first, in the standard [list envelope](/docs/api/pagination). Only jobs submitted through this API are listed; the clips an agent's `clip_video` tool cuts inside a session reach that session as [files](/docs/api/files), not as jobs here.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an [endpoint](/docs/api/webhooks) to `media.job.queued`, `media.job.completed` (`data.file_ids` names the clips) or `media.job.failed` (`data.code`) to be told rather than poll. Every envelope carries `data.job_id` and `data.kind: "clip"`.

## Pricing

A job is billed what it actually cost — input minutes, transcript words, scoring tokens, cut clips — once it finishes, and `cost_micro_usd` is that figure. See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#media-generation--per-finished-job-media-component).


# Computers
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/computers

Sandboxed compute environments with a browser and filesystem.

A **computer** is a durable, sandboxed environment an [agent](/docs/api/agents) can use: a shell, a filesystem, and an optional browser constrained to an allowlist of domains. Computers can be paused to stop compute charges and snapshotted for fast restore.

A [session](/docs/api/sessions) whose toolset needs a filesystem works on its agent's computer, started the first time one is needed, and reports it as `computer_id`. An agent's computer appears in this list named `agent {id}`, with `agent_id` set, so you can tell it from the ones you created; it belongs to the agent, not to any one session (see [An agent's computer](#an-agents-computer)). A session started before agents had their own computer may still hold one it provisioned for itself, named `session {id}`, until it ends.

## The computer object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `cmp_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `computer`.

**name** `string`

Human-readable name.

**vcpu** `integer`

Provisioned vCPU for a micro-VM (1–16).

**memory\_mb** `integer`

Provisioned memory in MiB (128–65536).

**disk\_gb** `integer`

Root disk size in GiB.

**status** `string`

Lifecycle state — see [below](#lifecycle).

**browser** `object`

Browser configuration, or `null` if disabled. Every field has a default, so `{}` alone is a complete option and the browser reaches the open web. Drive it through the [Browser](/docs/api/browser) routes.

**browser**

**allowed\_domains** `string[]`

Domain allowlist (supports wildcards, e.g. `*.example.com`). Defaults to `["*"]`; an explicit `[]` is refused.

**timeout\_minutes** `integer`

Session lifetime, 1–360. Default `15`.

**region** `string`

`us-west` (default), `us-east`, `eu-central` or `ap-southeast`.

**keep\_alive** `boolean`

Keep the session open across idle periods. Default `false`.

**viewport** `object`

`{ width, height }` in pixels.

**os** `string`

`windows`, `mac`, `linux`, `mobile` or `tablet` — the device the browser presents as.

**block\_ads** `boolean`

Default `false`.

**solve\_captchas** `boolean`

Default `true`.

**stealth** `boolean`

Default `false`.

**allow\_writes** `boolean`

Permit actions that change a page (submit, buy, delete, …). Default `false`.

**allow\_extract** `boolean`

Permit reads from a browser that holds a saved login. Default `false`.

**context\_name** `string`

Open on a saved login of that name (see [Browser](/docs/api/browser#save-a-login)).

**persist\_context** `boolean`

Write the login state back to that context at close. Default `false`.

**human\_login** `boolean`

Hold the context for a person to sign in through the live view; locks it for 15 minutes. Default `false`.

**proxy** `boolean`

Route through a residential proxy. Needs a bounded allow-list, not `*`. Default `false`.

**volume** `object | null`

Attached persistent volume. Always `null` — a volume separate from the boot disk is not provisioned today; size the root disk with `disk_gb`.

**snapshot\_id** `string | null`

Snapshot this computer was restored from, if any.

**agent\_id** `string | null`

The [agent](/docs/api/agents) this computer belongs to (see [An agent's computer](#an-agents-computer)), or `null` for one you created.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Lifecycle

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `creating` | Provisioning; not yet usable. |
| `running` | Ready and billable for compute: a computer you create is billed in 10-minute blocks at its size, in advance, and paused when your balance cannot cover the next block. |
| `paused` | Stopped; bills nothing, and the disk is kept. Resume to use again. Pausing a computer you created does not refund the rest of its 10-minute block already paid, and any exec, fs, snapshot or execStream call on a paused computer resumes it, so billing restarts. |
| `failed` | Provisioning failed; the computer never became usable. Terminal. |
| `destroyed` | Permanently deleted. Terminal. |

## Create a computer

`POST /v1/computers` → `202 Accepted`. Provisioning is asynchronous: the response returns immediately with `status: "creating"`. **Wait for readiness before using the computer**: poll `GET /v1/computers/{id}` until `status` is `running`. There is no computer lifecycle [event](/docs/api/events) to subscribe to — the event stream is session-scoped. If provisioning fails the computer moves to `failed`, and calls that need a live machine return `409` with code `computer_unavailable`.

Creating (or resuming) a computer needs a balance of at least 10 minutes of it; otherwise the call is `402` with code `insufficient_credits`. The 10-minute block a new computer starts in is charged when it is created.

**name** `string`

Human-readable name. Defaults to `computer`.

**vcpu** `integer`

Provisioned vCPU. Defaults to `2`.

**memory\_mb** `integer`

Provisioned memory in MiB. Defaults to `4096`.

**disk\_gb** `integer`

Root disk size in GiB. Defaults to `5`.

**browser** `object | null`

Browser config — `{}` enables one on the open web, `{ "allowed_domains": ["*.example.com"] }` scopes it; the full option object is [above](#the-computer-object). Defaults to `null`, which disables the browser.

**snapshot\_id** `string`

Snapshot (`snp_…`) to restore this computer from. The field is `snapshot_id`, not `snapshot`; an id that is not your organization's is `404`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{ "name": "box", "vcpu": 4, "memory_mb": 8192, "disk_gb": 40, "browser": { "allowed_domains": ["*.example.com"] } }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "cmp_01H8YZ...",
  "object": "computer",
  "name": "box",
  "vcpu": 4,
  "memory_mb": 8192,
  "disk_gb": 40,
  "status": "creating",
  "browser": {
    "allowed_domains": ["*.example.com"],
    "timeout_minutes": 15,
    "region": "us-west",
    "keep_alive": false,
    "block_ads": false,
    "solve_captchas": true,
    "stealth": false,
    "allow_writes": false,
    "allow_extract": false,
    "persist_context": false,
    "human_login": false,
    "proxy": false
  },
  "volume": null,
  "snapshot_id": null,
  "agent_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

## Retrieve & list

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/computers/{id}     # retrieve one -> 200 (poll status here)
GET /v1/computers          # list (cursor-paginated) -> 200
```

See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination) for list parameters.

## An agent's computer

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/agents/{id}/computer   # the agent's computer, or null -> 200
```

Each agent has one computer, and every session of the agent works on it and sees the same files. The answer is the agent's `computer`, or `null` before any session has needed one. The machine under it can change: the files are kept, and after a change this route names the new `cmp_` id. Another organization's agent is `404` `not_found`. It takes the same scope as `GET /v1/computers/{id}`.

The agent looks after its computer: it starts it when a session needs it, pauses it after a few idle minutes, and removes it when the agent is deleted. Your files are kept across all of that. So some calls on an agent's computer work differently:

| Call | On an agent's computer |
| - | - |
| `POST …/pause` | `409` `computer_unavailable` while a session or a person is using it. |
| `POST …/resume` | Wakes it. Nobody using it, it pauses again after 3 idle minutes. |
| `exec`, `fs/*`, `snapshot` | Wakes it if paused, and keeps it running until the call ends. |
| `POST …/takeover` | You hold it. The agent's sessions wait until you hand it back. Your time on it is not billed. `409` while a session is using it. |
| `DELETE …/takeover` | Hands it back. A takeover you do not hand back ends after an hour. |
| `DELETE /v1/computers/{id}` | `409` `computer_unavailable`: it goes when the agent goes. |

A call that names an older machine of the agent is `409` `computer_unavailable`; read the agent's computer for its current one. `takeover` on a computer you created is `409` too: nothing else uses it, so pause it instead.

## Rename

`PATCH /v1/computers/{id}` → `200 OK`. The name is the one field a computer has that you can change after creation; the body is strict, so any other field is `400` `validation_failed`. Returns the computer, and is recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `computer.updated`.

**name** `string` *required*

1–200 characters.

## Inspect

`GET /v1/computers/{id}/inspect` → `200 OK`. What the computer is doing right now, from two sources: the provider's own record of it (`status`, `last_active_at`, and `home` — the directory the `fs/*` calls are rooted in, or `null` when the provider does not confine them), and — only when that record says `running` — a single probe command run inside the machine. Inspecting never wakes a paused computer, so a paused or stopped one always answers with `probe: null`. A probe that cannot run or cannot be parsed is also `probe: null`, never an error; the numbers are a sample taken at `sampled_at`, not a metrics feed.

This call requires the **`computers:write`** scope. Despite the verb, it is not a plain read: the probe runs a command inside your machine, on compute you are billed for. Use `GET /v1/computers/{id}` for a read that does not touch the machine.

The `home` in the example below is illustrative. **Read it from this call rather than hardcoding a path** — it is what the machine's image reports, and it can differ between computers.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "computer_inspect",
  "id": "cmp_01H8YZ...",
  "status": "running",
  "last_active_at": "2026-09-08T03:19:11Z",
  "home": "/home/naive",
  "probe": {
    "sampled_at": "2026-09-08T03:19:12Z",
    "uptime_seconds": 12345,
    "processes": 87,
    "load_1m": 0.42,
    "memory_used_mb": 1000,
    "memory_total_mb": 3952,
    "disk_used_gb": 1.0,
    "disk_total_gb": 5.0
  }
}
```

## Execute a command

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/exec` → `200 OK`. Runs a shell command and returns its output once it has finished. A `paused` computer is resumed first and stays `running` afterwards — pausing does not lock a computer; a `creating`, `failed`, or destroyed one returns `409` with code `computer_unavailable`. Every run — by this route or the streamed one below — is recorded in the computer's [command history](#command-history).

**command** `string` *required*

The command to run.

**timeout\_ms** `integer`

Max runtime, up to `600000`. Defaults to `30000`. When it elapses the command and every process it started (other than one detached with `setsid`) is killed, `exit_code` is `124` and `timed_out` is `true`.

`stdout` and `stderr` are each returned up to 262 144 characters; `truncated` is `true` when either was cut.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H8YZ.../exec \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "command": "ls -a ~" }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "exit_code": 0, "stdout": ".\n..\n.bashrc\n...", "stderr": "", "duration_ms": 42, "timed_out": false, "truncated": false }
```

### Stream a command

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/exec/stream` → `200 OK`, `text/event-stream`. The same run as `exec`, delivered as it happens: the body is a stream of Server-Sent Events whose `data:` lines are JSON frames — zero or more `{"stdout": "…"}` / `{"stderr": "…"}` chunks in the order the process produced them, then exactly one `exit` frame and the stream closes. `command_id` names the row the run was recorded as. Same body as `exec`; the same `404`/`409`/`400` refusals are returned as ordinary JSON errors before the stream opens. The SDK reads this as `computers.execStream(id, command, { timeoutMs })`, an async iterable of frames.

```text Response theme={"system"}
data: {"stdout":"compiling\n"}

data: {"stderr":"warning: unused\n"}

data: {"exit":{"exit_code":0,"timed_out":false,"truncated":false,"duration_ms":412,"command_id":"cmd_01J..."}}
```

## Build a 3D model

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/build-3d` → `200 OK` — scope `computers:write`. Runs a Python script that builds a model with [build123d](https://github.com/gumyr/build123d) (`cad`, millimetres) or Blender (`blender`, metres) in this computer, checks it, renders previews and publishes the exports as [files](/docs/api/files). The same program an agent's `build_3d` tool runs ([3D assets](/docs/capabilities/3d)). The toolchain (about 1.9 GB) installs into the computer on first use, so the first call needs 3 GB free disk: create the computer with `disk_gb` of 10 or more. A 5 GB computer has about 2.1 GB free and is refused with `409 computer_unavailable`. A paused computer is resumed first, as for `exec`.

**engine** `string` *required*

`cad`: the script assigns `result`, a build123d shape. `blender`: the script builds the scene with `bpy`.

**script** `string` *required*

The Python source, up to 200 KB.

**name** `string` *required*

Base name of the outputs, `[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}`.

**export** `string[]`

Any of `step`, `stl`, `3mf`, `glb`, `obj`, `blend`. Default `["step", "stl"]` for `cad`, `["glb"]` for `blender`.

**render** `object | false`

`{ views?: ("iso"|"front"|"top"|"side")[], size?: number }` — up to 4 views (default `["iso"]`), 256–1024 px (default 768). `false` renders nothing.

**publish** `boolean`

Default `true`. `false` runs the checks without publishing anything; the outputs are deleted from the computer when the call ends either way.

**timeout\_s** `integer`

Seconds the script and its exports may run, 10–300. Default 120. Rendering the previews has its own allowance on top (about 40–60 s per view, more for larger sizes), so previews never eat into the script's time.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H8YZ.../build-3d \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "engine": "cad", "name": "plate", "script": "from build123d import *\nresult = Box(60, 40, 4) - Cylinder(3, 4)", "render": { "views": ["iso", "top"] } }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "ok": true,
  "files": [
    { "file_id": "fil_01J...", "name": "plate.step", "content_type": "model/step", "bytes": 21877 },
    { "file_id": "fil_01K...", "name": "plate.stl", "content_type": "model/stl", "bytes": 6884 }
  ],
  "previews": ["fil_01L...", "fil_01M..."],
  "checks": { "valid_solid": true, "watertight": true, "bbox_mm": [60, 40, 4], "volume_cm3": 9.49, "triangles": 136 },
  "error": null,
  "log_tail": "",
  "compute_seconds": 3.1
}
```

**ok** `boolean`

`false` when the script raised, a `cad` solid failed its checks, an STL or 3MF was withheld because the mesh is not watertight, or an output was over the file size limit (then nothing is published).

**files** `object[]`

The published exports. For `cad`, STEP, STL and 3MF are published only when `valid_solid` and `watertight` are both true. For either engine, STL and 3MF are never published from a mesh that is not watertight.

**previews** `string[]`

The rendered PNGs, as `fil_` ids.

**checks** `object | null`

`valid_solid` (`null` for `blender`), `watertight`, `bbox_mm``[x, y, z]`, `volume_cm3` (`null` when not closed), `triangles`. `null` when the script failed before producing a shape.

**error** `object | null`

`{ message, line }` — the script's own failure, with its line number when known. A failing script is a `200` with `ok: false`, not an error response.

**log\_tail** `string`

The last 4 KB of the build's log: everything the script and the toolchain printed.

**compute\_seconds** `number`

The computer time the build used.

There is no fee of its own: a build is billed as the computer's running seconds, like any other command. A `creating`, `failed`, or destroyed computer is `409` `computer_unavailable`; a body outside the limits above is `validation_failed`.

## Command history

`GET /v1/computers/{id}/commands` → `200 OK`. Every command run on the computer through `exec` or `exec/stream`, newest first, cursor-paginated ([Pagination](/docs/api/pagination)). Each row keeps the first 65 536 characters of `stdout` and of `stderr`; `truncated` is `true` when either was cut. `actor` is the principal that ran it — an API key, a user, or the platform acting for a session. Commands the agent runs *inside* a session through its own tools are not listed here; they are in the session's [event stream](/docs/api/events).

This read requires the **`computers:write`** scope — the same scope that runs a command. It hands back what those commands printed, so it is not readable by a credential that could not have produced it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Retention.** Command output is stored for **30 days** and then deleted; the rest of a computer's history is deleted with the computer. It is stored exactly as the command produced it — nothing scans or redacts it — so a command that prints a credential stores that credential for the window. Print secrets to a file, or read them from the [vault](/docs/identity/vault), rather than to stdout.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "cmd_01J...",
      "object": "computer_command",
      "computer_id": "cmp_01H8YZ...",
      "command": "make",
      "exit_code": 0,
      "timed_out": false,
      "duration_ms": 412,
      "stdout": "compiling\n",
      "stderr": "",
      "truncated": false,
      "actor": { "type": "key", "id": "key_01J..." },
      "created_at": "2026-09-08T03:19:11Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Pause & resume

Pausing stops compute charges while retaining state. Resuming makes it usable again. On an agent's computer both go through the agent; see [An agent's computer](#an-agents-computer).

```bash theme={"system"}
POST /v1/computers/{id}/pause    # -> 200, status: paused
POST /v1/computers/{id}/resume   # -> 200, status: running
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "cmp_01H8YZ...", "status": "paused" }
```

## Snapshot

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/snapshot` → `201 Created`. Captures the current filesystem state for fast restore. The body is empty — a snapshot has no name; its handle is the returned `snapshot_id`, which you pass as `snapshot_id` when creating a new computer. A snapshot outlives the computer it was taken from.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H8YZ.../snapshot \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "snapshot_id": "snp_0368aa449de84e308959ca72744a3bd5", "computer_id": "cmp_01H8YZ...", "created_at": "2026-08-20T18:00:00Z" }
```

### List snapshots

`GET /v1/snapshots` → `200 OK`. The organization's snapshots, newest first, [cursor-paginated](/docs/api/pagination) (`limit`, `after`); each item has the shape above.

### Delete a snapshot

`DELETE /v1/snapshots/{id}` → `200 OK` with `{ "id": "snp_…", "object": "snapshot", "deleted": true }`. Requires `computers:write`. Returns `409` with code `state_conflict` while a live computer was restored from it — destroy that computer first. A destroyed computer restored from it reads `snapshot_id: null` afterwards. An id that is not your organization's, or was already deleted, is `404`.

## Filesystem

The disk is reached through the governed `fs/*` operations — there is no separate upload/download channel. Each takes an absolute path. See [Filesystem](/docs/computer/filesystem) for limits and encoding details.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The `fs/*` operations are confined to the computer's home directory** — the `home` that [inspect](#inspect) reports. A path outside it (`/`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/tmp`) is refused with `403 forbidden` by every `fs/*` call, `read`, `mkdir` and `remove` included. Use [exec](#execute-a-command) to look at the rest of the disk.

### Read a file

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/fs/read` → `200`

**path** `string` *required*

Absolute path of the file to read.

**encoding** `string`

`text` (default) or `base64`. Ask for `base64` when the file is not valid UTF-8 — decoding binary as text substitutes U+FFFD and loses bytes silently.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "path": "/home/naive/notes.txt", "encoding": "text", "content": "hello\n" }
```

### Write a file

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/fs/write` → `200`

**path** `string` *required*

Absolute path to write or overwrite.

**content** `string` *required*

The file contents, in the named encoding.

**encoding** `string`

`text` (default) or `base64` for binary payloads.

### List a directory

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/fs/list` → `200`

**path** `string` *required*

Absolute path of the directory; lists its immediate children.

Each entry carries the file's own metadata: `type` is `file`, `directory`, `symlink` or `other`; `mode` is the POSIX mode bits as an integer; `modified_at` is `null` when the filesystem does not report a time. The SDK returns the typed list as `computers.listDir(id, path)`.

### Create a directory

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/fs/mkdir` → `200`

**path** `string` *required*

Absolute path to create; parents are created too (`mkdir -p`).

### Remove a path

`POST /v1/computers/{id}/fs/remove` → `200`

**path** `string` *required*

Absolute path to remove; directories are removed recursively (`rm -rf`). `/`, the home directory and any folder that holds it are refused with `400 validation_failed` before anything runs.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/computers/cmp_01H8YZ.../fs/list \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "path": "/home/naive" }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "entries": [
    { "name": "report.md", "path": "/home/naive/report.md", "type": "file", "size_bytes": 9, "mode": 33188, "modified_at": "2026-09-08T03:19:11Z" },
    { "name": "src", "path": "/home/naive/src", "type": "directory", "size_bytes": 4096, "mode": 16877, "modified_at": "2026-09-08T03:18:40Z" }
  ]
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> To persist an artifact beyond the computer's lifetime, publish it to [Files](/docs/api/files) (Naive Managed Agents object storage) rather than leaving it on the computer's disk.

## Destroy

`DELETE /v1/computers/{id}` → `200 OK`. Permanently destroys the computer and its non-snapshotted disk.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "cmp_01H8YZ...", "object": "computer", "deleted": true }
```

An agent's computer cannot be destroyed: the call is `computer_unavailable` (409). It is removed when the agent is deleted.

Ending or cancelling a session destroys nothing: its agent's computer, and the files on it, stay for
the agent's next session. Only a computer an older [session](/docs/api/sessions) provisioned for itself —
listed as `session {id}` — is tied to that session. It cannot be destroyed while the session can
still run a turn (the call is `computer_unavailable` (409) naming the session); it is destroyed with
the session, and one left resting at `idle` is reclaimed after an hour of silence.


# Connections
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/connections

Connected third-party accounts for a persona — auth configs, the Connect Link, and revocation.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A connection lets an [identity](/docs/api/identities) act in a third-party account the organization has authorized. There is **no fixed list of supported apps** — search the catalogue.

Three calls, in this order:

1. **Find the app.** `GET /v1/connections/apps?search=…` searches the catalogue — over a thousand apps — and answers with the `slug` every later call takes as `connector`.
2. An **auth config** is org-level and says *how* that app authenticates. Created once, shared by every identity that connects it.
3. A **connection** is identity-level: the connected account itself, minted against an auth config.

A connected account is the **provider's** object, not a row held here — a read reconciles state against the provider before answering.

## Apps

### The app object

**object** `string`

Always `connection_app`.

**slug** `string`

The app's id. This is what `connector` takes.

**name** `string`

The app's display name.

**description** `string`

One line about what the app is.

**categories** `string[]`

What the app is used for — e.g. `customer-support`, `crm`.

**auth** `string[]`

Which setup paths work for this app. `managed_oauth` means one call and no credentials of your own; `oauth` means registering an app with the vendor first; `api_key` means the person authorizing types a key on the hosted page.

**tool\_count** `number`

How many operations the app publishes in total.

### Search apps

`GET /v1/connections/apps` — scope `agents:read`

**search** `string`

Matches an app's name, id or description. Omit it to list the most-used apps.

**limit** `number`

Page size, 1–100.

**after** `string`

The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Opaque — it is not a row id.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/connections/apps?search=helpdesk" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "connection_app",
      "slug": "zendesk",
      "name": "Zendesk",
      "description": "Customer support software with ticketing, live chat and a knowledge base.",
      "categories": ["crm", "customer-support"],
      "auth": ["managed_oauth", "oauth"],
      "tool_count": 12
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "Mi0z"
}
```

### Retrieve an app

`GET /v1/connections/apps/{slug}` — scope `agents:read`

Everything the two setup calls need before either is made. `not_found` (404) for an id the catalogue does not know — this is what replaced the old connector enum.

**default\_tools** `string[]`

The operations an auth config pins when `tools` is not given.

**connect\_fields** `object[]`

What the person authorizing must still supply — an account subdomain, a region, a workspace. Each has `name`, `label`, `description` and `required`. Pass them to `POST /v1/connections` as `fields`, or leave them and the hosted page asks.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "connection_app",
  "slug": "zendesk",
  "name": "Zendesk",
  "auth": ["managed_oauth", "oauth"],
  "tool_count": 12,
  "default_tools": ["ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_TICKETS", "ZENDESK_REPLY_ZENDESK_TICKET"],
  "connect_fields": [
    { "name": "subdomain", "label": "Subdomain", "description": "the part before .zendesk.com", "required": true }
  ]
}
```

### Retrieve an app's logo

`GET /v1/connections/apps/{slug}/logo` — scope `agents:read`

The app's logo as image bytes, not JSON: the response carries the image's own `content-type` and `cache-control: public, max-age=86400`, so it can sit directly in an `<img>` tag. The app object itself carries no logo URL. `not_found` (404) when the catalogue has no image for the app.

## Auth configs

### The auth config object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `ac_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `auth_config`.

**connector** `string`

The app this config authenticates — an app `slug`.

**auth** `string`

`managed_oauth`, `oauth`, or `api_key`.

**scopes** `string[]`

The scopes the config actually carries, read back after creation — not the ones requested.

**tools** `string[]`

The operations a connection made from this config may call. Everything else is refused.

**connect\_fields** `object[]`

What `POST /v1/connections` will still be asked for. Same shape as on the app.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

### Create an auth config

`POST /v1/connections/auth_configs` — scope `agents:write`

**connector** `string` *required*

An app `slug` from the catalogue.

**auth** `string`

`managed_oauth` (default), `oauth`, or `api_key`. Check the app's `auth` first — not every app offers every path.

**scopes** `string[]`

Scopes to request. Ignored where the app's managed OAuth app is registered with a fixed set.

**tools** `string[]`

Pin the callable operations. Omitted, the app's `default_tools` are pinned. This is a hard boundary — anything not pinned does not exist to the agent.

**client\_id** `string`

Your own OAuth client id. Required when `auth` is `oauth`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/connections/auth_configs \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "connector": "zendesk", "auth": "managed_oauth" }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "ac_01H9CN...",
  "object": "auth_config",
  "connector": "zendesk",
  "auth": "managed_oauth",
  "scopes": ["tickets:read", "tickets:write"],
  "tools": ["ZENDESK_LIST_ZENDESK_TICKETS", "ZENDESK_REPLY_ZENDESK_TICKET"],
  "connect_fields": [
    { "name": "subdomain", "label": "Subdomain", "description": "the part before .zendesk.com", "required": true }
  ],
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:10:00Z"
}
```

### List auth configs

`GET /v1/connections/auth_configs` — scope `agents:read`. Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination).

### Delete an auth config

`DELETE /v1/connections/auth_configs/{id}` — scope `agents:write`. Connections already minted against it stop refreshing.

## Connections

### The connection object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `ca_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `connection`.

**auth\_config\_id** `string`

The auth config it was minted against.

**identity\_id** `string`

The persona that acts in the account.

**connector** `string`

The app the account is in — an app `slug`.

**status** `string`

`initiated` — minted, waiting for someone to complete the Connect Link.
`active` — authorized and usable.
`failed` — authorization did not complete.
`disconnected` — the stored credential was dropped.

**status\_reason** `string | null`

Why a `failed` or `disconnected` account got there.

**connect\_link** `string | null`

The hosted authorization URL. Present only while `initiated`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **This URL is not on a Naive Managed Agents domain.** The authorization page is served by the connection provider, on the provider's own host, carrying the provider's name and a "Secured by" badge. Hand it to an end user; do not treat it as part of your product's surface. See [Connections](/docs/identity/connections) for what the provider's own white-labelling does and does not cover.

**connect\_link\_expires\_at** `string | null`

When that link stops working.

**last\_refreshed\_at** `string | null`

Last successful credential refresh.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

### Connect an account

`POST /v1/connections` — scope `billing:write`

Mints the connected account and its Connect Link; the account starts `initiated`. This is `billing:write` on the wire and not `agents:write` because a managed account is a per-account charge at the provider.

**auth\_config\_id** `string` *required*

The `ac_` config to mint against.

**identity** `string` *required*

The `idn_` identity that will act in the account.

**fields** `object`

Values for the config's `connect_fields`, e.g. `{ "subdomain": "acme" }`. Omitted, the hosted page asks the person instead — so this is a convenience, never a gate.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/connections \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "auth_config_id": "ac_01H9CN...", "identity": "idn_01H...", "fields": { "subdomain": "acme" } }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "ca_01H9CQ...",
  "object": "connection",
  "auth_config_id": "ac_01H9CN...",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H...",
  "connector": "zendesk",
  "status": "initiated",
  "status_reason": null,
  "connect_link": "https://<provider-host>/link/...",
  "connect_link_expires_at": "2026-08-20T18:10:00Z",
  "last_refreshed_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:10:00Z"
}
```

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) when `identity` is not an `idn_` id or `auth_config_id` is not an `ac_` id; `not_found` (404) for an unknown auth config or identity; `forbidden` (403) without `billing:write`; `insufficient_credits` (402).

### List connections

`GET /v1/connections` — scope `agents:read`

**identity** `string`

Filter to one persona.

Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of connection objects.

### Retrieve a connection

`GET /v1/connections/{id}` — scope `agents:read`

Reconciles status against the provider before answering — **this read is the refresh**. Poll it to watch an `initiated` account become `active`, rather than assuming the Connect Link was completed. There is no `connection.*` webhook yet, so polling this route is the only way to learn that a person finished authorizing.

### Disconnect

`DELETE /v1/connections/{id}` — scope `agents:write`

Revoke. The provider drops the stored credential and every later call through the connection is refused. Returns the standard deleted envelope.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ca_01H9CQ...", "object": "connection", "deleted": true }
```

> [card] [Identities](/docs/api/identities)
>
> The persona a connection is bound to.


# Credits
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/credits

Real-USD balance, metered ledger, and top-ups.

Billing is **real US dollars** held as a credit balance on the [organization](/docs/api/organizations). Every metered action debits the balance; top-ups credit it. All money fields are integer **micro-USD** (`*_micro_usd`, where 1 USD = 1,000,000 micro-USD).

## Balance

`GET /v1/credits/balance` returns the current balance.

**object** `string`

Always `credit_balance`.

**balance\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Available balance, in micro-USD.

**mode** `string`

`live` or `test` — the tier this balance is held in.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/balance \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "object": "credit_balance", "balance_micro_usd": 48250000, "mode": "live" }
```

## Ledger

`GET /v1/credits/ledger` lists metered entries, newest first. Cursor-paginated — see [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination). Each inference debit carries a **5-tier token line-item** breakdown of what was metered.

**data** `object[]`

Ledger entries.

**entry**

**id** `string`

Entry id (e.g. `led_01H...`).

**type** `string`

`debit` (usage) or `credit` (top-up/adjustment).

**amount\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Signed amount, in micro-USD.

**balance\_after\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Running balance after this entry.

**actor** `object`

The principal responsible for the entry — the same shape as the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) actor.

**actor**

**type** `string`

`user`, `key`, or `system`.

**id** `string`

Id of the member (`usr_…`) or API key (`key_…`). A settled top-up is credited by `{ "type": "system", "id": "payment_webhook" }`.

**session\_id** `string | null`

The session that incurred the charge, if any.

**agent\_id** `string | null`

The agent that ran the session, if any.

**deployment\_id** `string | null`

The deployment whose run incurred the charge, if any.

**resource\_id** `string | null`

The computer (`cmp_…`), browser session (`brw_…`) or phone (`mob_…`) the charge is for, if any.

**line\_items** `object[]`

The 5-tier token breakdown of a metered inference debit. Each inference debit records all five classes. Non-model charges carry one line on their own tier.

**line\_item**

**tier** `string`

A token class — `input`, `cache_write`, `cache_read`, `output`, `reasoning` — or a metered capability: `computer` (sandbox time), `search`, `media`, `social`, `browser`, `email` (one outbound email send), `voice` (live voice call minutes), `storage` (a [storage](/docs/api/storage) bucket-day; no rate is published yet, so no `storage` line is booked).

**amount\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Amount metered for this token class.

**created\_at** `string`

Entry timestamp.

Filter the ledger with any combination of `?type=`, `?session_id=`, `?agent_id=`, `?deployment_id=`, `?from=`, and `?to=` (each `from`/`to` bound is a date like `2026-08-01` or a timestamp like `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z`, an offset's `+` sent as `%2B`; anything else is `400 validation_failed` naming the parameter).

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/ledger?limit=20&type=debit&agent_id=agt_01H..." \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "led_01H9KK...",
      "type": "debit",
      "amount_micro_usd": -412300,
      "balance_after_micro_usd": 48250000,
      "actor": { "type": "key", "id": "key_01H8XK..." },
      "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...",
      "agent_id": "agt_01H8XK...",
      "deployment_id": null,
      "resource_id": null,
      "line_items": [
        { "tier": "input",       "amount_micro_usd": 148000 },
        { "tier": "cache_write", "amount_micro_usd": 32100 },
        { "tier": "cache_read",  "amount_micro_usd": 11400 },
        { "tier": "output",      "amount_micro_usd": 196500 },
        { "tier": "reasoning",   "amount_micro_usd": 24300 }
      ],
      "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:04Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "led_01H9KK..."
}
```

## Spend

`GET /v1/credits/spend` → `200 OK`. What the matching debits spent, in positive micro-USD, summed over the whole range: the total, the split by tier, and the 50 dearest agents and sessions, dearest first. It takes the ledger's `?session_id=`, `?agent_id=`, `?deployment_id=`, `?from=` and `?to=`. Use it for any total or chart: a sum over one ledger page misses every debit past it.

`?days=` (1 to 90) adds `by_day`: the company's spend per day for that many days, ending today, on `?timezone=` (default the organization's). It is the whole company's spend, so it takes no other filter. With `?days=`, `spent_micro_usd` is those days' total and `by_tier`, `by_agent` and `by_session` are empty: read the splits with `?from=` instead.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/spend?from=2026-08-01T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "spent_micro_usd": 41873200,
  "by_tier": { "input": 30112000, "output": 9861200, "computer": 1900000 },
  "by_agent": [{ "agent_id": "agt_01H8XK...", "spent_micro_usd": 41873200 }],
  "by_session": [{ "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "spent_micro_usd": 12004100 }]
}
```

## Top up

`POST /v1/credits/topups` opens a hosted charge and returns a **topup object** describing it. It does **not** move the balance: credit is applied when the payment provider's signed callback arrives and is verified, so poll the [balance](#balance) rather than reading the create response as settlement. Requires the `billing:write` scope.

A company [being set up](/docs/api/organizations#set-up-a-company) cannot top up: it runs on its one-time setup credit, and its next step is the plan. The call is refused with `subscription_required` (402) until the company is activated.

**amount\_micro\_usd** `integer` *required*

Amount to add, in micro-USD.

**return\_to** `string`

Optional app-relative path to preserve through the hosted checkout. Absolute and protocol-relative URLs are refused.

### The topup object

**id** `string`

Opaque top-up id. Store it as a string and do not parse it or rely on its format. When the charge settles, the `credits.topped_up`[audit](/docs/api/audit-logs) row names it as `resource_id`.

**amount\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Amount requested, in micro-USD.

**status** `string`

Lifecycle state. One of:

* `pending` — the charge is being processed.
* `requires_action` — the payment needs additional authentication (e.g. 3-D Secure). Complete it via `action_url`, then poll.
* `succeeded` — the charge cleared and the balance was credited.
* `failed` — the charge was declined; the balance is unchanged.

**action\_url** `string | null`

Present only when `status` is `requires_action`: the URL to complete authentication.

**balance\_after\_micro\_usd** `integer | null`

Always `null` on this response — the balance moves only when the provider callback settles the charge. Read the [balance](#balance) instead.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/topups \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{ "amount_micro_usd": 50000000 }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "9f2c41d7e0b3...",
  "object": "topup",
  "amount_micro_usd": 50000000,
  "status": "requires_action",
  "action_url": "https://checkout.example/pay/cs_01H9LL...",
  "balance_after_micro_usd": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:35:00Z"
}
```

### Confirming a charge that is not yet terminal

A charge can land in `pending` or `requires_action`, so the `status` on the create response is not always the final word.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **There is no `GET /v1/credits/topups/{id}`.** A top-up is not individually addressable — that route is not served and answers `404 not_found`. Confirm a charge by re-reading the balance or the ledger, not by polling a top-up id.

Two ways to reach the terminal state:

* **Poll the balance.** `GET /v1/credits/balance` reflects the credit as soon as the charge clears. This is the simplest check when you know the amount you expect.
* **Read the ledger.** `GET /v1/credits/ledger` lists entries newest-first; the settled top-up appears as a `credit` entry. Match it by `created_at` and `amount_micro_usd`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/ledger?limit=1 \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

When `status` comes back `requires_action`, send the payer to `action_url` first; the balance does not move until they complete authentication.

> [!NOTE]
>
> When the balance is too low to cover a call, the API returns `insufficient_credits` (402); when a call would breach a configured per-agent or per-session cap it returns `budget_exceeded` (402). Top up (or raise the cap), then retry — see [Errors](/docs/api/errors) and [Agents](/docs/api/agents). Successful top-ups are recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `credits.topped_up`.

## The plan

Credits pay for what an agent *does*. The **plan** is separate: it is the right to use the organization at all. Every organization needs an active plan before any route outside billing will answer. Without one the API returns `subscription_required` (402) with the message telling you exactly what to do.

| Plan | Price | Included credit | Free trial |
| - | - | - | - |
| `standard` | **\$20 per month** | \$20 each paid month | 7 days, with \$10 of credit |
| `pro` | **\$200 per month** | \$200 each paid month | none |

Included credit is added to the prepaid balance and **rolls over**: it never expires. Creating an organization does not start a plan. Buy one, then the organization works.

### Reading the plan

`GET /v1/credits/subscription` returns the current plan. Requires the `billing:read` scope, and is answerable whether or not a plan is active.

**include\_payment\_method** `boolean` (default: false)

`true` adds `payment_method`, the card the plan bills. It is read from the payment provider at call time, so it is left out of the default read. It also needs the `billing:write` scope, and is refused (`403 forbidden`) without it and for any call an agent makes.

**status** `string`

One of:

* `none` — no plan has ever started. Every gated route is refused.
* `active` — the organization can be used.
* `past_due` — the last payment did not go through. The organization keeps working until `grace_until`, then is refused.
* `canceled` — the plan ended. Every gated route is refused.

A free trial reads `active` too: there is no `trialing` status. `trial_end` says the trial is running.

**plan** `string | null`

`standard` or `pro`. `null` until the organization first subscribes.

**price\_micro\_usd** `integer | null`

The plan's monthly list price — `20000000` or `200000000`. `null` while `plan` is.

**included\_credit\_micro\_usd** `integer | null`

The credit each paid month adds to the balance. `null` while `plan` is.

**current\_period\_end** `string | null`

When the paid period ends, or `null` if no plan has ever started.

**grace\_until** `string | null`

While `past_due`, the moment the organization stops working. `null` means no grace remains.

**cancel\_at\_period\_end** `boolean`

`true` once a cancellation has been asked for. The organization stays usable until `current_period_end` and is refused after it.

**trial\_end** `string | null`

While the free trial is running, the moment it converts to a paid Standard month. `null` otherwise.

**pending\_plan** `string | null`

The plan a scheduled downgrade moves to at `current_period_end`, else `null`.

**trial\_eligible** `boolean`

Whether `POST` with `{"plan": "standard"}` from this caller would start the free trial. One trial per organization and one per person: an organization that already had a plan is not offered one, and neither is an organization whose caller, owners or creator — under any `+tag` or Gmail-dot spelling of their address — asked for a trial at another organization that started one (or one opened there in the last 24 hours), or belongs to or created an organization that used one. Leaving an organization does not reset it.

**trial\_days** `integer`

The free trial's length on this deployment, in days. `0` when trials are off.

**trial\_credit\_micro\_usd** `integer`

The credit the free trial starts with. `0` when trials are off.

**plans\_available** `string[]`

The plans this deployment sells: `["standard", "pro"]`, or `["standard"]` where Pro is not offered. `POST` or `PATCH` with a plan not listed answers `501 feature_not_configured`.

**payment\_method** `object | null`

Only with `include_payment_method=true`. The card the plan bills, as `{"last4": "4242"}`, so a screen can name it before an upgrade charges it. `null` when the organization has no plan with a card, or the card could not be read.

**plans** `object[]`

Each plan in `plans_available`, in the same order, as `{ plan, price_micro_usd, included_credit_micro_usd }`: its monthly list price and the credit each paid month adds. Present whether or not a plan is held, so the price can be shown before checkout.

**action\_url** `string | null`

Always `null` on a read; see below.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **An `active` plan whose `current_period_end` is more than three days in the past stops being honoured.** Renewals reach us as signed callbacks, and a callback that never arrives must not become permanent free access. Any later callback moves the deadline forward again, so a plan that is genuinely paid heals itself the moment the next event lands.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/subscription \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "subscription",
  "status": "active",
  "plan": "standard",
  "price_micro_usd": 20000000,
  "included_credit_micro_usd": 20000000,
  "current_period_end": "2026-09-22T17:30:00Z",
  "grace_until": null,
  "cancel_at_period_end": false,
  "trial_end": "2026-09-22T17:30:00Z",
  "pending_plan": null,
  "trial_eligible": false,
  "trial_days": 7,
  "trial_credit_micro_usd": 10000000,
  "plans_available": ["standard", "pro"],
  "plans": [
    { "plan": "standard", "price_micro_usd": 20000000, "included_credit_micro_usd": 20000000 },
    { "plan": "pro", "price_micro_usd": 200000000, "included_credit_micro_usd": 200000000 }
  ],
  "action_url": null
}
```

### Starting or renewing the plan

`POST /v1/credits/subscription` opens a hosted checkout page and returns its URL as `action_url` (`201`). The body is optional: `{"plan": "standard"}` (the default — an empty body is Standard) or `{"plan": "pro"}`. Requires the `billing:write` scope.

**plan** `string` (default: standard)

`standard` or `pro`.

**The free trial.** When the plan is `standard` and `trial_eligible` is `true`, the checkout starts a **7-day free trial**: a card is required on the page, $10 of credit is granted when the trial starts (on an eligible card: see [Pricing](/platform/pricing)), and unless it is cancelled first the trial converts to $20 per month — with the full \$20 of credit — when it ends. Cancel during the trial (`DELETE` below, or the account page) and nothing is charged. A caller who is not eligible gets the same checkout without the trial, billed on the day. Pro has no trial.

Like a top-up, it changes **nothing** on its own: the organization becomes usable once the payment (or the trial) is confirmed, which is normally a second or two after the customer completes the page. Re-read `GET /v1/credits/subscription` until `status` is `active`.

An organization whose plan is already `active` is refused with `state_conflict` (409): a second checkout would be a second plan billed. Change the tier with `PATCH` below instead. A company [being set up](/docs/api/organizations#set-up-a-company) starts here: the payment that makes its plan `active` **activates** it (`setting_up` turns `false`), and the crew it held while it was set up is built ([installs](/docs/api/apps)).

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X POST https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/subscription \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"plan": "standard"}'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "subscription",
  "status": "none",
  "plan": null,
  "price_micro_usd": null,
  "included_credit_micro_usd": null,
  "current_period_end": null,
  "grace_until": null,
  "cancel_at_period_end": false,
  "trial_end": null,
  "pending_plan": null,
  "trial_eligible": true,
  "action_url": "https://checkout.example/c/pay/..."
}
```

### Changing the plan

`PATCH /v1/credits/subscription` with `{"plan": "pro"}` or `{"plan": "standard"}` changes an `active` plan in place. Requires the `billing:write` scope; audited as `subscription.plan_changed`.

**plan** `string` *required*

`standard` or `pro`.

* **Standard → Pro is immediate.** The difference for the rest of the current month is charged at once on the card already on file, the billing date stays the same, and the answer reads `plan: "pro"`. Upgrading during the free trial ends the trial and charges $200 now. The proration invoice grants what it collected as credit, up to $200.
* **Pro → Standard takes effect at the end of the period already paid for.** Nothing is refunded and the Pro credit already granted is kept. Until then the plan reads `plan: "pro"` with `pending_plan: "standard"`; asking for `pro` again before then takes the downgrade back, free.
* Asking for the plan already held, with nothing pending, changes nothing and answers `200`.
* An organization with no `active` plan is refused with `state_conflict` (409) naming `POST`.
* A plan set to cancel at the end of its period is refused with `state_conflict` (409): there is no plan to change.

Like every route here, the read is the truth: the answer reports what was asked, and the confirmed callback rewrites it a moment later.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/subscription \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"plan": "pro"}'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "subscription",
  "status": "active",
  "plan": "pro",
  "price_micro_usd": 200000000,
  "included_credit_micro_usd": 200000000,
  "current_period_end": "2026-09-22T17:30:00Z",
  "grace_until": null,
  "cancel_at_period_end": false,
  "trial_end": null,
  "pending_plan": null,
  "trial_eligible": false,
  "action_url": null
}
```

### Cancelling the plan

`DELETE /v1/credits/subscription` stops the plan **at the end of the period already paid for** — never immediately, and nothing is refunded or charged again. Requires the `billing:write` scope, and like the two routes above it answers whether or not the organization is currently usable: a recurring charge you can only stop by paying first is not one a customer can stop.

The organization keeps working until `current_period_end`, and is refused after it. Re-read `GET /v1/credits/subscription` to see `cancel_at_period_end` become `true` — the state follows the payment provider's confirmation, so the read is the truth, not this response.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X DELETE https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/subscription \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "subscription",
  "status": "active",
  "plan": "standard",
  "price_micro_usd": 20000000,
  "included_credit_micro_usd": 20000000,
  "current_period_end": "2026-09-22T17:30:00Z",
  "grace_until": null,
  "cancel_at_period_end": true,
  "trial_end": null,
  "pending_plan": null,
  "trial_eligible": false,
  "action_url": null
}
```

Cancelling also drops a scheduled downgrade. Cancelling during the free trial ends it at `trial_end` with nothing charged. To restart after cancelling, `POST /v1/credits/subscription` again — without a second free trial.

### Managing the payment method, invoices and cancellation

`POST /v1/credits/billing_portal` returns a link to the payment provider's own hosted account page, where a customer can change the card on file, download past invoices, and cancel. It takes no body and requires the `billing:write` scope. The link is single-use and expires — follow it, do not store it.

Like every other route on this page it changes **nothing** by itself. Whatever the customer does on that page arrives back as the same confirmed events that already move the plan, so re-read `GET /v1/credits/subscription` afterwards rather than assuming an outcome.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X POST https://api.vetta.sh/v1/credits/billing_portal \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "billing_portal_session",
  "action_url": "https://billing.example/session/..."
}
```

An organization that has never held a plan has no account to manage, and this answers `404 not_found` rather than an empty page:

```json 404 theme={"system"}
{
  "error": {
    "type": "not_found",
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "this organization has no billing account to manage; start the plan with `POST /v1/credits/subscription` first",
    "request_id": "req_..."
  }
}
```

### What stays open without a plan

An organization with no plan can still identify itself, read its own billing state, and pay. Everything else is refused with `subscription_required` (402).

| Open without a plan | Refused without a plan |
| - | - |
| `POST /v1/organizations`, `POST /v1/organizations/setup`, `POST /v1/auth/session`, `POST /v1/auth/users` | `/v1/agents/*`, `/v1/sessions/*`, `/v1/computers/*` |
| `GET /v1/me`, `GET /v1/organizations`, `GET /v1/organizations/{id}`, `GET /v1/organizations/{id}/members` | `/v1/deployments/*`, `/v1/files/*`, `/v1/skills/*` (except the public catalogue, `GET /v1/skills/catalog` and its entries) |
| `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /v1/credits/subscription`, `POST /v1/credits/billing_portal` | `/v1/api_keys`, `/v1/webhooks`, `/v1/vaults/*` |
| `GET /v1/credits/balance`, `GET /v1/credits/ledger`, `GET /v1/credits/spend`, `POST /v1/credits/topups` | `/v1/identities/*`, `/v1/domains/*`, `/v1/connections/*` |

**A company being set up** ([organizations](/docs/api/organizations#set-up-a-company)) has no plan yet but is not locked: on top of the column above, it may run its CEO chat — reading and making its CEO, the CEO's sessions and their messages, events and plans, recording a template as `held`, renaming the company and setting its logo and brand kit — on the setup model, paid for by its setup credit. Files, transcription, voice and everything else in the right-hand column stay `subscription_required` (402) until it is activated.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **A session already running is never cut off mid-turn.** The plan is checked when work is *admitted* — starting a session, sending it a message, or a schedule firing — not on every turn of a session already under way. A lapse stops new work; it does not kill a task in flight. Plan changes are recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `subscription.updated`, and a customer's own cancellation as `subscription.canceled`.


# CRM and Calendar
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/crm

A company's clients, their timelines, and its meetings.

A company's clients and its meetings, kept by its agents and open to a person. Every route takes `agents:write`, the reads too.

## Contacts

A contact has a `name`, `company`, `email`, `phone`, `stage` (`lead`, `talking`, `proposal`, `won`, `lost`), `value_micro_usd`, `next_step`, `next_step_at` and `source`. An email is on file once per company: adding one already on file updates that contact, and never moves its stage.

* `GET /v1/crm/contacts`, newest touched first. Filter with `stage` and `q` (name, company or email).
* `POST /v1/crm/contacts`
* `GET /v1/crm/contacts/{id}`, with its `activity`, newest first.
* `PATCH /v1/crm/contacts/{id}`. A stage that changes writes its own line on the timeline.
* `DELETE /v1/crm/contacts/{id}`. Deletes the contact and its timeline.

## Timeline

A line has a `kind` (`note`, `email`, `call`, `meeting`, `stage`), a `body`, `at`, `ends_at`, and `by`: the agent that wrote it, or `null` for a person. Only a meeting may stand without a contact. A `stage` line is written by the move itself, and stays.

* `POST /v1/crm/activity`
* `PATCH /v1/crm/activity/{id}`
* `DELETE /v1/crm/activity/{id}`

## Calendar

`GET /v1/crm/calendar?from=&to=` reads meetings, and each open contact's next step on its day, soonest first, across at most a year.

## From an agent

In a company whose template declares the CRM, agents have `crm.read` and `crm.write`, and `open_panel` turns the panel beside the chat to `crm`, `calendar` or `ads`. An agent cannot delete a contact.


# Data
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/data

Search a catalogue of read-only data tools in 18 domains, read one's input schema, and run it — priced per run.

Three routes over one catalogue of read-only data tools in 18 domains — social media, people, companies, funding, markets, SEO, news, law, weather, jobs, property, reviews, trade, shopping and travel. The same catalogue an agent's `data_*` [tools](/docs/capabilities/tools) use; the guide is [Data](/docs/capabilities/data). The [social data routes](/docs/api/social-data) are its `social` domain under their own names.

## The data tool object

**object** `string`

Always `data_tool`.

**id** `string`

Opaque. Pass it back to [describe](#describe-a-tool) or [run](#run-a-tool) unchanged; it has no prefix and is not a stored object.

**name** `string`

What the tool does, briefly.

**description** `string`

What it returns. On [describe](#describe-a-tool), the long form.

**domains** `string[]`

What it is about: `social`, `search`, `people`, `companies`, `compliance`, `funding`, `seo`, `finance`, `crypto`, `news`, `legal`, `weather`, `jobs`, `real_estate`, `reviews`, `trade`, `shopping`, `travel`. See [Domains](/docs/capabilities/data#domains).

**platforms** `string[]`

For a `social` tool, the networks it reads (empty for every other domain): `x`, `instagram`, `tiktok`, `facebook`, `reddit`, `youtube`, `snapchat`, `linkedin`, `threads`, `telegram`, `douyin`, `kuaishou`, `xiaohongshu`, `weibo`, `bilibili`, `zhihu`, `wechat`, `lemon8`, `pipixia`, `toutiao`, `xigua`.

**price** `object`

What a run costs **you**: `basis` (`per_call`, `per_result` or `varies`), `micro_usd` (integer; for `varies`, the highest case) and `text` (`"$0.002 per call"`).

## Search tools

`GET /v1/data/tools` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. Free.

**query** `string` *required*

What you need, as a short noun phrase (1–200 characters): `company funding rounds`, `homes for sale`.

**domain** `string`

Only tools in this domain (one of `domains` above).

**platform** `string`

Only social tools for this network (one of `platforms` above); implies `domain=social`.

**limit** `integer`

1–20, default 8.

Answers `{ data: data_tool[] }`, best match first. There is no cursor: the ranking is the page.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/data/tools?query=company%20funding%20rounds&domain=funding&limit=3" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const { data } = await client.data.searchTools({ query: "company funding rounds", domain: "funding", limit: 3 });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive data search "company funding rounds" --domain funding --limit 3
```

## Describe a tool

`GET /v1/data/tools/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. Free.

Answers the [tool](#the-data-tool-object) plus:

**input** `object`

A JSON Schema per input location — `path`, `query`, `body` — each present only when the tool takes it. A [run](#run-a-tool) sends parameters in the same three places.

**notes** `string[]`

Usage notes: quirks, limits, the parameter that controls volume.

An `id` that is not a data tool is `404 not_found`.

## Run a tool

`POST /v1/data/runs` → `200 OK` — scope `sessions:write`. Priced. [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) optional: a retry under the same key replays the first answer and is billed once.

**tool\_id** `string` *required*

An `id` from search.

**query** `object`

Query parameters, as `input.query` describes.

**path** `object`

Path parameters, as `input.path` describes.

**body** `object`

Body fields, as `input.body` describes.

The request returns when the run ends — usually seconds, at most about two minutes.

**object** `string`

Always `data_run`.

**tool\_id** `string`

The tool that ran.

**status** `string`

`succeeded` or `failed`. A failed run is still a `200`: it happened, and `error` says why.

**data** `any`

The source's data, unchanged. `null` when failed.

**error** `string | null`

Why it failed, in words that say what to change — often the parameter the source refused.

**cost\_micro\_usd** `integer`

What this run debited, on the `search` tier. Normally `0` for a failed run, and then no ledger entry is written; a stopped per-result run debits what it gathered.

**created\_at** `string`

ISO 8601.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/data/runs \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "tool_id": "<tool_id>", "query": { "company": "acme.com" } }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const run = await client.data.run({ tool_id, query: { company: "acme.com" } });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive data run <tool_id> --query company=acme.com
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "data_run",
  "tool_id": "<tool_id>",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "data": { "company": "acme.com", "rounds": [{ "type": "Series A", "amount_usd": 12000000 }] },
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": 2000,
  "created_at": "2026-10-04T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Errors

| Status | `code` | When |
| - | - | - |
| 400 | `validation_failed` | A missing `tool_id`, a parameter location that is not an object, an argument the tool's `input` schema requires but you left out or gave the wrong type (`param` names it, e.g. `query.username`), or input the service refused before running. Nothing is billed. |
| 402 | `insufficient_credits` | The prepaid balance is below the tool's listed price for one call (or for 25 results on a per-result tool, the most one run returns). Checked before the run starts. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The `tool_id` is not a data tool. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many runs at once; retry shortly. |
| 501 | `feature_not_configured` | Data is not enabled on this deployment. |
| 502 | `provider_error` | The service did not answer, the run passed two minutes and was stopped, or a run succeeded but the service had not reported its cost yet (its output is withheld; retry). Nothing is billed. |

## Pricing

Search and describe are free. Each run is capped at 25 results: any result-count field above 25, at any depth of the input (`limit`, `maxItems`, `maxResults`, `resultsPerPage`, `pageSize`, `num…`, `max…`, `…Count`), is lowered to 25, and the balance must cover the listed price for one call (or for 30 results on a per-result tool, since some sources bill results in blocks of 10). It is then booked at the tool's `price`, once on the `search` component; a failed or stopped run is normally free, but one the source billed (a timeout or stop that had already gathered results) costs what it gathered. See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#priced-tools).


# Database
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/database

The managed database of a fullstack app as its own primitive: SQL, the table catalogue, a REST passthrough over every table, and a migration ledger.

Every `fullstack` [app](/docs/api/apps) comes with a managed Postgres database. These routes reach it
directly — no connection string, no client library — so an agent, the SDK or the CLI can work with
data the way they work with any other resource.

All routes live under one app: `/v1/apps/{id}/db/…`. `{id}` is an `app_` id, an app **name**, or the
word **`default`**, which resolves the organization's only `fullstack` app — the standalone feeling
for the common case of one app. With two or more `fullstack` apps `default` answers
`409 ambiguous_app`, with the candidate ids in the message; with none, `404 not_found`. `default`
never moves: when the app it named is deleted while another exists, it answers `409 ambiguous_app`
rather than resolve to the one left. Every answer
carries the resolved app in a `vetta-app-id` response header: a script that creates a second app
later pins the one it meant by passing that id instead of `default`.

The database exists only once the app is `active`: a `frontend_only` app answers
`501 feature_not_configured`, and a still-provisioning backend answers a retryable `job_not_ready`.

## Run SQL

`POST /v1/apps/{id}/db/query` — scope `agents:write`

**query** `string` *required*

The SQL to run.

A request's SQL may run for **30 seconds**. Past that the database cancels it and the request answers
`400 validation_failed` with "canceling statement due to statement timeout"; nothing it did is kept.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "app_db_result",
  "rows": [{ "count": 42 }],
  "row_count": 1
}
```

## List tables

`GET /v1/apps/{id}/db/tables` — scope `agents:read`

Every user table in the database, including the `vetta_migrations` ledger once a migration has
run. Not paginated: one database has a bounded catalogue.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    { "object": "db_table", "name": "todos", "schema": "public", "rows": 12, "size_bytes": 16384 }
  ]
}
```

`rows` and `size_bytes` are estimates from the database's statistics and may be `null` on a table
that has never been analysed.

## REST

| Route | Scope | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `GET /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:read` | Read rows: `…/rest/todos?done=eq.false&select=id,title&order=id`. |
| `HEAD /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:read` | The same read without the body — with `Prefer: count=exact`, just the count in `Content-Range`. |
| `POST /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:write` | Insert the JSON body's rows. |
| `PATCH /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:write` | Update the rows the filter selects with the JSON body. |
| `PUT /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:write` | Upsert one row by its primary key filter. |
| `DELETE /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | `agents:write` | Delete the rows the filter selects. |

A passthrough to the database's REST layer: every table is a resource under `…/db/rest/`, filters and
ordering ride the query string, and JSON goes in and out. `/v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/todos?done=eq.false&order=id` reads
open todos; `POST …/rest/todos` with a JSON body inserts; `PATCH …/rest/todos?id=eq.7` updates;
`DELETE …/rest/todos?id=eq.7` deletes. Filters are `column=op.value`: `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`,
`lt`, `lte`, `like`, `ilike`, `is`, `in`, and their `not.` negations.

Three request headers are forwarded — `Prefer` (`return=representation` to get the written rows
back, `count=exact` for a total), `Range` and `Content-Type` — and a success's status and JSON body
come back verbatim, with the `Content-Range` header when the upstream set it. A refused call answers
in the usual [error](#errors) shape with the database's own message.

One read returns **at most 1,000 rows**, whatever `limit` says; `Content-Range` (`0-999/*`) tells you
which rows came back. To read more, fix an `order` and page with `offset=0`, `1000`, `2000`, … until a
page holds fewer than 1,000 rows.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **This is admin access.** Calls run as the database's service role, so the row-level security
> policies your app enforces for its own users do not apply here. Every call — read or write — is
> recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `app.db_rest` with its method, path and status; the
> body is never recorded.

## Apply a migration

`POST /v1/apps/{id}/db/migrations` — scope `agents:write`. **`Idempotency-Key` is required.**

**name** `string` *required*

Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`; up to 128 characters. The name is what makes the migration idempotent.

**sql** `string` *required*

The SQL to run. It is hashed (SHA-256) and recorded alongside the name.

A migration is applied **once per name**, tracked in a `vetta_migrations` table the platform keeps
on the app's own database:

* new name → the SQL runs and the response is `201` with the ledger row;
* same name, same SQL → nothing runs and the response is `200` with the existing row — a replay;
* same name, **different** SQL → `409 version_conflict`; a migration's SQL is immutable, so write a
  new one.

The `vetta_migrations` table is read-only outside this route: a REST write to it, or SQL that
writes it, answers `403 forbidden`. Schema changes (DDL) also work through [Run SQL](#run-sql), but
only a migration is recorded and replay-safe, so prefer one.

A newly applied migration is recorded in the audit log as `app.db_migrated` and pushed to
[webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) subscribers as `app.db.migrated` with `{ app_id, migration_id, name }`; a
replay is neither.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "dbm_01H...",
  "object": "db_migration",
  "name": "0001_todos",
  "sha256": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
  "applied_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z",
  "statements": 1
}
```

## List migrations

`GET /v1/apps/{id}/db/migrations` — scope `agents:read`

The ledger, in `applied_at` order, as `{ "data": db_migration[] }`.

## Errors

| Code | Status | When |
| - | - | - |
| `ambiguous_app` | 409 | `default` (or an omitted app in the SDK/CLI) and the organization holds several `fullstack` apps — or the app `default` named was deleted while another existed, and `default` does not move to that one. The message lists the ids; name one. |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such app — or, for `default`, no `fullstack` app at all. |
| `feature_not_configured` | 501 | The app is `frontend_only` and has no database. |
| `job_not_ready` | 409 | The backend is still provisioning; retry. |
| `validation_failed` | 400 | SQL the database refused (the message says why) or that ran past 30 seconds, a REST request it refused, a REST path that escapes the table space, a bad migration name, or a missing `Idempotency-Key`. |
| `version_conflict` | 409 | A migration name re-applied with different SQL. |
| `state_conflict` | 409 | A REST write the database refused as a conflict, such as a duplicate key. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | A write without `agents:write`, or a write to the `vetta_migrations` ledger outside a migration. |
| `provider_error` | 502 | The database itself failed; retry. |


# Deployments
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/deployments

Run an agent on a cron schedule.
