A **deployment** runs an [agent](/docs/api/agents) automatically on a cron schedule. Each fire creates a new [session](/docs/api/sessions) from a fixed first input (`input_template`), subject to its own budget. Use deployments for recurring, unattended work.

## The deployment object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `dep_01H...`).

**agent\_id** `string`

The agent to run.

**agent\_version** `integer | null`

Pinned [agent version](/docs/api/agents#the-agent-version-object) each run uses. `null` means every fire tracks the agent's `current_version`. A pin on the version an update or rollback replaces moves up to the new version; a pin on any older version stays.

**cron** `string`

Cron expression defining the schedule, read in `timezone`.

**timezone** `string`

IANA zone the `cron` is read in (default: the [organization's `timezone`](/docs/api/organizations)), so `0 9 * * 1` stays 09:00 local across a daylight-saving shift.

**input\_template** `string`

Text used as the session's first input on each run. The input ends with the time the run was scheduled for (or, for `POST /v1/deployments/{id}/run`, when it started), in the deployment's timezone and in UTC, so a template can say "since the last run".

**budget\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Per-run session budget, in micro-USD. Always set — it is required at create. `0` means none of its own: each fire runs on the agent's `budget.max_task_micro_usd`.

**window** `string`

Completion window for scheduled runs.

**on\_idle** `string | null`

URL POSTed with the `session.idle` envelope when a fire goes idle. A non-null value has a [webhook endpoint](/docs/api/webhooks) behind it, listed by `GET /v1/webhooks` with `events: ["deployment.on_idle"]`; `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate` returns the secret these deliveries are signed with, and `GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries` is their log. This field is the authority: if the endpoint behind it is re-pointed elsewhere, the push is refused rather than sent to the other URL.

**identity** `string | null`

The [persona](/docs/identity/personas) every fire speaks as, as an `idn_` id. `null` runs each fire as no persona.

**enabled** `boolean`

Whether the schedule is active — what you asked for.

**schedule\_status** `string`

Whether anything will act on it — what you get. `scheduled` (a clock is watching it), `paused` (`enabled: false`), or `unscheduled` (enabled, but no clock runs schedules on this installation, so it will never fire on its own).

**next\_run\_at** `string | null`

Next fire time, and **`null` unless `schedule_status` is `scheduled`** — a date nothing will honour is worse than none. An `unscheduled` deployment still fires on demand with `POST /v1/deployments/{id}/run`.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Create a deployment

`POST /v1/deployments` → `201 Created`.

**agent\_id** `string` *required*

The agent to run on schedule.

**agent\_version** `integer`

Pin runs to a specific agent version for staged rollout or rollback. Omit to always track the agent's `current_version`. To hold a schedule back while the agent changes, pin a version older than the current one: a pin on the current version follows the next update.

**cron** `string` *required*

Cron expression (e.g. `0 9 * * 1` = Mondays at 09:00), read in `timezone`. A schedule may fire at most every 5 minutes: one with any two fires closer than that (`* * * * *`, `*/2 * * * *`) is refused.

**timezone** `string`

IANA zone the `cron` is read in. Defaults to the [organization's `timezone`](/docs/api/organizations), not UTC: a routine created without one runs on the company's clock.

**input\_template** `string` *required*

The input each run sends to its session.

**budget\_micro\_usd** `integer` *required*

Per-run budget in micro-USD. It must be stated. `0` runs each fire on the agent's own task budget (`budget.max_task_micro_usd`), the ceiling any session of that agent has. At most the agent's `cap_micro_usd` (`validation_failed` otherwise).

**window** `string`

Completion window (`immediate | priority | loose`). Defaults to the agent's window.

**on\_idle** `string`

URL POSTed with the `session.idle` envelope each time a fire goes idle. Defaults to `null`, which pushes nothing. Setting it provisions the webhook endpoint the pushes are delivered through, so they inherit the signature, the retry schedule, the auto-disable and the delivery log.

**identity** `string`

The [persona](/docs/identity/personas) every fire speaks as — an `idn_` id **or** the persona's name, exactly as when creating a [session](/docs/api/sessions). The agent must already hold a grant to it. It is resolved at create and stored as the id, so the response echoes `idn_…` even when you sent a name, and renaming the persona later cannot re-point the schedule. Defaults to `null`: the fire runs as no persona.

**enabled** `boolean`

Start active. Defaults to `true`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/deployments \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{
    "agent_id": "agt_01H8XK...",
    "agent_version": 2,
    "cron": "0 9 * * 1",
    "input_template": "Summarize last week'\''s refunds and publish a report.",
    "budget_micro_usd": 3000000,
    "window": "loose"
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "dep_01H9EF...",
  "object": "deployment",
  "agent_id": "agt_01H8XK...",
  "agent_version": 2,
  "cron": "0 9 * * 1",
  "input_template": "Summarize last week's refunds and publish a report.",
  "budget_micro_usd": 3000000,
  "window": "loose",
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "on_idle": null,
  "identity": null,
  "enabled": true,
  "schedule_status": "scheduled",
  "next_run_at": "2026-08-24T13:00:00Z",
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) for a missing or malformed field, an unparseable cron, one that fires more often than every 5 minutes, or an unknown timezone. Every invalid field is listed in `message` at once; `param` names the first. `not_found` (404) for an unknown agent, `agent_version` or `identity`.

## Retrieve & list

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/deployments/{id}   # retrieve one -> 200
GET /v1/deployments        # list (cursor-paginated) -> 200
```

See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

## Update a deployment

`PATCH /v1/deployments/{id}` → `200 OK`. Scope `agents:write`. A partial update — send only the fields you are changing.

Every field of the deployment is patchable **except `agent_id`**: repointing a schedule at a different agent would silently change what the cron does while keeping its history, so create a new deployment instead.

**cron** `string`

New cron expression. Recomputes `next_run_at`.

**timezone** `string`

IANA zone the cron is read in.

**input\_template** `string`

The message each fire starts with.

**agent\_version** `integer`

Pin a different agent version.

**budget\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Per-run cap, in micro-USD, at most the agent's `cap_micro_usd` (`validation_failed` otherwise).

**on\_idle** `string`

The idle-push URL, or `null` to stop pushing — `null` deletes the endpoint behind it and its signing secret. A new URL re-points the endpoint and re-enables it, so this is how a target that auto-disabled after repeated failures is brought back.

**identity** `string`

The persona each fire speaks as, or `null` to run as none. Re-validated against the agent's grants.

**enabled** `boolean`

The schedule switch — the same state [pause and resume](#pause--resume) toggle.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/deployments/dep_01H9EF... \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "cron": "0 9 * * 1-5", "timezone": "Europe/London" }'
```

Returns the full deployment object, including the recomputed `next_run_at` and `schedule_status`.

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) for an unparseable cron, an unknown timezone, an attempt to change `agent_id`, or an `identity` the agent does not hold; `not_found` (404), including an `identity` that does not exist.

## Pause & resume

`POST /v1/deployments/{id}/pause` and `POST /v1/deployments/{id}/resume` → `200 OK`. Toggle the schedule without deleting the deployment.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "dep_01H9EF...", "enabled": false, "schedule_status": "paused", "next_run_at": null }
```

## Run once, now

`POST /v1/deployments/{id}/run` → `202 Accepted`. Fires the deployment immediately, whatever its schedule says — including while it is `paused` or `unscheduled`. Every fire, scheduled or manual, is an ordinary session carrying this deployment's `deployment_id`.

## List runs

`GET /v1/deployments/{id}/runs` → `200 OK`. Lists the sessions produced by this deployment, newest first. Cursor-paginated.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    { "session_id": "ses_01H9GG...", "status": "idle", "started_at": "2026-08-24T09:00:02Z" }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Delete a deployment

`DELETE /v1/deployments/{id}` → `200 OK`. Removes the schedule. Sessions it already created are retained.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "dep_01H9EF...", "object": "deployment", "deleted": true }
```


# Digest
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/digest

The company's sessions and agents in one read: what waits on you, what failed, recent work, and each channel.

The digest is the dashboard's side rail in one request. It reads the lists the rail draws, for the
company the credential belongs to, and nothing else. Each list is cut at a cap. Past a cap, page the
list route itself.

## Read the digest

`GET /v1/digest` — scopes `sessions:read` and `agents:read`

No query parameters. Every session in it is top-level (a delegated thread is not listed) and
newest first.

| Field | What it holds | Cap |
| - | - | - |
| `agents` | The company's agents, newest first, as `GET /v1/agents` lists them. | 100 |
| `waiting.awaiting_approval` | Idle sessions parked on an approval. | 100 |
| `waiting.awaiting_answer` | Idle sessions parked on a question. | 100 |
| `waiting.budget_paused` | Idle sessions paused at their budget. | 100 |
| `failed` | Failed sessions. | 50 |
| `recent` | All sessions. | 50 |
| `channels` | For each agent in `agents`, its channel's current session: the newest one marked `metadata.room` with that agent's id that has not completed, failed or been cancelled. An agent with none has no entry. | one per agent |

Each capped list is `{ data, has_more }`. `has_more` is `true` when the list goes on past its cap.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "digest",
  "agents": { "data": [{ "object": "agent", "id": "agt_…", "name": "CEO" }], "has_more": false },
  "waiting": {
    "awaiting_approval": { "data": [{ "object": "session", "id": "ses_…", "status": "idle", "stop_reason": "awaiting_approval" }], "has_more": false },
    "awaiting_answer": { "data": [], "has_more": false },
    "budget_paused": { "data": [], "has_more": false }
  },
  "failed": { "data": [], "has_more": false },
  "recent": { "data": [{ "object": "session", "id": "ses_…" }], "has_more": true },
  "channels": { "data": [{ "object": "session", "id": "ses_…", "metadata": { "room": "agt_…" } }] }
}
```

Agents and sessions are the full objects their own routes answer.

The digest only reads. A channel from before channels were marked shows no session here; reading it
with `GET /v1/sessions?room={agent_id}` finds its conversation.

A key missing either scope is `forbidden`. A company without an active plan is
`subscription_required`, except for the person setting it up and its CEO. An agent's own token cannot read it.


# Domains
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/domains

Org-level sending and receiving domains, their DNS records, and the three readiness tracks.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Domains are part of [Identity](/docs/identity/overview). A domain belongs to the **organization**, not to one persona — two identities can send from the same domain.

A domain is what makes an [email inbox](/docs/api/messaging) deliverable. Connect a domain you own (`external`) or mint the organization's system subdomain (`system`), then publish the DNS records the API hands back.

## Three readiness tracks

Verification is not one boolean. A domain advances along three independent tracks, and each gates a different capability:

| Field | Gates | Values |
| - | - | - |
| `dns_status` | **Sending** mail (SPF/DKIM) | `pending_verification`, `provisioned`, `failed` |
| `inbound_status` | **Receiving** mail (MX) | `pending`, `verified`, `failed` |
| `app_connect_status` | HTTP/app hosting | `pending`, `connected`, `failed` |

A send is refused with a retryable `job_not_ready` until `dns_status` is `provisioned`. Receiving is unaffected by `dns_status` and waits on `inbound_status`.

## The domain object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `dom_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `domain`.

**name** `string`

The fully-qualified name, lowercase, no trailing dot.

**kind** `string`

`external` (a domain you own), `system` (a subdomain minted for the org), or `purchased` (bought with Naive credits).

**status** `string`

Overall lifecycle state of the domain record — `pending_dns`, `active`, or `failed`.

**dns\_status** `string`

Mail-sending track. See the table above.

**inbound\_status** `string`

Mail-receiving track.

**app\_connect\_status** `string`

App/HTTP track.

**records** `object[]`

The DNS records to publish. Same shape as [List DNS records](#list-dns-records).

**last\_verified\_at** `string | null`

When verification last ran.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Connect a domain

`POST /v1/domains` — scope `agents:write`

Idempotent on `name`: connecting a domain that already exists returns the existing record rather than a duplicate.

**kind** `string`

`external` (a domain you own) or `system` (a subdomain minted under the org slug). Defaults to `external`. Purchases use the separately privileged endpoint below.

**name** `string`

The domain to connect. Required for `kind: "external"`; omit for `system` and the API mints the subdomain.

**receive** `boolean`

Also request inbound (MX) records. Defaults to `true`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/domains \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "kind": "external", "name": "mail.acme.dev", "receive": true }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "dom_01H9DM...",
  "object": "domain",
  "name": "mail.acme.dev",
  "kind": "external",
  "status": "pending_dns",
  "dns_status": "pending_verification",
  "inbound_status": "pending",
  "app_connect_status": "pending",
  "records": [
    { "type": "TXT", "host": "@", "value": "v=spf1 include:...", "priority": null, "managed": true }
  ],
  "last_verified_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) when `name` is not a valid FQDN or `kind` is unknown; `forbidden` (403) without `agents:write`.

## Buy a domain with Naive credits

First call `POST /v1/domains/quote` with `{ "name": "example.com" }` using `billing:read`.
It returns authoritative availability plus `registration_price_micro_usd` and
`renewal_price_micro_usd`. Quoting does not reserve the domain or move credits.

Then call `POST /v1/domains/purchase` using `billing:write`, an `Idempotency-Key`, and:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "name": "example.com", "max_price_micro_usd": 12000000, "receive": true }
```

The API rechecks availability and price, refuses premium domains, and will not buy if the live
price exceeds the explicit ceiling. It debits the organization's Naive-credit balance before the
registrar call. The platform registrar account funds the external purchase; this endpoint neither
accepts nor forwards a customer card. Automatic renewal is off.

A completed registration returns `201`. A registration still processing returns `202` with
`Cache-Control: no-store`; retry the same request with the same idempotency key to reconcile it.
You do not have to: the platform checks every pending purchase about every 10 minutes and finishes
it. A confirmed registrar rejection refunds the debit. An ambiguous outcome stays pending, because
completed registrations are non-refundable and an eager refund could give away a domain. If no
registration exists a day later, the debit is refunded.

A refused or refunded attempt never blocks the next one. Top up after a `402` and buy again. Delete
a failed purchase and buy again with a new `Idempotency-Key`; the new attempt is charged on its own.
An `Idempotency-Key` names one attempt: reusing the key of a refunded attempt is refused, and can
never register a free domain.

**Errors** — `insufficient_credits` (402); `validation_failed` (400) for an unavailable domain
(including one another organization is buying), missing idempotency key, or a price above the
ceiling; `state_conflict` (409) when the registrar rejected the purchase (credits refunded), when a
failed purchase of the name must be deleted first, when the `Idempotency-Key` belongs to a finished
attempt, or when another request for the name is still
starting (retry shortly); `feature_not_configured` (501) when the platform registrar account is not
configured.

## List domains

`GET /v1/domains` — scope `agents:read`

**limit** `integer`

Page size. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

**after** `string`

Cursor from the previous page.

Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of domain objects.

## Retrieve a domain

`GET /v1/domains/{id}` — scope `agents:read`

Returns the domain object. `not_found` (404) if the id does not belong to your organization.

## Verify a domain

`POST /v1/domains/{id}/verify` — scope `agents:write`

Re-runnable. Each readiness track advances on its own, so calling `verify` after publishing only the SPF/DKIM records moves `dns_status` and leaves `inbound_status` where it was. The **domain object** comes back as the answer — read the three status fields to see what changed.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X POST https://api.vetta.sh/v1/domains/dom_01H9DM.../verify \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

**Errors** — `not_found` (404); `forbidden` (403). A track that is still unpublished is not an error: it simply stays `pending`.

## List DNS records

`GET /v1/domains/{id}/records` — scope `agents:read`

Always allowed on every `kind` — reading the zone is never the dangerous half.

**type** `string`

`TXT`, `CNAME`, or `MX`.

**host** `string`

The record host, relative to the registrable zone.

**value** `string`

The record value.

**priority** `integer | null`

MX priority; `null` for `TXT` and `CNAME`.

**managed** `boolean`

`true` for records the platform owns — DKIM, `_dmarc`, and the inbound MX. An agent may read a managed record and must never edit or delete it: removing the DKIM record breaks the signature on its own mail.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "type": "MX",    "host": "@",                "value": "inbound.vetta.sh", "priority": 10,   "managed": true },
    { "type": "TXT",   "host": "_dmarc",           "value": "v=DMARC1; p=none", "priority": null, "managed": true },
    { "type": "CNAME", "host": "sel._domainkey",   "value": "sel.dkim...",      "priority": null, "managed": true }
  ]
}
```

## Delete a domain

`DELETE /v1/domains/{id}` — scope `agents:write`

Returns the standard deleted envelope. Inboxes on the domain stop delivering; released addresses are not reusable until the domain is reconnected and re-verified.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "dom_01H9DM...", "object": "domain", "deleted": true }
```

> [card] [Email & SMS](/docs/api/messaging)
>
> Give a persona an inbox on this domain.


# Errors
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/errors

The typed error envelope and every error code.

The API uses conventional HTTP status codes and returns **exactly one JSON error envelope** on every failure. Inspect `error.code` for programmatic handling; `error.message` is human-readable and may change.

## Error envelope

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request",
    "code": "window_unavailable",
    "message": "The selected model does not support the 'loose' completion window.",
    "request_id": "req_01H8XK2M...",
    "param": "window"
  }
}
```

**error.type** `string`

Coarse class tied to the HTTP status (see below). The [SDK](/docs/sdk/errors) throws one `ApiError` carrying `type`, `code` and `status`.

**error.code** `string`

Stable, machine-branchable string. **Switch on this** — it is the one taxonomy that never changes meaning.

**error.message** `string`

Human-readable explanation. Do not parse.

**error.request\_id** `string`

The id of the failing request (matches the `x-request-id` response header). Quote it in support requests.

**error.param** `string | null`

The request field that caused the error, when the failure is attributable to one.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `request_id` is returned on **every** response — success and error — via the `x-request-id` header. On errors it is also mirrored inside the envelope. See the [overview](/docs/api/overview#request-ids).

## Types

`type` is the coarse class and maps onto the HTTP status. The [SDK](/docs/sdk/errors) does not subclass on it: it throws one `ApiError` carrying `type`, `code` and `status`.

| Type | HTTP |
| - | - |
| `invalid_request` | 400, or 405 for `method_not_allowed` |
| `authentication` | 401 |
| `quota` | 402 |
| `permission` | 403 |
| `not_found` | 404 |
| `conflict` | 409 |
| `rate_limit` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500, or 502 when the failure was an upstream's |
| `not_implemented` | 501 |

## Codes

`code` is the stable, machine-branchable string. Branch on it; it never changes meaning across versions.

| Code | Type | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - | - |
| `validation_failed` | `invalid_request` | 400 | The request was malformed or failed validation. |
| `window_unavailable` | `invalid_request` | 400 | The model does not support the requested [completion window](/docs/concepts/completion-window). |
| `unauthorized` | `authentication` | 401 | Missing or invalid API key. |
| `budget_exceeded` | `quota` | 402 | The call would breach an agent/session/org [budget](/docs/api/credits). |
| `insufficient_credits` | `quota` | 402 | The org's [credit balance](/docs/api/credits) is too low to cover the call. |
| `subscription_required` | `quota` | 402 | The org holds no active [plan](/docs/api/credits). Start or renew it with `POST /v1/credits/subscription`. |
| `forbidden` | `permission` | 403 | The key or member lacks the required scope/role, or a [permission policy](/docs/api/agents) denied the action. |
| `not_found` | `not_found` | 404 | The resource does not exist in this organization. |
| `method_not_allowed` | `invalid_request` | 405 | The path exists but does not serve this method. The `Allow` header lists the methods it does. |
| `version_conflict` | `conflict` | 409 | Optimistic-concurrency mismatch on an [agent update](/docs/api/agents): the `expected_version` is stale. Also a [database migration](/docs/api/database) re-applied under an existing name with different SQL. |
| `ambiguous_app` | `conflict` | 409 | A [database](/docs/api/database) or [storage](/docs/api/storage) call named no app and the organization holds several `fullstack` apps; the message lists the candidate ids — pass `app`. |
| `revision_conflict` | `conflict` | 409 | A shared declaration moved underneath an [apply](/docs/api/apps#apply): the install's `revision` is not the `expected_revision` you sent. The message names the paths that drifted. |
| `name_conflict` | `conflict` | 409 | The name is held by a resource another `project` owns, and the request did not ask to `adopt` it (see [Apps](/docs/api/apps)), or another live agent or identity already has it. |
| `idempotency_conflict` | `conflict` | 409 | An `Idempotency-Key` was reused with a different body or endpoint, or its first request is still in flight. See the [overview](/docs/api/overview#idempotency). |
| `state_conflict` | `conflict` | 409 | A lifecycle action the object's current status does not admit — forming a company on an unverified [verification](/docs/api/legal), writing to a frozen [wallet](/docs/api/wallet), cancelling a [card](/docs/api/cards) that is not active. Read the status and act on what it says. |
| `session_running` | `conflict` | 409 | Input was sent to a running [session](/docs/api/sessions) without `interrupt`. |
| `session_terminal` | `conflict` | 409 | The [session](/docs/api/sessions) has already ended and cannot accept input. |
| `computer_unavailable` | `conflict` | 409 | The requested [computer](/docs/api/computers) is not ready or has failed. |
| `job_not_ready` | `conflict` | 409 | Nothing is wrong — the work is not ready yet. Retry. |
| `compliance_pending` | `conflict` | 409 | The action waits on a verification or carrier approval that has not cleared. Retry later. |
| `context_locked` | `conflict` | 409 | A saved [browser login](/docs/api/browser#save-a-login) is held for a person's sign-in (`human_login`) for up to 15 minutes; saving it releases the lock. Retry after `locked_until`. |
| `rate_limited` | `rate_limit` | 429 | Too many requests; back off and retry after `Retry-After`. |
| `provider_error` | `api_error` | 502 | An upstream capability the call depended on (a [browser](/docs/api/browser) `act`, a generation model, the [audio](/docs/api/audio) provider, a stock library, or a step of an asynchronous job such as a [clip](/docs/api/clips)) failed or reported that nothing happened. Nothing was billed; retry with backoff (the same `Idempotency-Key` is safe), or fall back to a deterministic action. |
| `internal_error` | `api_error` | 500 | Something failed on our side. Retry with backoff; the `request_id` is what to quote. |
| `feature_not_configured` | `not_implemented` | 501 | The feature is recognized but not configured for this organization. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `version_conflict` **is** a returned error: agent updates use optimistic concurrency, so a stale `expected_version` fails with `409`. Refetch `current_version` and re-apply your change.

### The four `409`s are four different remedies

A `409` is not one thing, and the code is what tells you which. `version_conflict` means one versioned object is stale — re-read it and re-apply. `revision_conflict` means a whole shared declaration moved — merge, using the paths the message names. `name_conflict` means somebody else owns the name — pick another or `adopt`. `job_not_ready` and `compliance_pending` mean nothing is wrong at all — **retry**, and a client that treats them as terminal gives up on work that was going to succeed.

### A `403` that is not JSON

Every error the API itself returns is the JSON envelope above. A `403` whose body is an HTML page never reached the API: the network edge in front of it blocked the request, most often because a request body looks like SQL (a search for `'; drop table`, say). The SDK and CLI report it as `forbidden` with the message "the request was blocked before it reached the API (HTTP 403); this can happen when a request body looks like SQL". It has no `request_id`. Nothing ran and nothing was billed. Rephrase the body and retry; if a legitimate request keeps being blocked, contact support with the time of the request.

## Handling errors

Retry `429` and transient `5xx` responses with exponential backoff, honoring `Retry-After` on `429`. Treat `400`, `401`, `402`, `403`, and `404` as terminal — fix the request or credentials rather than retrying. **Branch a `409` on its `code`, never on the status** — two of them are retryable and the rest are not.

```typescript theme={"system"}
const res = await fetch(url, options);
if (!res.ok) {
  const { error } = await res.json();
  switch (error.code) {
    case "version_conflict": // refetch current_version and retry
    case "revision_conflict": // the declaration moved: merge on error.message's paths, re-apply
    case "name_conflict":    // another project owns the name: rename, or re-send with adopt
    case "job_not_ready":    // not an error — back off and retry
    case "compliance_pending": // not an error — retry once verification clears
    case "rate_limited":     // back off and honor Retry-After
    case "subscription_required": // send the customer to POST /v1/credits/subscription
    case "insufficient_credits": // top up credits, then retry
    case "budget_exceeded":  // raise the cap or top up credits
    default:                 // surface error.message + error.request_id
  }
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Every mutation accepts an `Idempotency-Key`, so retrying a request that failed with a network error or `429` will not double-apply. See the [overview](/docs/api/overview#idempotency).


# Events
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/events

List and stream a session's events, resumable by sequence.

Every [session](/docs/api/sessions) emits an ordered stream of **events**, each with a monotonically increasing `seq`. You can list past events or subscribe to a live Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream. Both are **resumable**: pass the last `seq` you handled to continue with no gaps or duplicates.

Event types use a `{domain}.{action}` naming scheme. For the full catalog across all phases, see [Events & streaming](/docs/concepts/events-and-streaming).

## The event object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `evt_01H...`).

**seq** `integer`

Monotonic sequence number within the session — starts at 1, gap-free on the log and the stream. The [list](#list-events) leaves out the opt-in types unless you pass `include_accepted=true`, so without it the `seq`s it returns can skip (seq 1, the first `message.accepted`, among them). Use it to resume. Mirrored as `last_seq` on the session and as the SSE `id:`.

**type** `string`

The `{domain}.{action}` type — see [below](#event-types).

**session\_id** `string`

The session that emitted the event.

**data** `object`

Type-specific payload.

**created\_at** `string`

When the event happened. Order events by `seq`, not by this: a message sent while a turn is running is logged the moment it arrives, and the turn's own events are logged when the turn ends, so a few events can carry a `created_at` earlier than one with a lower `seq`.

## Event types

| Type | Data | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `message.delta` | `content` | A chunk of the agent's text. |
| `message.completed` | `content`, `role?`, `client_message_id?`, `from?` | A message finished. The agent's reply has no `role: "user"`; a message you sent is recorded the same way with `role: "user"` (and its `client_message_id`), and one with `from: "platform"` is a platform notice. |
| `tool.started` | `tool_call_id`, `name`, `args` | A tool call began. |
| `tool.completed` | `tool_call_id`, `name`, `output`, `is_error` | A tool call finished. `output` is the tool's text result; `is_error` is `true` when the call failed. |
| `tool.confirm` | `tool_call_id`, `name`, `args` | A tool requires approval (`ask` [permission](/docs/api/agents)). Answer via [tool confirmations](/docs/api/sessions#respond-to-a-tool-confirmation). |
| `tool.confirm.resolved` | `tool_call_id`, `decision`, `reason`, `scope`, `actor`, `decided_at`, `proposed_args`, `final_args` | A person answered a `tool.confirm`. `decision` (`allow`/`deny`), `reason` and `scope` are what was sent to [tool confirmations](/docs/api/sessions#respond-to-a-tool-confirmation); `actor` is the user or key that sent it; `proposed_args` are the arguments the card showed; `final_args` are the ones that run — the same, unless the person edited a template install's `answers` as they approved it. For a team member's call it is on the member's session. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. |
| `tool.confirm.answered` | `tool_call_id`, `answers`, `answered_at` | A person answered a question the agent parked (`awaiting_answer`). `answers` are exactly what was sent to [answer a question](/docs/api/sessions#answer-a-question), keyed by field. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`; the live stream sends it either way. Never sent to [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks). |
| `session.mode` | `mode` | The session changed [mode](/docs/concepts/session-operations#plan-mode): `plan` or `build`, from a send or from the approval of its plan. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. |
| `plan.updated` | `object`, `markdown`, `version`, `by` | The session's plan was written — by the agent (`by: "agent"`) or through [`PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/plan`](/docs/api/sessions#edit-the-plan) (`by: "owner"`). The data is the plan. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. |
| `outcome.evaluation.started` · `outcome.evaluation.progress` · `outcome.evaluation.completed` | `outcome_id`, `iteration`, `thread_id`; `completed` adds `result`, `explanation`, `criteria`, `token_usage`, `consumed_micro_usd` | A session held to an outcome is being graded: a grader thread started, began working, and wrote its result (`satisfied`, `needs_revision`, `failed`, `max_iterations_reached`, `interrupted`). `thread_id` is `null` on an `interrupted` no grader wrote. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. Never sent to [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks). |
| `session.running` | — | The agent started a turn. |
| `message.accepted` | `client_message_id`, `content` | A message you sent was accepted into the session's inbox and is not yet answered. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. |
| `handoff.sent` | `client_message_id`, `content`, `handoffs`, `refusals` | A person's fan-out, recorded on the sender's log without waking it: `handoffs` are `{ agent_id, session_id, status }`, `refusals` are `{ agent, code, message }`. Listed only with `include_accepted=true`. |
| `session.retrying` | `attempt`, `in_ms`, `code` | A turn failed and will be retried: `attempt` is the 1-based number of the attempt that failed, `in_ms` the wait before the next, `code` its [error code](/docs/api/errors). The session stays `running`; the next attempt sends its own `session.running`. Treat a `tool.started` the failed attempt left open as failed. |
| `session.degraded` | `reason`, `detail?` | The turn ran without something it needed, one row per missing thing. `reason` is open; today it is `sandbox_unavailable` or `vendor_resume_unavailable` (the turn's [computer](/docs/api/computers) could not be woken), `app_tools_unavailable`, or `mcp_server_unavailable`. `detail` is prose: never parse it. Not a failure and not a status. |
| `session.computer_replaced` | `reason`, `from`, … | The session moved to a fresh computer. `reason: "expired"` (the machine was lost and rebuilt from its newest archive) carries `from` and `to`; `resume_refused` or `vendor_resume_unavailable` (the old one would not wake) carries `from`, `failures` and `replacements`, and the next turn starts on a new computer. Files changed since the newest archive are gone; `from` stays readable through [Computers](/docs/api/computers) while it lives. |
| `session.usage` | `token_usage`, `consumed_micro_usd`, `active_seconds`, `tool_calls` | Cumulative usage snapshot, emitted before every idle/terminal transition. `consumed_micro_usd` is the session's running total — the same figure as the session object's — not a per-turn delta. |
| `session.idle` | `stop_reason`, `pending_actions?`, `structured_output`, `error?`, `code?`, `background?` | A turn yielded control. Read `stop_reason` (see [session lifecycle](/docs/api/sessions#lifecycle)). `structured_output` is `null` unless an [output schema](/docs/capabilities/structured-outputs) was satisfied; `error` appears only when a required schema was not. `code` appears only when the session stopped on failure: the [error code](/docs/api/errors) of its last attempt. `background` is `[{ job_id, kind }]`: every job the session started and has not finished — a video, a 3D model, a clip, an edit or a skill build, `kind` as on `media.job.*` — `[]` when none. A turn's idle always carries it; an idle with no turn (a wake while waiting on you) leaves it out, and the last one that has it still stands. It is on the [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) and `on_idle` envelopes too. |
| `budget.exceeded` | `message`, `code`, `param?` | A call was refused because it would breach a cap or the balance. `code` is `budget_exceeded` or `insufficient_credits`; `param` names the cap that had no room (`budget_micro_usd`, `budget.cap_micro_usd` or `budget.max_task_micro_usd`) and is absent for `insufficient_credits`. `message` is prose. |
| `media.job.queued` | `job_id`, `kind`, `model` | A media job was submitted — by an agent's `generate_video` or `generate_3d_model` ([video](/docs/api/video)), its `clip_video`, `edit_video` or `build_media_skill`, or by `POST /v1/media/clips` ([clips](/docs/api/clips)). `kind` is `video` (an edit too), `mesh`, `clip`, or `skill_build`; `model` is `null` for a clip, an edit and a build. `job_id` is its `med_` (`clj_` for an agent's clip, `ctp_` for a build). On a session's stream it comes at the job's first check, just after the turn that started it. A REST submit has no session, so it reaches [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) only. |
| `media.job.completed` | `job_id`, `kind`, `file_ids`, `cost_micro_usd?` | The job's files are in [Files](/docs/api/files); the session has been woken with the first id and told the settled cost. A skill build makes a skill, not files: its `file_ids` is `[]` and it has no `cost_micro_usd` (it is billed outside the session). |
| `media.job.failed` | `job_id`, `kind`, `code` | The job produced nothing and billed nothing; `code` is an [error code](/docs/api/errors). A skill build the session stopped watching (it may still finish) says neither. |
| `file.imported` | `file_id`, `url` | A [URL import](/docs/api/files#import-a-file-from-a-url) landed in [Files](/docs/api/files). A REST import has no session, so this reaches [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) only. |
| `app.db.migrated` | `app_id`, `migration_id`, `name` | A [migration](/docs/api/database#apply-a-migration) was applied to an app's database for the first time; a replay emits nothing. No session is involved, so this reaches [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) only. |
| `app.storage.bucket.created` | `app_id`, `bucket` | A [bucket](/docs/api/storage#buckets) was created on an app's object store. Webhooks only, like `app.db.migrated`; object reads and writes are [audit](/docs/api/audit-logs) rows, not events. |
| `app.storage.bucket.deleted` | `app_id`, `bucket` | A bucket was deleted (`?force=true` empties it first). Webhooks only. |
| `browser.session.opened` | `browser_session_id`, `computer_id`, `region` | The agent's `browser` tool opened its [browser](/docs/api/browser) on the session's computer — lazily, on the first action. A REST open has no session and is audit-logged instead. |
| `browser.session.closed` | `browser_session_id`, `minutes` | The browser closed and its minutes were settled on the `browser` line; the tool's browser closes when the session ends or pauses for input. |
| `browser.context.saved` | `context_id`, `identity_id` | The `save_context` action marked a [saved login](/docs/api/browser#save-a-login) saved from the browser opened with it; the close persists the storage. |
| `browser.context.granted` | `grant_id`, `context_id`, `grantee_type`, `grantee_id` | A saved login was shared with an agent or role over REST. No session, so [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) only. |
| `browser.context.revoked` | `context_id` | A saved login was deleted over REST, and every grant on it with it. Webhooks only. |
| `wallet.created` | `wallet_id`, `identity_id`, `network`, `address` | A [wallet](/docs/api/wallet) was provisioned for an identity on that network. Operator action over REST, so [webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks) only. |
| `wallet.policy.updated` | `wallet_id`, `identity_id`, `policy` | The per-tx or daily cap changed; the new policy is at the provider already. Webhooks only. |
| `wallet.transaction.confirmed` | `wallet_id`, `identity_id`, `transaction_id`, `kind`, `amount_micro_usd`, `counterparty`, `tx_hash`, `status` | A `fund`, `transfer` or `pay` settled on chain. A `pending` or `failed` transaction emits nothing. Never carries a key, a signature or a payment header. |
| `wallet.swept` | `wallet_id`, `identity_id`, `transaction_id`, `amount_micro_usd`, `counterparty`, `tx_hash`, `status` | The whole balance was drained and the wallet retired. Webhooks only. |
| `card.issued` | `card_id`, `identity_id`, `status`, `load_micro_usd`, `brand`, `last4` | A prepaid [card](/docs/api/cards) became `active` — on the buy, on a `retry`, or on the reconcile a read does. Never carries a credential. |
| `card.failed` | `card_id`, `identity_id`, `status`, `load_micro_usd`, `reason` | The issuer could not complete the order. The debit stays on the row so `retry` re-runs issuance; `refund` returns the credits. |
| `card.cancelled` | `card_id`, `identity_id`, `status`, `load_micro_usd` | A card was marked cancelled. Local status only — a prepaid card cannot be voided at the issuer. |
| `card.refunded` | `card_id`, `identity_id`, `status`, `load_micro_usd`, `price_micro_usd` | The credits for a `pending_payment` or `failed` card went back to the balance. |
| `card.credentials_revealed` | `card_id`, `identity_id`, `status`, `load_micro_usd` | Someone read the card's number/PIN. The event names the card, never the credential; the [audit](/docs/api/audit-logs) row names the caller. |
| `thread.created` · `thread.idle` · `thread.terminated` | `thread_id`, … | A [team](/docs/team/delegation) coordinator's view of a delegated member session: spawned, result folded back, or failed to start. Payloads are on [Context and budgets](/docs/team/context-and-budgets). `thread.running` is in the enum but nothing emits it today. |
| `span.model_request.start` · `span.model_request.end` | `.end`: `model`, `window`, `token_usage`, `stop_reason`, `resolved_model`, `provider_ms`, `consumed_micro_usd` | Bracket each model call. `.end` carries the call's usage and price; `resolved_model` is the model that answered when `model` is a router. A call that produced nothing has no `.end`. |
| `span.transcript_load.*` · `span.harness_load.*` · `span.harness_build.*` · `span.box_resume.*` | — | `.start` / `.end` pairs with empty data timing what a turn did before its first model call: reading the transcript, loading and building the agent, and waking the computer. Sort them by `created_at`, not `seq`. |

The `session.idle` `stop_reason` is one of `end_turn`, `awaiting_input`, `awaiting_approval`, `awaiting_answer`, `awaiting_delegation`, `budget_paused`, `interrupted`, `max_iterations`, `context_exhausted`, or `error` — the same enum as the [session object](/docs/api/sessions#lifecycle), which is where each one is explained.

Three of them park the turn on something outside the loop, and only two of those park it on a *person*: `awaiting_approval` and `awaiting_answer` both carry `pending_actions` and both wait for a reply, while `awaiting_delegation` waits for the coordinator's own children and no reply will move it.

## List events

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` → `200 OK`. Past events in `seq` order (the log's order; see `created_at` above). Resume by passing `after_seq`; combine with `limit` for paging. Events are replayable for at least 72 hours.

**after\_seq** `integer`

Return events with `seq`**strictly greater** than this. Omit to start from the beginning.

**limit** `integer`

Max log rows the page reads. Default `20`, max `100`. Rows that `include_accepted` leaves out count toward it, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` events (even none) with `has_more: true`. Keep reading from `next_cursor` until `has_more` is `false`.

**include\_accepted** `boolean`

Include the types this release added — `message.accepted` (a message the session has accepted and not yet answered), `handoff.sent` (a person's fan-out, recorded on the sender's log), `tool.confirm.resolved` (a person's decision on a held tool call), `tool.confirm.answered` (a person's answers to a parked question), `session.mode`, `plan.updated`, and an outcome's grade — `outcome.evaluation.started`, `outcome.evaluation.progress` and `outcome.evaluation.completed`. Off by default, so clients published before those types existed keep reading the page; the live stream sends them either way. It changes only which rows are in `data`: `has_more` and `next_cursor` are the page's own, so nothing is skipped by leaving it off.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../events?after_seq=140&limit=50" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "evt_01H9II...", "seq": 141, "type": "session.running", "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "data": {}, "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:01Z" },
    { "id": "evt_01H9IJ...", "seq": 142, "type": "message.delta", "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "data": { "content": "Looking up order #4821…" }, "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:01Z" },
    { "id": "evt_01H9IK...", "seq": 143, "type": "session.idle", "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "data": { "stop_reason": "end_turn" }, "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:04Z" }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Stream events (SSE)

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/stream?after_seq={seq}` opens a Server-Sent Events stream. Each SSE message carries one event as JSON in its `data:` field, with the event `seq` as the SSE `id:`. On reconnect, pass the last `seq` you saw as `after_seq` to replay everything since.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -N "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../stream?after_seq=140" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "accept: text/event-stream"
```

```text Stream theme={"system"}
id: 141
data: {"seq":141,"type":"session.running","data":{}}

id: 142
data: {"seq":142,"type":"message.delta","data":{"content":"Looking up order #4821…"}}

id: 143
data: {"seq":143,"type":"session.idle","data":{"stop_reason":"end_turn"}}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Track the highest `seq` you have fully processed. After any disconnect, reconnect with `?after_seq=<that seq>` — the stream is gap-free and duplicate-free from that point.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `tool.confirm` pauses the turn (`stop_reason: "awaiting_approval"`) until you resolve it via [`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool_confirmations`](/docs/api/sessions#respond-to-a-tool-confirmation). `budget.exceeded` accompanies a `session.idle` with `stop_reason` `budget_paused`.
>
> **A question emits no event of its own.** An agent that calls `ask_operator` parks the same way, and the only signal on the stream is the `session.idle` — `stop_reason: "awaiting_answer"`, with the question in `pending_actions`. Answer it via [`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/answers`](/docs/api/sessions#answer-a-question). A stream reader that branches only on `tool.confirm` will sit on a session that is waiting for it.


# Files
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/files

Naive Managed Agents object storage for uploads, imports and published artifacts — the asset library.

**Files** is Naive Managed Agents' object storage and its media asset library. Use it to upload inputs an [agent](/docs/api/agents) can read, to hold artifacts an agent publishes, and to find them again by `kind`, `tag` or a word from the title. Files are either **session-scoped** (temporary, tied to a [session](/docs/api/sessions)) or **published/persistent** (retained at the organization level).

## The file object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `fil_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `file`.

**name** `string`

File name.

**content\_type** `string`

MIME type.

**size\_bytes** `integer`

Size in bytes.

**scope** `string`

`session` (temporary) or `published` (persistent).

**session\_id** `string | null`

Owning session, for session-scoped files.

**sha256** `string`

Content hash.

**created\_at** `string`

Upload timestamp.

**kind** `string`

Derived from `content_type`: `image`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `model` (3D) or `other`.

**title** `string | null`

A human title, editable.

**description** `string | null`

Free text, editable and searchable.

**tags** `string[]`

Labels to filter by; up to 32, each up to 64 characters.

**folder** `string | null`

The [folder](#folders) the file is in, or `null`.

**source** `object | null`

Where the bytes came from: `{ type, job_id, url }`. `type` is `upload`, `url_import`, `image_generation`, `video_generation`, `video_clipping`, `screenshot`, `speech_generation`, `mesh_generation` (a generated 3D model) or `model_build` (a file `build-3d` published); `job_id` names the `med_`/`clj_` job that produced it, `url` the address an import fetched. A generated picture or clip also carries `model` and `prompt`: what it was made with. An edited clip also carries `from_file_id`: the library clip it was made from, when it was made from one. `null` for files written before provenance was recorded.

**agent\_id** `string | null`

The agent whose session made the file. `null` for an upload, an import, or a render asked for over the API.

**width** `integer | null`

Pixel width, read from the bytes of a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or MP4 at write time.

**height** `integer | null`

Pixel height, likewise.

**duration\_seconds** `number | null`

Length of an audio or video file: as its producer reported it (for [generated speech](/docs/api/audio)), or read from an MP4's own header at write time. `null` otherwise.

**thumbnail\_file\_id** `string | null`

Reserved for a preview image; always `null` today.

## Session-scoped vs published

| Scope | Lifetime | Created by |
| - | - | - |
| `session` | Tied to the session. Sessions are never deleted, so it stays until you delete it. | Uploads to a session, scratch work. |
| `published` | Persistent, org-level. | An upload with `scope: published`, a [URL import](#import-a-file-from-a-url), [publishing](#publish-a-file) a session file, or an agent's `publish_file` tool — which writes a **published** file directly, with the `session_id` kept as provenance, so it outlives the session. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> Anything an agent should keep beyond a run is a **published** file. Scratch work stays session-scoped. Promotion emits no [event](/docs/api/events); an import emits `file.imported`.

## Getting bytes out of a session

Files travel **outward** by default: an agent writes an artifact with the built-in `publish_file` tool and you read it back through this API. There is no create-time mount — a session takes no `files[]`. Inward, the agent asks: the built-in [`fetch_file`](/docs/capabilities/tools#reading-a-file-back-into-the-sandbox) tool takes up to eight `fil_` ids the organization holds and writes those files into the session's sandbox, which is how an agent post-processes an asset the platform rendered for it. The sandbox file tools themselves still address the sandbox filesystem and not file ids — there is no `read_file` — and `find_files` still returns ids and metadata, never bytes. To put an input in front of an agent, name its `fil_` id in the session's first `message` and let it fetch the bytes, or put the content in the message itself.

Each `publish_file` call mints a **new** file id, including for a name that already exists: nothing is superseded and both remain listed. Pick the one you want by `created_at`, or give it a `title` and `tags` and find it by those.

## Upload a file

`POST /v1/files` → `201 Created`. Accepts a multipart upload. The `file` part carries the bytes; other parts set metadata.

**file** `file` *required*

The file contents (multipart).

**scope** `string`

`session` or `published`. Defaults to `published`.

**session\_id** `string`

Required when `scope` is `session`.

**name** `string`

Override the file name.

**title** `string`

A human title for the library.

**description** `string`

A longer description, searchable.

**tags** `string`

Comma-separated labels, e.g. `launch,web`.

**folder** `string`

Put the file in this [folder](#folders).

The body is capped at **25 MiB**. The stored `kind` is derived from the content type, and an image's `width`/`height` are read from its bytes. `source` is `{ "type": "upload" }`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -F "file=@invoice.pdf" \
  -F "scope=published"
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "fil_01H9CD...",
  "object": "file",
  "name": "invoice.pdf",
  "content_type": "application/pdf",
  "size_bytes": 20481,
  "scope": "published",
  "session_id": null,
  "sha256": "e3b0c442...",
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:20:00Z",
  "kind": "document",
  "title": null,
  "description": null,
  "tags": [],
  "source": { "type": "upload", "job_id": null, "url": null },
  "width": null,
  "height": null,
  "duration_seconds": null,
  "thumbnail_file_id": null
}
```

## Upload up to 60 MiB with a link

`POST /v1/files/uploads` → `201 Created`. Scope `files:write`. Mints a one-shot link; the bytes go to it in a second request that needs no key, so a browser can send them straight from the page.

**name** `string` *required*

The file name.

**content\_type** `string` *required*

A MIME type, e.g. `video/mp4`. The PUT must send the same.

**size\_bytes** `integer` *required*

The exact size, at most **60 MiB**.

**folder** `string`

Put the file in this [folder](#folders) when it lands.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "file_upload",
  "file_id": "fil_01H9CF...",
  "upload_url": "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/uploads/eyJv...",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-13T12:15:00Z"
}
```

`PUT /v1/files/uploads/{token}` → `201 Created`, with the [file object](#the-file-object). No key: the token is the proof. Send the bytes as the body within 15 minutes, with the declared `Content-Type` and a `Content-Length` of exactly `size_bytes`; anything else is `validation_failed`. The link works once. A used, expired or altered link is `forbidden`. The file is `published`, with `source.type: "upload"`. The route answers CORS, so any page may call it.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PUT "$UPLOAD_URL" -H "content-type: video/mp4" --data-binary @clip.mp4
```

The mint is audit-logged as `file.created`.

## Import a file from a URL

`POST /v1/files/imports` → `201 Created`. Scope `files:write`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key replays the same file instead of fetching twice.

The API fetches the URL **server-side** and stores the bytes as a `published` file with `source.type: "url_import"` and `source.url` set to the address you gave. The stored `content_type` is what the bytes say (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, MP4, WebM, MP3, WAV, Ogg, PDF are recognised by signature), falling back to what the server declared.

**url** `string` *required*

A public `http(s)` URL.

**name** `string`

The stored file's name, up to 500 characters. Omitted, the URL's last path segment. A [stock photo](/docs/api/images) carries a neutral `file_name` to pass here.

**title** `string`

A human title for the library.

**description** `string`

A longer description, searchable.

**tags** `string[]`

Labels to filter by.

**folder** `string`

Put the file in this [folder](#folders).

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/imports \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "url": "https://cdn.example.com/hero.png", "title": "Launch hero", "tags": ["launch"] }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "fil_01H9CE...",
  "object": "file",
  "name": "hero.png",
  "content_type": "image/png",
  "kind": "image",
  "width": 1600,
  "height": 900,
  "title": "Launch hero",
  "tags": ["launch"],
  "scope": "published",
  "source": { "type": "url_import", "job_id": null, "url": "https://cdn.example.com/hero.png" }
}
```

**Limits.** Only `http` and `https`; no credentials in the URL; the host must be public — loopback, private-network, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused, and every redirect is checked the same way before it is followed (three at most). The body is capped at **25 MiB**, the same as an upload; a larger declared or actual body fails the import. All of these, and an upstream error status, are `validation_failed` (400) on `url`.

The import is audit-logged and emits a `file.imported { file_id, url }` [event](/docs/api/events) to webhooks subscribed to it.

## Update a file's metadata

`PATCH /v1/files/{id}` → `200 OK` with the updated file. Scope `files:write`. Only the library metadata changes; the bytes, name, scope and provenance do not.

**title** `string | null`

Set or clear (`null`) the title.

**description** `string | null`

Set or clear the description.

**tags** `string[]`

Replace the tags; `[]` clears them.

**folder** `string | null`

Move the file to this [folder](#folders); `null` takes it out.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/fil_01H9CE... \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "title": "Launch hero (final)", "tags": ["launch", "approved"] }'
```

Any other field in the body is `validation_failed` (400).

## Retrieve a file

`GET /v1/files/{id}` → `200 OK` with file metadata. Append `?download=true` to receive the raw bytes instead of JSON.

The bytes carry an `ETag` (the file's `sha256`) and honour `Range`, `If-Range` and `If-None-Match`; a copy you already hold is answered `304 Not Modified`. A generated image or video is sent `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`, every other file `private, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/fil_01H9CD... \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "fil_01H9CD...", "name": "invoice.pdf", "scope": "published", "size_bytes": 20481 }
```

## A link that needs no key

`POST /v1/files/{id}/url` → `201 Created`. Scope `files:read`.

A file id is not something a person can watch. `?download=true` above wants an `authorization`
header, and an `<img>` or `<video>` tag sends none — so this mints an address that carries its own
proof instead, good for **seven days**.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X POST https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/fil_01H9CD.../url \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "file_url",
  "url": "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/fil_01H9CD.../clip.mp4?org=org_01H9...&expires=1757212800000&sig=...",
  "expires_at": "2026-09-14T04:00:00.000Z"
}
```

`GET /v1/files/{id}/{name}?org=&expires=&sig=` — that URL, with no credential at all — returns the bytes, `inline`, with the content type they
were stored under. The filename is in the path so the address ends in a real extension, which is what
lets a browser tag and a fetch-once publishing provider recognise it before opening it.

The signature covers every other field in the URL, so there is nothing in it you can edit: change the
expiry, the file, the organization or the name and it answers `403`. A generated picture's or clip's
link also carries `in=media`, which is signed too. A forged link and an expired one
answer the same thing. Deleting the file revokes every link ever minted for it.

## List files

`GET /v1/files` → `200 OK`, cursor-paginated, newest first. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination). Filters combine:

| Query | Matches |
| - | - |
| `scope` | `session` or `published`. |
| `session_id` | Files a given session produced. |
| `kind` | `image`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `model` or `other` — or several, comma-separated. |
| `exclude_kind` | None of these kinds, comma-separated. |
| `agent_id` | Files an agent's sessions made. |
| `ids` | Exactly these files: up to 100 `fil_` ids, comma-separated. |
| `source` | A `source.type` — `upload`, `url_import`, `image_generation`, … |
| `tag` | Files carrying exactly this tag. |
| `search` | A case-insensitive substring of the `title`, `name` or `description` — or, for a generated picture or clip, of the prompt it was made from. |
| `order` | `desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc`. |
| `folder` | Files in this [folder](#folders). Case does not matter. |
| `character` | Renders of this [character](/docs/api/characters): a `chr_` id, matched against `source.character_id`. |

Working pictures a skill build cuts from its source videos are left out of every list except an `ids` one. Each is still read by its id.

Everything an agent's pictures and clips need is one call: `?kind=image,video&agent_id=agt_…`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files?kind=image,video&agent_id=agt_01H9CD...&limit=30" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files?kind=image&tag=launch&search=hero" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [ { "id": "fil_01H9CD...", "name": "invoice.pdf", "scope": "published", "size_bytes": 20481 } ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Folders

A folder is a name on a file. A file is in one folder or none, and folders do not nest. A name is 1–64 characters with no `/`. There is no folder object to create: a folder exists while a file is in it.

* **Case.** A name that matches an existing folder in another case takes that folder's spelling. `launch` files into `Launch`.
* **Default.** A file written with no folder lands in the folder of the newest filed file in its session, else in none. So an agent's next render lands beside its last.
* **Once.** The folder is set when a file is written. Writing the same file again never changes it; only a move does.

Grouping by agent, chat, kind or date is a filter on the list, never a folder.

### Move files

`POST /v1/files/move` → `200 OK`. Scope `files:write`. Name `ids` or `from`, not both.

**ids** `string[]`

Up to 100 `fil_` ids to move. An id the organization does not hold is skipped.

**from** `string`

Move every file in this folder: a rename. If `folder` is already in use, the two merge.

**folder** `string | null` *required*

The folder to move to. `null` takes the files out of any folder; with `from`, that empties the folder.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/move \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "from": "launch", "folder": "Launch 2026" }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "object": "file_move", "folder": "Launch 2026", "file_ids": ["fil_01H9CD...", "fil_01H9CE..."] }
```

`folder` is the name the files now carry, in the spelling that won. Only the name on each file changes. No file is deleted and no bytes move.

### List folders

`GET /v1/files/folders` → `200 OK`. Scope `files:read`. Every folder, newest first, in one page.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "file_folder",
      "name": "Launch 2026",
      "file_count": 12,
      "newest_at": "2026-10-20T09:00:00.000Z",
      "cover_file_ids": ["fil_01H9CD...", "fil_01H9CE..."],
      "agent_id": "agt_01H9AB..."
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

`cover_file_ids` holds up to four of the newest pictures and clips in the folder. `agent_id` is set when one agent made every file in it, else `null`. All of it is worked out when you read it. To read a folder's files, list with `?folder=`.

## Publish a file

`POST /v1/files/{id}/publish` → `200 OK`. Scope `files:write`.

The promotion boundary: a `session`-scoped file becomes a durable, org-level `published` one. Use it when work that started as scratch turns out to be the deliverable — it saves re-uploading the bytes.

**Idempotent.** Publishing an already-published file returns it unchanged rather than erroring, so a retry is safe. No request body.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X POST https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/fil_01H9CD.../publish \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "fil_01H9CD...", "object": "file", "name": "invoice.pdf", "scope": "published", "size_bytes": 20481 }
```

The file now outlives its session and is billed as org-level storage. No event is emitted.

**Errors** — `not_found` (404); `forbidden` (403) without `files:write`.

## Delete a file

`DELETE /v1/files/{id}` → `200 OK`. Removes the object.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "fil_01H9CD...", "object": "file", "deleted": true }
```

## Delete many files

`POST /v1/files/delete` → `200 OK`. Scope `files:write`. Deletes up to 100 files in one request, each as `DELETE /v1/files/{id}` would. An id the organization does not hold is skipped. Each delete is filed as `file.deleted` in the audit log.

**ids** `string[]` *required*

1–100 `fil_` ids to delete.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/files/delete \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "ids": ["fil_01H9CD...", "fil_01H9CE..."] }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "object": "file_delete", "file_ids": ["fil_01H9CD...", "fil_01H9CE..."] }
```

`file_ids` lists the files that were deleted.


# Harnesses
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/harnesses

The agent loops an agent can run on — what each one can be admitted for, and what an idle session on it costs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A **harness** is the agent loop itself: how context is managed, how tools are chosen, how a long task is decomposed and resumed. It is one field on an [agent](/docs/api/agents), and nothing else about your call changes when you change it. Unlike [models](/docs/api/models), this catalogue is a constant of the deploy — a harness needs an adapter compiled in — so it does not change without a release.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The loops themselves are described in [Harnesses](/docs/concepts/harnesses) — what each one is, and
> which of them holds a sandbox between turns. This page is the wire contract.

## The harness object

**base** `string`

The value you pass as `harness` on an agent.

**label** `string`

A display name, for a picker.

**location** `string`

`hosted` runs on our infrastructure. `local` runs on your own machine against your own logged-in account, and is not available to a hosted session.

**billing** `string`

`usage` is metered to your credit balance. `account` bills the account you are already signed in to, so it does not touch your balance.

**status** `string`

`ga`, or `preview` when the loop runs but its contract may still move.

**execution** `string`

Where the loop runs, and therefore **what an idle session costs**. `isolate` runs in the session itself and holds no sandbox between turns. `sandbox` runs the agent on a micro-VM, which the session holds across turns. `local` runs on your machine. This is a different question from `location`, which is about who operates it.

**runnable** `boolean`

Whether a session on it runs **on this deploy**. A harness whose agent is a process also needs a base image, which is per-environment — so the same harness can be runnable in one environment and not another, and this field answers for the one you are talking to. A published harness with `false` is refused when the session starts, with `501` naming the field — so a picker can show it disabled rather than let someone discover it by trying.

**capabilities** `object`

What the loop can be admitted for. See below.

## Capabilities

Harnesses differ, and the differences are load-bearing. Read them before you create an agent.

**approvals** `boolean`

The loop can hold a tool call and wait for a decision on [tool confirmations](/docs/api/sessions). A harness with `false` cannot serve a toolset whose permission is `ask`.

**structured\_output** `boolean`

The loop can enforce `structured_output_required`. **`vetta` publishes `true` here and cannot yet produce one** — the loop has no submit path, so the pairing is admitted by every gate and fails at the turn. Use `pi` for a typed answer. See [Known gaps](/docs/concepts/harness-capabilities#known-gaps).

**streaming\_deltas** `boolean`

The loop emits incremental `message.delta`[events](/docs/api/events). With `false` you still get `message.completed` — the answer arrives whole rather than as it is written.

**injected\_tools** `boolean`

The tools **Naive Managed Agents** contributes reach the loop's model — the [team tools](/docs/team/delegation), an agent's [`mcp_servers`](/docs/api/mcp), a [connected account's](/docs/api/connections) tools, social publishing and apps — all governed by the agent's `tools` policy under the same names. It does not say by which road: a loop Managed Agents hosts is handed them for the turn, while an agent that is a CLI process in a machine of its own is given a session-scoped tool endpoint to call and keeps its own file, shell and search tools alongside ours. Three limits apply on the second road: Managed Agents' own built-ins (web search and fetch, media generation, skill disclosure, `publish_file`, the managed browser) do not travel it, and — both following from `approvals: false` on those harnesses — a tool whose permission is `ask` is left out rather than gated, and `wait_for_agents` does not pause the turn (the coordinator parks once it goes idle and still opens its threads). See [Harness capabilities](/docs/concepts/harness-capabilities#platform-injected-tools).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two configurations are refused earlier than the rest, at `POST`/`PATCH``/v1/agents`, because the agent's own configuration settles them: `multiagent` on a harness with `injected_tools: false` (the coordinator would have no `send_to_agent`) and a non-empty `mcp_servers` on the same (nothing would surface them). Both answer `400``validation_failed` naming the field to change. **No published harness declares `false`,** so neither refusal fires today; they stand as the guard for a base added later.

> [!NOTE]
>
> All four are on the object. `injected_tools` is the one that decides whether an agent can lead a [team](/docs/team/overview), because the team tools arrive the same way as [MCP servers](/docs/api/mcp) and [Connections](/docs/api/connections). The per-harness values for all four are in [Harness capabilities](/docs/concepts/harness-capabilities).

> [!NOTE]
>
> A session asking for a capability its harness does not declare is refused **at start** with a `400` naming `harness`. It is never a quiet best effort that looks like it worked — an `ask` toolset that silently became `allow` would remove your human-in-the-loop gate with no event and no error to notice it by.

## GET /v1/harnesses

Every harness, including those in preview and those not yet runnable.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl https://api.vetta.sh/v1/harnesses \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "base": "pi",
      "label": "Pi",
      "location": "hosted",
      "billing": "usage",
      "status": "ga",
      "execution": "sandbox",
      "runnable": true,
      "capabilities": {
        "approvals": true,
        "structured_output": true,
        "streaming_deltas": true,
        "injected_tools": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

The list is a hand-written table and fits one page, so `has_more` is always `false` — but the envelope is the same as every other listing, so one loop reads both this and [models](/docs/api/models).

## GET /v1/harnesses/\{id}

One harness, for when you already hold a base and want to know what it can be admitted for.

A base the catalogue does not publish is `404` — including an id reserved in a picker but not yet runnable as a harness.

## Choosing one

Two questions decide it, and they are separate:

* **What must the loop be able to do?** If your toolset uses `ask`, you need `approvals`. If you require a structured answer, you need `structured_output`. If the agent leads a team, declares MCP servers, or acts through a connected account, you need `injected_tools` — every published harness has it, so in practice this question is about the two limits that come with `approvals: false`.
* **What should an idle session cost?** A harness with `execution: "isolate"` holds no sandbox between turns. One with `"sandbox"` holds a micro-VM, because the agent *is* a process running on it.


# Identities
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/identities

Create and manage the personas an agent acts as — email, phone, web domains, and connections.

> [!NOTE]
>
> An identity is a named persona an agent acts as, governed by the [policy](/docs/concepts/policies) layer.

An identity is a named persona that owns communication endpoints and connections. One agent can hold several identities; one identity can be shared by several agents. See the [Identity](/docs/identity/overview) guide for concepts.

## The identity object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `idn_01H...`).

**name** `string`

Human-readable name.

**description** `string | null`

What this persona is for; helps agents choose between multiple identities.

**emails** `string[]`

Inbox addresses on verified domains.

**phones** `string[]`

Provisioned numbers in E.164.

**domains** `string[]`

Web domains attached to the identity.

**connections** `string[]`

IDs of authorized third-party connections.

**metadata** `object`

Arbitrary key/value pairs.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**updated\_at** `string`

When the persona was last changed.

## Create an identity

`POST /v1/identities`

**name** `string` *required*

Human-readable name.

**description** `string`

What the persona does. Defaults to `null`.

**metadata** `object`

Arbitrary key/value pairs.

`name` is unique among your live identities, ignoring case. A second identity with the same name is refused `409 name_conflict` on `name`; deleting an identity frees its name.

A persona is created empty. Its `emails`, `phones`, `domains` and `connections` are reads of sub-resources minted through their own routes — [inboxes](/docs/api/messaging#create-an-inbox), [numbers](/docs/api/messaging#provision-a-number) and [connections](/docs/api/connections) — and sending either list here is refused with `validation_failed`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/identities \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Acme Billing",
    "description": "Handles invoices and refunds for Acme"
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "idn_01H9AB...",
  "object": "identity",
  "name": "Acme Billing",
  "description": "Handles invoices and refunds for Acme",
  "emails": [],
  "phones": [],
  "domains": [],
  "connections": [],
  "metadata": {},
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

## List, retrieve, delete

```bash theme={"system"}
GET    /v1/identities            # list (cursor-paginated)
GET    /v1/identities/{id}       # retrieve
DELETE /v1/identities/{id}       # delete
```

See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination) and [Errors](/docs/api/errors).

Deleting an identity revokes every grant to it and deletes its email inboxes, so mail to those addresses stops arriving. A persona that still owns phone numbers cannot be deleted: the delete is refused `state_conflict` (409), naming them, until each is released with `DELETE /v1/identities/{id}/phones/{phone_id}`.

## Update an identity

`PATCH /v1/identities/{id}`

**name** `string`

New human-readable name.

**description** `string`

New description. Send `null` to clear it.

**metadata** `object`

Replaces the metadata object wholesale.

All fields are optional; omitted fields are left unchanged. The read-only lists — `emails`, `phones`, `domains`, `connections` — cannot be patched here; manage them through their own routes.

## Binding identities to agents

The grant is a **many-to-many** edge, and it hangs off the **agent** — the question it answers is which personas *that agent* may act as. Four routes, read from either side.

### Attach an identity

`POST /v1/agents/{id}/identities` — scope `agents:write`

**identity** `string` *required*

The `idn_` identity to grant.

Returns the grant, echoed back. It is **idempotent**: attaching a persona that is already attached succeeds with `attached: true` and `created: false`, so a re-run of a provisioning script is safe.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/agents/agt_01H.../identities \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "identity": "idn_01H9AB..." }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "identity_grant",
  "agent_id": "agt_01H...",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H9AB...",
  "attached": true,
  "created": false
}
```

**Errors** — `not_found` (404) for an unknown agent or identity; `forbidden` (403) without `agents:write`.

### Detach an identity

`DELETE /v1/agents/{id}/identities/{identity_id}` — scope `agents:write`

Removes the grant. The identity itself is untouched and stays available to any other agent that holds it. Sessions already running under the persona are not interrupted; the next session cannot select it. Detaching an identity the agent does not hold answers `404 not_found`.

### List an agent's identities

`GET /v1/agents/{id}/identities` — scope `agents:read`. A [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of full identity objects — *which personas may this agent wear.*

### List an identity's agents

`GET /v1/identities/{id}/agents` — scope `agents:read`. A [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of agent references — *who may wear this persona.* The reverse direction of the same edge, and the one to check before deleting an identity.

## Sub-resources

| Resource | Reference |
| - | - |
| Sending and receiving domains | [Domains](/docs/api/domains) |
| Inboxes, numbers, inbound feed | [Email & SMS](/docs/api/messaging) |
| Third-party accounts | [Connections](/docs/api/connections) |
| Social accounts | [Social](/docs/api/social) |
| Write-only credentials | [Vaults](/docs/api/vaults) |

> [card] [Next: vaults](/docs/api/vaults)
>
> Write-only credentials injected at the network boundary.


# Images
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/images

Generate images over REST — one call, and it waits; every rendered image comes back as a file — and search a licensed stock photo library, free.

`POST /v1/media/images` renders synchronously: the reply carries the finished [files](/docs/api/files) and what the render cost. There is no job to poll — an image is done before the request returns, so it is never a [`media_job`](/docs/api/video#the-media-job-object). The same render is what an agent's [`generate_image`](#in-a-session) tool does; the [catalogue](/docs/api/media) is shared. Images are not [model calls](/docs/concepts/model-router): the image catalogue is its own, and an image model is never an agent's `model`.

## The image generation object

**object** `string`

Always `image_generation`.

**model** `string`

The model that rendered, which is the one you named or the default it picked.

**files** `File[]`

One [file](/docs/api/files#the-file-object) per rendered image, `n` of them when the model produced that many. Each is `published` and carries `source.type = image_generation`.

**cost\_micro\_usd** `integer`

What was debited for the render, in integer micro-USD, on the media tier. See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#media-generation--per-finished-job-media-component).

## Generate images
