`POST /v1/media/images` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) **required**.

**prompt** `string` *required*

What to render.

**model** `string`

A model id from [`GET /v1/media/models?kind=image`](/docs/api/media#search-models). Omitted, the platform's default image model is used — the first the catalogue lists that takes what the request carries: with `image_urls`, one whose catalogue entry takes an image input; with `character`, one that pins a character. If that default is unavailable (`403`/`404`, `429` or a `5xx`), the next one is tried, and the reply's `model` says which rendered; a model you name never falls back. A named model whose entry says it takes none of what you sent is `validation_failed` before anything is billed; an id the catalogue does not know is `validation_failed`.

**image\_urls** `string[]`

Up to 4 reference images for an edit (the platform's own edit model takes 3) or an image-to-image render, each a stored image's `fil_` id — an upload, or an earlier render's file — or a public `http(s)` URL. A `fil_` this organization does not hold is `not_found`; one that is not an image, a private or loopback host, and a `data:` or `file:` URL are `validation_failed`.

**character** `string`

Render as a trained [character](/docs/api/characters) — its `chr_` id or name — so the same face carries across every image. It must be `ready`; one still `training` or `failed` is `validation_failed`. With `image_urls`, every one must be a still of that character (a `fil_` rendered with it): the image is then an edit of those stills that keeps their room, props and outfit and changes only the pose and framing, and it counts as a still of the character, so it can open a [character video](/docs/api/characters). Such an edit runs on the platform's set-edit models; naming any other `model` is `validation_failed`. Each edit is checked against the still it came from: if it shows someone else, it is rendered once more, and if the second one is someone else too it is filed (and billed) as a plain image, not as a still of the character.

**style** `string`

Draw the image in a named [look](#looks), by name or slug, such as `Phone snap` or `quiet-luxury`. An unknown look is `validation_failed`, and the message lists them.

**character\_strength** `number`

With `character` only: 0.5 to 1, how strictly the face is held. Leave it out unless a face drifts in a close-up; `0.85` is a good start. Without `character`, or outside 0.5–1, it is `validation_failed`.

**n** `integer`

How many images, 1–4. Default 1. Every one that renders is filed; when some of them fail, the rest are still filed and billed, and only all of them failing is `provider_error`.

**aspect\_ratio** `string`

Such as `16:9` or `1:1`. On a model that publishes the ratios it takes, one it does not is clamped to the nearest it does; a model that takes none ignores it. Anything that is not `W:H` in whole numbers, or is wider than `8:1` or taller than `1:8` (no model takes more), is refused with `validation_failed` on `aspect_ratio` before anything renders or is billed.

**seed** `integer`

Repeat an earlier result, on models that honour a seed.

That is the whole request. Each output is filed in the format the model returned it — PNG unless the model says otherwise — and `content_type` on the file says which. Not on the request today: an explicit `size` or `resolution`, `quality`, `output_format`, a transparent `background`, more than 4 references or outputs, and any per-model or per-provider passthrough. A body that carries one of them is `validation_failed`, not quietly dropped; ask for the field if you need it.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/images \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "prompt": "a paper kite over a grey harbour", "n": 2, "aspect_ratio": "16:9" }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const out = await client.media.images.generate({
  prompt: "a paper kite over a grey harbour",
  n: 2,
  aspect_ratio: "16:9",
});
for (const file of out.files) console.log(file.id, file.content_type);
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind image --prompt "a paper kite over a grey harbour" --n 2 --aspect-ratio 16:9
```

As a trained character — no `image_urls`, because the character is the reference:

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/images \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "prompt": "Ava waves at the camera on a rooftop at golden hour", "character": "Ava", "aspect_ratio": "9:16" }'
```

Each rendered file records `source.character_id` — the `chr_` it rendered as.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "image_generation",
  "model": "example/thrifty-image",
  "files": [
    {
      "id": "fil_01J...",
      "object": "file",
      "name": "image-fil_01J....png",
      "content_type": "image/png",
      "size_bytes": 184201,
      "scope": "published",
      "session_id": null,
      "sha256": "…",
      "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "cost_micro_usd": 38723
}
```

Read the bytes with [`GET /v1/files/{id}?download=true`](/docs/api/files#retrieve-a-file).

## Looks

A look sets the scene, light and wardrobe of a render; with `character`, the face stays theirs. The looks are: Candid selfie, Phone snap, Realistic, Everyday, Library, Quiet luxury, Through the glass, Flight mode, Selfcare, Japandi, Foggy morning, Rainy day, 90s editorial, Wide-angle outfit, Elevator mirror, Escalator and Tokyo street style. A character's usual looks are its [`style_pack`](/docs/api/characters#the-character-object).

## Billing

A render is billed **what it actually cost**, once it has happened, on the media tier; nothing is quoted or held beforehand, because a picture costs cents. A request on an empty balance is refused with `insufficient_credits` (402) before it reaches a model; a low balance is not turned away. The debit settles under the request's idempotency key, so a replayed request returns the same files and charges once — and the same key reaches the model's provider, so a retried render is not rendered twice. A render the model refuses or fails is `provider_error` and is not billed.

## In a session

An agent renders with the [`generate_image`](/docs/capabilities/tools#generation-tools) tool — the same route, the same catalogue, the same fields (`prompt`, `model?`, `image_urls?`, `character?`, `style?`, `character_strength?`, `n?`, `aspect_ratio?`, `seed?`) — and gets the `file_id`s back in the same turn, because the render is synchronous. Two differences from calling the route yourself:

* **The model default is yours to set.** `tools.configs.generate_image.config.models` on the agent names the model that runs when the agent does not choose one; with none pinned, the platform's default is used, as here. It is a default, not an allow-list — the agent may still name any id the catalogue publishes.
* **The bill lands on the agent.** The debit carries the `session_id` and settles against the agent's [budget](/docs/concepts/budgets) as the `media` component; a render through this route carries no session and settles against the organization.

## Errors

| Code | When |
| - | - |
| `validation_failed` | Missing `Idempotency-Key`, an unknown `model`, an `image_urls` entry that is a private host or a stored file that is not an image, a `character` that is not `ready`, a `character` with `image_urls` that are not all stills of it, a set edit that names a `model` outside the set-edit models, an unknown `style`, a `character_strength` without a `character` or outside 0.5–1, `n` outside 1–4, a field the request does not carry. |
| `not_found` | A `character`, or an `image_urls` `fil_`, this organization does not have. |
| `insufficient_credits` | The prepaid balance is empty. Nothing is rendered or billed. A retry of a request already billed under its `Idempotency-Key` is not refused. |
| `provider_error` | The model failed or refused; nothing is filed and nothing is billed. A refusal carries the model's reason after the status when it can be repeated — e.g. `the media provider answered 400: …` — so the request can be corrected. |
| `feature_not_configured` | This deploy has no generation provider configured, or `character` was sent to one that trains no characters. |

## Stock photos

`GET /v1/media/stock` — scope `agents:read`

Searches a stock photo library and returns up to `count` photos, each with a direct image URL at the size you asked for, a small preview, and the photographer credit the licence asks you to show. Free: a search is booked to the [ledger](/docs/platform/billing) as a `search` line at `$0`, so it shows up in a spend breakdown as a call that happened, not as one that was never priced.

**query** `string` *required*

What the photo should show. 1–200 characters.

**count** `number` (default: 10)

How many photos to return, 1–30. There is no cursor: `count` is the whole page.

**orientation** `string`

`landscape`, `portrait` or `square`.

**color** `string`

A dominant colour — a name such as `red`, `blue`, `brown`, `black`, `white`, or a hex value such as `#978E82`.

**size** `string`

The image size `url` points at: `small`, `medium` or `large`. Default `large`. Picks the rendition only — it does not narrow the results.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/stock?query=office+workspace&count=3&orientation=landscape" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const { data } = await client.media.stock.search({ query: "office workspace", count: 3, orientation: "landscape" });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media stock "office workspace" --count 3 --orientation landscape
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "stock_photo",
      "id": "2014422",
      "width": 3024,
      "height": 2016,
      "url": "https://images.example/2014422.jpeg?w=940",
      "preview_url": "https://images.example/2014422.jpeg?w=280",
      "alt": "Brown rocks during golden hour",
      "photographer": "Joey Farina",
      "attribution_url": "https://photos.example/photo/2014422/",
      "dominant_color": "#978E82"
    }
  ]
}
```

### The stock photo object

**object** `string`

Always `stock_photo`.

**id** `string`

The library's own id for the photo. Opaque and unprefixed — it is not a Naive Managed Agents resource id and cannot be fetched on its own; keep the photo by importing its `url` as a file.

**width** `number`

Pixel width of the original.

**height** `number`

Pixel height of the original. `width > height` is a landscape photo.

**url** `string`

A direct image URL at the requested `size`. Fetchable without a key.

**preview\_url** `string`

A small thumbnail, for picking before downloading.

**alt** `string | null`

A one-line description of the photo, when the library has one.

**photographer** `string | null`

Who took it. The licence asks that this credit be shown wherever the photo is used.

**attribution\_url** `string | null`

The page to link the credit to. This is the one field that may point at the library's own domain.

**dominant\_color** `string | null`

The photo's average colour as a hex value.

### Keeping a photo

A result is a URL, not a file. To hold the bytes as a `fil_` — so a session can attach it, or a page can serve it from your own storage — import `url` through [Files](/docs/api/files); the imported file records where it came from as a URL import.

### In a session

Agents reach the same search as the [`find_stock_photo`](/docs/capabilities/tools) tool, which takes `query`, `count` and `orientation`. It is on by default with permission `allow`.

### Errors

| Status | Code | When |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | `validation_failed` | `query` missing, `count` outside 1–30, or a filter value outside its set. |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | The library's request allowance for this deploy is spent; retry shortly. |
| `501` | `feature_not_configured` | This deploy has no stock photo library configured. |
| `502` | `provider_error` | The library answered with an error. |


# Legal
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/legal

Identity-owned verification cases and company formations: hosted verification links, formation filing, and documents.

Every route is nested under an identity. `{identity}` accepts an `idn_…` id or the identity's name.
An identity may hold any number of **verifications** (a case with one or more members who each
complete a hosted verification) and **companies** (a formation that references a verified case).
Money is integer micro-USD (`1 USD = 1000000`).

> [!NOTE]
>
> On a deployment with no legal provider bound, every route below answers `501 feature_not_configured`.

## Verifications

### List verifications

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/verifications` — scope `agents:read`

Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of `legal_verification` objects, newest first.

### Start a verification

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/verifications` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "members": [
    { "first_name": "Ava", "last_name": "Stone", "email": "ava@example.com",
      "role": "primary", "is_responsible_party": true, "ownership_percent": 100 }
  ]
}
```

Exactly one member is `primary` and exactly one is the responsible party; ownership percentages
sum to 100. Answers `201` with the case; the primary member's `link_url` is set on this response
only, and every secondary member is emailed their own link (a secondary who could not be emailed
gets `link_url` here too). Honours `Idempotency-Key`.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "lgv_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wa",
  "object": "legal_verification",
  "identity_id": "idn_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wb",
  "status": "in_progress",
  "ready_for_formation": false,
  "members": [
    { "id": "lgm_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wc", "object": "legal_member",
      "verification_id": "lgv_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wa",
      "first_name": "Ava", "last_name": "Stone", "email": "ava@example.com",
      "role": "primary", "is_responsible_party": true, "ownership_percent": 100,
      "status": "link_ready", "link_url": "https://verify.example.com/s/…",
      "link_expires_at": "2026-09-09T00:00:00Z", "completed_at": null }
  ],
  "started_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z", "completed_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z"
}
```

Member status moves `pending → link_ready | link_sent → in_progress → pending_review | verified | failed`.
`verified` and `failed` are terminal and are never changed by a later callback or read. The case is
`failed` if any member failed, else `pending_review` if any member is under review, else `verified`
once every member is verified, else `in_progress`.

### Read a verification

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/verifications/{verification}` — scope `agents:read`

The case with its members, `link_url` always `null`. Each unfinished member's status is refreshed
from the provider on this read, so a missed callback is caught up. `ready_for_formation` is `true`
once every member is `verified`.

### Complete a member

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/verifications/{verification}/members/{member}/complete` — scope `billing:write`

Pass `{ "token": "…" }` from the hosted page's redirect. Answers the `legal_member`.

### Resend a member's link

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/verifications/{verification}/members/{member}/resend` — scope `billing:write`

Mints a fresh hosted link for a member who has not finished. Answers the `legal_member` with
`link_url` set. A `verified` or `failed` member answers `state_conflict`.

## Companies

### List companies

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies` — scope `agents:read`

### Form a company

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "verification_id": "lgv_…",
  "state": "WY",
  "name_options": ["Acme Labs"],
  "naics_code": "541511",
  "description": "Software consulting",
  "mailing_address": { "line1": "1 Main St", "line2": null, "city": "Cheyenne", "state": "WY", "postal_code": "82001", "country": "US" }
}
```

The verification must be `verified` (`state_conflict` otherwise). The fee — the formation price
plus the state's filing fee, both reported by `GET /v1/legal/states` — is debited from the
organization's credits **before** anything is filed; a short balance answers `402 insufficient_credits`.
Name endings are canonicalised to `LLC`. Answers `201` with status `paid`. Honours `Idempotency-Key`.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "lgc_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wd",
  "object": "legal_company",
  "identity_id": "idn_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wb",
  "verification_id": "lgv_01j9x2k7q4m8n3p5r6s7t8v9wa",
  "status": "paid",
  "entity_type": "llc",
  "state": "WY",
  "name_options": [{ "name": "Acme Labs", "ending": "LLC" }],
  "legal_name": null,
  "naics_code": "541511",
  "description": "Software consulting",
  "mailing_address": { "line1": "1 Main St", "line2": null, "city": "Cheyenne", "state": "WY", "postal_code": "82001", "country": "US" },
  "ein_status": "none",
  "price_micro_usd": 449000000,
  "required_actions": [],
  "failure_reason": null,
  "submitted_at": null, "formed_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z", "updated_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00Z"
}
```

`price_micro_usd` is what was debited: `449000000` is \$449.00.

### Read a company

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies/{company}` — scope `agents:read`

Status moves `awaiting_payment → paid → submitted → formed | failed`. `required_actions` lists
anything a person still has to do.

### Submit a company

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies/{company}/submit` — scope `billing:write`

Files the formation. Idempotent once submitted (a second call answers the same `submitted`
company); a company that already `failed` answers `state_conflict`. A provider refusal is
recorded as status `failed` with a provider-neutral `failure_reason` and answered as the company,
not as an error.

### Documents

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies/{company}/documents` — scope `agents:read`

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/legal/companies/{company}/documents/{document}` — scope `agents:read`

The first lists `legal_document` objects (`kind` is `articles`, `ein_letter`, `operating_agreement`
or `other`); the second answers a short-lived `legal_document_link`:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "object": "legal_document_link", "url": "https://files.example.com/…", "expires_at": "2026-09-08T01:00:00Z" }
```

## Reference data

`GET /v1/legal/naics_codes?q=software` — scope `agents:read`

`GET /v1/legal/states` — scope `agents:read`

Both are paginated. `naics_code` is `{ "code", "title" }`; `legal_state` carries the state's filing
fee, which is added to the formation price:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "object": "legal_state", "code": "WY", "name": "Wyoming", "formation_fee_micro_usd": 100000000 }
```

## Verification callback

`POST /v1/webhooks/legal` — no scope; the verification provider calls it

The provider's signature is verified over the raw body before anything is parsed; a body that does
not verify answers `401 unauthorized`. A verified event flips the named member to `verified`,
`failed` or `pending_review` and recomputes the case. A member already in a terminal state is left
as it is, so a redelivered event changes nothing. Answers `202 { "object": "legal_webhook", "accepted": true | false }`;
`false` means the event named a member this deployment does not hold or one already settled.

## Errors

`validation_failed` for member, name, state and description rules; `state_conflict` for a company on
an unverified case or a second submit of a failed one; `job_not_ready` when reference data cannot be
answered right now; `insufficient_credits`; `feature_not_configured`. See [Errors](/docs/api/errors).


# MCP server
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/mcp

The Naive Managed Agents API published to a model as an MCP tool catalog, generated from the route table.

`POST /v1/mcp` publishes **this API itself** as a [Model Context Protocol](/docs/capabilities/tools#mcp-connector) tool catalog. Point an agent at it and the agent can operate a Naive Managed Agents account — create agents, start sessions, read events, exec on a computer, check credits — the same way it operates any other connected system.

It is a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint. It is **not** a REST resource: there is no object, no list, no `GET`. Everything it can do, it does by dispatching one of the routes documented elsewhere in this reference.

```jsonc theme={"system"}
{
  "mcp_servers": [
    { "type": "url", "name": "vetta", "url": "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/mcp" }
  ]
}
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> There is no generic `client.mcp.call` or CLI JSON-RPC passthrough, on purpose. Every operation behind
> this endpoint already has a typed method and a command; a second, weaker way to call the same routes
> would be a surface to keep in sync for no gain. `client.mcpSessions` and `naive mcp` manage the
> endpoint's credentials; the endpoint itself exists for **MCP clients** — an agent's runtime, or your own.

## Authentication

Use either an organization-scoped API key or a short-lived [MCP session](/docs/api/mcp-sessions), in the
same header. An MCP session adds an explicit tool allowlist, expiry, immediate revocation, and an
optional identity binding.

```bash theme={"system"}
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
```

```bash theme={"system"}
Authorization: Bearer mcp_...
```

Two properties follow from how a tool call is executed, and both are the point of the design:

* **A tool call is an ordinary API call.** It is re-dispatched through the full middleware chain — authentication, scope check, plan gate, rate limit, strict request validation — as a real request carrying **the caller's own bearer**. There is no second authorization path, because there is no second path.
* **A tool can never reach further than its credential.** A credential scoped `agents:read` calling `agents_create` gets `403 forbidden` back as a tool error, in the control plane's own words. An MCP session additionally sees and calls only its `allowed_tools`.

The endpoint itself declares no scope of its own — any authenticated principal may open the catalog — because every tool inside it is authorized by the route it actually is. The [plan gate](/docs/platform/billing) applies as usual.

## Handshake

The server speaks MCP revision `2025-06-18` and exactly the methods a tool catalog needs: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Any other method answers JSON-RPC error `-32601`.

```bash initialize theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/mcp \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{}}}'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
    "capabilities": { "tools": {} },
    "serverInfo": { "name": "vetta", "version": "2026-09-30" }
  }
}
```

## The tool catalog

`tools/list` returns one tool per served route — **284 tools** on this deploy today, from 372 routes less the 41 open ones and the 47 [withheld](#withheld-routes). The catalog is **generated from the server's own route table**, the same table [`GET /v1/openapi.json`](/docs/api/overview#machine-readable-description) is generated from — so it describes exactly what the deploy you are talking to serves. A tool cannot exist without a route, and a route cannot acquire a tool by being described twice.

**name** `string`

`resource_verb`, derived from the route's resource and its handler — `agents_create`, `agents_list`, `sessions_list_events`, `computers_exec_command`, `credits_get_balance`. A sub-resource keeps its word: the [browser](/docs/api/browser) on a computer is `computers_browser_run_action`, `computers_browser_login`, `computers_browser_save_context`. Namespaced by the server name in an agent's tool config, a tool is `vetta.agents_create`.

**description** `string`

What the operation does, the `METHOD /v1/…` it maps to, one sentence about the resource, and the scope it requires.

**inputSchema** `object`

JSON Schema. Path parameters, declared query filters and body fields arrive as **one flat object** — a model fills a flat schema reliably and a nested one it does not. The body fields are the same zod schema the server validates with, so the arguments offered are the arguments enforced. `additionalProperties` is `false`.

**annotations.readOnlyHint** `boolean`

`true` when the call changes nothing, `false` when it does. That is the method in almost every case — `GET` reads, the rest write — with named exceptions in both directions: a POST whose body is only the question (pricing a payment or a card, minting a file link) is `true`; the one `GET` that returns a live card credential is `false`. This is what lets a caller allow reads without maintaining a list.

**annotations.destructiveHint** `boolean`

`true` when the call is one a person should see before it runs: every `DELETE`, and any call that spends money or acts outside your account (a payment or transfer, a card order or its credential reveal, a credits charge, paid media generation, a company formation, a social post, an outbound email or SMS, an account created in a third party's system), changes the organization's security posture (vaults, webhooks, the organization and its members, domains, app secrets and login links, saved browser logins), rewrites data (a schema migration, raw SQL through `apps_query_db`, a path removal), decides what an agent may do (creating, updating or rolling back an agent — its version is the model, toolset, permissions and budget every later session runs under), or runs code (a command on a computer, a browser action that acts on a page, an action on a mobile device, a browser login or sign-up). Creating a session, an identity, an inbox, a skill, a file or a deployment is `false`. A read-only tool is never destructive. This is what lets a caller allow benign writes and `ask` only on the dangerous ones.

Listing routes additionally accept `limit` (1–100) and `after`; a read addressed to a single id accepts neither. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "name": "sessions_list_events",
  "description": "List events — GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events — a session is one metered, resumable run of an agent, with a gap-free event log. Requires the `sessions:read` scope.",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "id": { "type": "string", "description": "the `id` path segment" },
      "after_seq": { "type": "string", "description": "filter" },
      "limit": { "type": "string", "description": "page size, 1–100. Ask for a small one: a tool result is truncated at 8000 characters." },
      "after": { "type": "string", "description": "cursor: the id of the last row of the previous page." }
    },
    "required": ["id"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  },
  "annotations": { "readOnlyHint": true, "destructiveHint": false }
}
```

## Calling a tool

```bash tools/call theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/mcp \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call",
       "params":{"name":"agents_get","arguments":{"id":"agt_01H8XK..."}}}'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"id\":\"agt_01H8XK...\",\"object\":\"agent\",\"name\":\"support\"}" }]
  }
}
```

The response body of the underlying call is returned verbatim as the tool's text content.

### Failures

A failed call is a **tool error**, not a transport error. The JSON-RPC envelope stays `200` and the result carries `isError: true` with the API's own [error envelope](/docs/api/errors) as its text — a non-200 here would make an MCP client conclude the *transport* is broken and drop the whole catalog for the turn.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_request\",\"code\":\"not_found\",\"message\":\"agent not found\",\"request_id\":\"req_01H...\"}}" }],
    "isError": true
  }
}
```

Naming a tool that is not in the catalog answers `no such tool: <name>` with `isError: true`, rather than guessing a route.

### Results are capped at 8,000 characters

A tool result is read by a model, on a budget, so a result longer than 8,000 characters is cut and the cut says so — terminally. The notice states that the reply was cut, that **paging will not fix it** (the rows themselves are large, so the next page is cut too), and that the model should report what it can see rather than call again.

This wording is deliberate and was measured. An earlier version suggested narrowing the call, and models then walked the cursor to their iteration limit — 24 model calls to count sixteen rows, every page truncated. Ask for a small `limit`, or filter, before you call.

## Withheld routes

**Some served routes are deliberately absent from the catalog.** They answer normally over HTTP with the same key; they are simply never handed to a model. Each exclusion is a property you can rely on, not an oversight — the reason is recorded next to the route in the server and enforced by a test that fails if a withheld route disappears.

| Route | Why it is withheld |
| - | - |
| `POST /v1/mcp` | This endpoint. A tool that re-enters the catalog is a loop with a credential in it. |
| `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/stream` | An SSE body that never ends — a tool call has to return. `sessions_list_events` reads the same log. |
| `POST /v1/files` | Multipart upload: the body is bytes, not JSON, so there is no argument schema to publish. |
| `POST /v1/api_keys` | **Mints a live credential and returns it in the response body** — i.e. into the transcript. |
| `POST /v1/api_keys/{id}/rotate` | Same: the response carries a new secret. |
| `GET /v1/api_keys` | Withheld with the rest of the key family; nothing an agent does needs to enumerate credentials. |
| `DELETE /v1/api_keys/{id}` | Revoking the key the caller is authenticated with is a foot-gun, not a task. |
| `POST /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials` | A route that **accepts a secret value**. A model typing one writes it into a `tool.started` event. |
| `POST /v1/proxy/anthropic/v1/messages` | The [model proxy](/docs/api/proxy). Handing a model a credentialed, billed model call is a loop, and its streaming half is an SSE body that never ends. |
| `GET /v1/computers/{id}/browser/live-view` | Answers a [dashboard session](/docs/api/browser#live-view) only, and its answer is a bearer URL for a person's eyes, not a transcript. |
| `POST /v1/computers/{id}/browser_sessions/{bid}/live_view` | Mints a bearer credential that grants full control of the browser, for the person in the dashboard; the agent driving the browser never sees its own live view. |
| `POST /v1/mobile_devices/{id}/live_view` | The same bearer credential for a [mobile device](/docs/api/mobile-devices)'s screen, withheld for the same reason. |
| `POST /v1/browser/contexts/{name}/grants` | Dashboard session only: a [saved login](/docs/api/browser#grant-a-saved-login) is default-deny and a model must not grant itself one. |
| `DELETE /v1/browser/contexts/{name}` | Dashboard session only, like the grant it revokes. |
| `POST /v1/browser/credentials` | **Accepts a password value**, like the vault write above; the `login` action reads what a person sealed. |
| `POST /v1/proxy/openai/v1/chat/completions` | The same proxy in its second dialect. |
| `POST /v1/models/auto_select` | A credentialed, billed model-side call like the proxy, and its answer is an id for the next line of the same program — an SDK-only add-on. |
| `POST /v1/sandbox/mcp` | The session tool bridge — a transport for tools a model already has. |
| `POST /v1/sandbox/handoffs` | The door behind [`send_to_agent`](/docs/capabilities/tools#handoffs) with `wait: false`. It answers only a bearer the session runtime mints for the session it is running; a model that may hand work on already holds the tool. |
| `POST /v1/sandbox/channel/messages` | The door behind `post_to_channel`: a room's member speaks into its root. Same per-session bearer; a member already holds the tool, and anyone else has no room to post into. |
| `POST /v1/sandbox/board/cards/{id}/wake` | Starts the teammate a member's `board_write` just handed a card to. Same per-session bearer; the session runtime calls it after the write, so a model never needs to. |
| `GET` `HEAD` `POST` `PATCH` `PUT` `DELETE /v1/apps/{id}/db/rest/*` | The [database REST passthrough](/docs/api/database#rest): its arguments *are* the rest of the URL — any path, any filter, a body no flat schema describes. The `apps` tool's `db_rest` action hands it to an agent whole. |

Two rules generate that table, and they are worth stating plainly because they are the security properties the endpoint offers:

> [card] No route that returns a secret
>
> The four `/v1/api_keys` routes are withheld as a family because two of them return live credentials into the model's transcript and the log that records it; the browser and phone live views are bearer credentials for the same reason. A [key](/docs/api/authentication) is issued by a person, in the dashboard or the CLI — never by an agent.

> [card] No route that accepts a secret
>
> `POST /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials` and `POST /v1/browser/credentials` are the routes whose body carries a secret *value*. [Vault](/docs/api/vaults) reads never return values, so the rest of the vault family is published; the writes are not.

The rest are not security exclusions at all — they are shape exclusions. A never-ending stream, a byte body with no JSON schema, the catalog itself, a billed model call that also streams, and a REST passthrough whose arguments are an arbitrary URL cannot be expressed as a flat tool call that returns. The database one is not lost to agents: the built-in `apps` tool's `db_rest` action carries the whole request.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Withholding is not an access control. It keeps these operations out of a model's *reach*; it does not stop the key from performing them. If an agent must not be able to touch a resource at all, scope its key — the tool call is checked against that key like any other request.

## Permissions

Because the catalog arrives as an ordinary external MCP server, an agent's own tool policy governs it. `vetta.agents_create` is filtered by the same allow / ask / deny mechanism as `bash`, and the default permission for MCP tools is **`ask`** — a newly exposed tool never auto-runs. See [Tools](/docs/capabilities/tools#mcp-connector) for the `tools.configs` shape, and pair it with `annotations.readOnlyHint` and `annotations.destructiveHint` to allow reads and benign writes while asking on the dangerous ones.


# MCP sessions
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/mcp-sessions

Mint short-lived, revocable, least-privilege credentials for the Naive MCP server.

An MCP session is an opaque bearer for [`POST /v1/mcp`](/docs/api/mcp). It carries an organization,
control-plane scopes, an explicit tool allowlist, an expiry and, optionally, an
[identity](/docs/api/identities) as a label. The label is not enforced yet: a session acts on any identity
its scopes and tools reach. Use one instead of a general API key when an MCP client should have a bounded lifetime and
blast radius.

Making a session with chosen scopes and tools needs `admin`. A signed-in person can [connect their own agent](#connect-your-own-agent) and manage it. The routes are withheld from the MCP catalog itself, so a
model cannot mint, enumerate, or revoke credentials.

## Connect your own agent

A signed-in person of any role sends a name alone and gets a **connected agent**:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "name": "Ada's agent" }
```

It is bound to them (`member_id`), holds a plain member's scopes whatever their role, reaches any tool those scopes allow (its `allowed_tools` is empty, and `tools/list` shows it `tools_search` and `tools_execute`, which find and run the rest), and lasts 90 days unless `expires_in_seconds` says less. The reply adds `url`, the address to give the agent. Removing the person deletes it. API keys and agents cannot make one.

A person lists, reads and revokes their own; an owner or admin, everyone's. Nobody else reaches these routes.

## Create

`POST /v1/mcp_sessions`

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/mcp_sessions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "release agent",
    "identity_id": "idn_01H...",
    "scopes": ["agents:read", "sessions:write"],
    "allowed_tools": ["agents_list", "sessions_create"],
    "expires_in_seconds": 3600
  }'
```

`scopes` and `allowed_tools` need `admin`, and API keys may use them. `expires_in_seconds` defaults to one day and must be between 60 seconds and 90 days. Duplicate
scopes and tool names are collapsed. If `identity_id` is present, it must name an identity in the
same organization (`404` otherwise), and `scopes` and `allowed_tools` must be sent with it: a connected agent acts as its person and takes no identity (`400 validation_failed`).

The response contains `secret` exactly once. Store it as a secret; the server stores only its
SHA-256 digest. Later reads expose the non-sensitive `prefix` so an operator can identify the
credential without replaying it.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "mcs_01H...",
  "object": "mcp_session",
  "name": "release agent",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H...",
  "member_id": null,
  "scopes": ["agents:read", "sessions:write"],
  "allowed_tools": ["agents_list", "sessions_create"],
  "prefix": "mcp_01H...",
  "expires_at": "2026-09-07T18:00:00Z",
  "revoked_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-07T17:00:00Z",
  "secret": "mcp_..."
}
```

The secret is shown only in this response. It is random and unrelated to the session's `id`; only its
SHA-256 and the `prefix` are stored. Use it as the MCP endpoint bearer:

```bash theme={"system"}
Authorization: Bearer mcp_...
```

`tools/list` returns only `allowed_tools`. A call must also satisfy its underlying route scope;
allowlisting a tool never widens `scopes`. The bearer also works on the REST route behind an
allowlisted tool, but never on a route the MCP catalog withholds (creating or rotating API keys,
creating MCP sessions, and the like), whatever the allowlist names: those answer `403`. Expiry and revocation are checked from storage on every
request, so revocation has no cache-delay window.

## List and inspect

* `GET /v1/mcp_sessions`
* `GET /v1/mcp_sessions/{id}`

Both return metadata only. Neither returns `secret` nor `secret_hash`.

## Revoke

`DELETE /v1/mcp_sessions/{id}` marks an active credential revoked. The next request made with that
bearer receives `401 unauthorized`. Revocation is one-way; mint a new session to restore access.

## TypeScript

```ts theme={"system"}
const session = await naive.mcpSessions.create({
  name: "release agent",
  scopes: ["agents:read"],
  allowed_tools: ["agents_list"],
  expires_in_seconds: 3600,
});

await naive.mcpSessions.list();
await naive.mcpSessions.get(session.id);
await naive.mcpSessions.revoke(session.id);
```


# Media
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/media

Images, video, clips, audio and stock photos — the media routes, the catalogue of models they accept, and the library every result lands in.

Media is one catalogue, one library and six routes, shared by the REST API and an agent's tools:

| | Route | Answers |
| - | - | - |
| [Images](/docs/api/images) | `POST /v1/media/images` | Synchronous — the finished [files](/docs/api/files), in one call. |
| [Stock photos](/docs/api/images#stock-photos) | `GET /v1/media/stock` | Licensed photos by description; import one as a file with `POST /v1/files/imports`. |
| [Video](/docs/api/video) | `POST /v1/media/videos` | A `202` **media job** you read back with `GET /v1/media/{id}` and list with `GET /v1/media`. |
| [Characters](/docs/api/characters) | `POST /v1/characters` | A `202` **character** in `training` — a reusable persona an image renders as, with `character` on `POST /v1/media/images`. |
| [Clips](/docs/api/clips) | `POST /v1/media/clips` | A `202` clip job — scored, captioned short clips cut from a long video. |
| [Mira](/docs/capabilities/tools#editing-a-clip-edit_video-mira) | `POST /v1/media/edits` | A `202` edit job — a short clip changed from a prompt. Read it with `GET /v1/media/edits/{id}`. |
| [Audio](/docs/api/audio) | `POST /v1/media/audio/transcriptions` · `POST /v1/media/audio/speech` · `POST /v1/media/audio/conversations` | Transcription as a media job; speech and a spoken reply as finished files. |
| Models | `GET /v1/media/models` | The catalogue below — which `model` each route accepts. |
| [Library](/docs/api/files) | `GET /v1/files` | Every result lands in [Files](/docs/api/files) with its `source` — filter by `kind`, `source`, `tag` or `search`. |

> [!NOTE]
>
> There is **no fixed list of generation models**. The catalogue is read from the provider on every call, so a model published today is callable today. Search it here; pass what you find as `model` to [`POST /v1/media/images`](/docs/api/images) / [`POST /v1/media/videos`](/docs/api/video) or to [`generate_image` / `generate_video`](/docs/capabilities/tools#generation-tools), or pin it on an agent with `tools.configs.<tool>.config.models`.

## The media model object

**object** `string`

Always `media_model`.

**id** `string`

The model's id. This is what `model` takes, on the generation routes and on the tools.

**name** `string`

The model's display name.

**kind** `string`

`image` · `video` · `mesh` · `stt` · `tts` · `s2s`. The three audio kinds are [the audio catalogues](/docs/api/audio#the-catalogues).

**description** `string`

What the model is good at, in the model author's own words.

**prices** `object[]`

Mesh models only. One entry per option the model offers: `texture` (boolean), `rig` (boolean), and `micro_usd` (integer, what that combination costs). Image, video and audio rows omit it.

Image, video and audio rows publish no price, for the same reason [`GET /v1/models`](/docs/api/models) publishes none: those jobs are billed **what they actually cost**, and that is only knowable once the job has finished. A mesh row publishes `prices`, because that job's price is fixed by the model and its `texture` and `rig` switches. See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#3d-assets).

## Search models

`GET /v1/media/models` — scope `agents:read`

**kind** `string` *required*

`image` · `video` · `mesh` · `stt` · `tts` · `s2s`. Required: each is its own capability with its own catalogue — the audio ones are described on [Audio](/docs/api/audio#the-catalogues).

**search** `string`

Matches a model's id, name or description. Omit it to list them all.

**limit** `number`

Page size, 1–100.

**after** `string`

The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Opaque — it is not a row id.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/models?kind=video&search=seedance" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "media_model",
      "id": "bytedance/seedance-2.5",
      "name": "Seedance 2.5",
      "kind": "video",
      "description": "A text- and image-to-video model for short cinematic clips.",
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

Ordering is the platform's own models first, then the rest; within each, cheapest-first where a per-output price is published. That is why an image request can leave `model` out: it runs the first entry that takes what it carries. A video request can leave it out too: it runs the first of the platform's video defaults the catalogue publishes — the standard video model, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-max`, `minimax/hailuo-3`, `bytedance/seedance-2.5`, then `alibaba/wan-3.0/text-to-video` (for an edit, only one the catalogue says takes a video; the platform's per-second video models take a first frame, not a clip to edit); otherwise name one. Every model listed is callable by its id, whichever backend renders it.

A deploy with no generation provider configured answers `501 feature_not_configured` rather than an empty list — "nothing is configured here" and "the provider has no models" are different facts.


# Media skills
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/media-skills

Turn 1–3 public short videos into a skill your agents can follow — built, sampled and saved for you.

A media skill build studies 1–3 public short videos (Instagram Reels or TikTok videos), writes a `SKILL.md` that captures their format, and renders a sample to show it. Every round that finishes is saved as the next version of one of your organization's [skills](/docs/api/skills), so it appears on the Skills page and any agent can use it. Not happy with it? Send feedback and the build runs another round.

A build runs in your organization and bills what it uses to your balance, up to a fixed budget per build. It needs a live key (`sk_live_…`); a test key is refused with `forbidden`.

Your agents can build and revise skills too, with the `build_media_skill` tool: it asks before it starts, runs in the background, and tells the agent the saved skill and its samples when the round is done. The same rules apply — a live organization, in credit, the same budget per build.

## The media skill build object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `ctp_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `media_skill_build`.

**name** `string`

The build's name; the saved skill's slug is made from it.

**state** `string`

`building` while a round runs, `ready` once one has finished, `setup` when none has.

**urls** `string[]`

The links, as accepted.

**rounds** `object[]`

Newest first. Each has `n`, `feedback`, `state` (`queued` → `authoring` → `rendering` → `ready` | `failed`), `skill_md`, `frames`, `samples` (each with a short-lived `url`), `spend_micro_usd`, `error`, `created_at` and `finished_at`.

**skill** `object | null`

`{ id, slug, version }` — the skill the newest finished round was saved as. `null` until the first round is ready.

**spend\_micro\_usd** `integer`

What the build has used so far.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Start a build

`POST /v1/media/skills` — scope `agents:write`. With `urls`, it starts a build; with `build_id` and `feedback`, it [revises one](#revise-a-build). An [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) header is **required**; a retry with the same key answers the build it already started. Your balance must be above zero (`insufficient_credits`).

**urls** `string[]` *required*

1–3 public reel or video links. Anything else is refused with `validation_failed` on `urls`.

**name** `string`

Up to 80 characters. Defaults to `Reel skill <6 characters of the id>`.

**description** `string`

What the format is for, up to 2000 characters; it becomes the skill's description.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/skills \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: 3b2e...91" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "urls": ["https://www.instagram.com/reel/DeimezNsQRN/"], "name": "Slow feast" }'
```

The answer is `202` with the build, its first round `queued`.

## Read a build

`GET /v1/media/skills/{id}` — scope `agents:read`. Builds move forward on their own; reading one also moves it forward, so poll this until `state` is `ready`. When a round is ready its skill is already saved: `skill.slug` at `skill.version` (e.g. `media-slow-feast`, version `1`). Its reference frames stay private to your organization: the `SKILL.md` names each one by its [file](/docs/api/files) id (`fil_…`), which your agents can read.

To run the skill as its own channel, install Short Form Social bound to it: `POST /v1/blueprints/installs` with `blueprint: "media"`, `template: "faceless"`, `skill: "<slug>@<version>"`, a new `project` and `expected_revision: 0` ([installs](/docs/api/apps)). Every agent of that install uses the skill, on every later apply too; no other install gets it. An agent that ran the build proposes exactly this install, and a person approves it. After a revision, it proposes re-applying the install already bound to the skill with the new version instead.

If a round cannot be saved it is `failed` (`the skill could not be saved — send a revision to try again`); a revision saves to the same skill. Reading a build moves a round you already started forward, which can start that round's paid author and demo sessions within its cap; it never starts a new round.

## List builds

`GET /v1/media/skills` — scope `agents:read`. Newest first, [paginated](/docs/api/overview#pagination), filtered by `?state=` (`setup`, `building` or `ready`). A list does not move builds forward.

## Revise a build

Send `POST /v1/media/skills` again with the build's id and your feedback instead of `urls`. It runs the next round; when that is ready, it is saved as the next version of the same skill. The same rules apply: an `Idempotency-Key` header is **required** (a retry with the same key answers the round it already started) and your balance must be above zero.

**build\_id** `string` *required*

The build to revise (`ctp_…`).

**feedback** `string` *required*

What to change, 1–4000 characters.

A body carries `urls` or `build_id`, never both (`validation_failed`). A revision while a round is still running is refused with `version_conflict`. Another organization's build is `not_found`.


# 3D models
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/meshes

Generate a textured 3D model over REST — a queued job you read back, with a GLB file on it.

A 3D model takes from under a minute (from a photo) to over ten (from a description), so `POST /v1/media/meshes` does not wait: it answers `202` with a [media job](/docs/api/video#the-media-job-object) of `kind: "mesh"` in `queued`, and you read it back with [`GET /v1/media/{id}`](/docs/api/video#retrieve-a-job) until it is `completed` or `failed`. The finished model is a GLB [file](/docs/api/files). The same job is what an agent's `generate_3d_model` tool submits. A generated model is about appearance; for a part with real dimensions, build it in code with [`POST /v1/computers/{id}/build-3d`](/docs/api/computers#build-a-3d-model) — see [3D assets](/docs/capabilities/3d).

## Generate a 3D model

`POST /v1/media/meshes` → `202 Accepted` — scope `sessions:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) **required**.

**prompt** `string`

What to model, up to 2,000 characters. Give this or `image_urls`, not both.

**image\_urls** `string[]`

One to four photos of the same object — stored `fil_` ids or public `https` URLs. Two to four are read as views of one object. A `fil_` this organization does not hold is `not_found`.

**model** `string`

A model id from [`GET /v1/media/models?kind=mesh`](/docs/api/media#search-models). Omitted, a description and photos each get the platform's default.

**texture** `boolean`

Default `true`. `false` returns geometry only, for less.

**rig** `boolean`

Default `false`. With a `prompt`, rigs the model and adds an idle animation. Rigging requires `texture`: a rigged model is always textured, so `rig: true` with `texture: false` is `validation_failed`, as is `rig` with `image_urls` or on a model that does not rig.

**seed** `integer`

Repeat an earlier result, on models that honour a seed.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/meshes \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "image_urls": ["fil_01J..."], "texture": true }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const job = await client.media.meshes.create({ image_urls: ["fil_01J..."] });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media mesh --image fil_01J... --wait --out lantern.glb
```

```json 202 Accepted theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01J...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "mesh",
  "status": "queued",
  "model": "example/photo-to-3d",
  "input": { "image_urls": ["fil_01J..."], "texture": true, "rig": false },
  "result": null,
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": null,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-10-17T12:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": null
}
```

Once `completed`, `result` holds the GLB:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "files": [{ "file_id": "fil_01K...", "content_type": "model/gltf-binary", "bytes": 8411204 }] }
```

Read it with [`GET /v1/files/{file_id}?download=true`](/docs/api/files#retrieve-a-file). The file has `kind: "model"`, `source.type = mesh_generation` and `source.job_id` = this job. List mesh jobs with `GET /v1/media?kind=mesh`. A job an agent submitted announces itself on its session's [event stream](/docs/api/events#event-types) as `media.job.queued`, then `media.job.completed` or `media.job.failed`, with `kind: "mesh"`.

## Billing

A job is one charge for the finished model. The amount is fixed by the model, `texture` and `rig`, and is debited once, on the `media` component, when the job completes. Render time, file size and polygon count leave it unchanged. A job that fails is not billed. `GET /v1/media/models?kind=mesh` lists every option as `prices[].micro_usd`, and [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#3d-assets) has the table.

## Errors

| Code | When |
| - | - |
| `validation_failed` | Missing `Idempotency-Key`; both or neither of `prompt` and `image_urls`; an empty `prompt`; more than 4 images, or a count the named `model` does not take (a single-photo model takes 1, the multi-view model 2–4); a `prompt` to a photo-only `model`; `rig` with `texture: false`, with images, or on a model that does not rig; an unknown `model`. |
| `not_found` | An `image_urls` `fil_` this organization does not hold. |
| `provider_error` | The model would not take the job. Nothing is queued or billed. |
| `feature_not_configured` | This deploy has no 3D generation, or the option combination has no price. It is refused, never served free. |


# Email & SMS
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/messaging

Inboxes and phone numbers on an identity, outbound send, and the unified inbound message feed.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Email and SMS hang off an [identity](/docs/api/identities) — the persona is decided by **where** a message arrived, not by who sent it. Deliverability comes from a verified [domain](/docs/api/domains).

An inbox and a phone number are **identity-level**; the domain behind an inbox is **org-level**. One identity may hold several endpoints, and everything that arrives at any of them lands in the same [message feed](#list-inbound-messages).

## Email inboxes

### The inbox object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `eml_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `email_inbox`.

**identity\_id** `string`

The persona that owns the address.

**domain\_id** `string`

The [domain](/docs/api/domains) it is hosted on.

**address** `string`

The full address, e.g. `ava-sales@mail.acme.dev`.

**localpart** `string`

The part before the `@`.

**owning\_agent\_id** `string`

The agent mail to this address wakes, as this persona, billed to your credits. Each message that passes the [guards](/docs/identity/inbound#safety-inbound-is-untrusted) starts one session. The agent must hold the persona. Fixed when the inbox is created.

**wake** `boolean`

Whether mail to this address wakes `owning_agent_id`. `true` for a new inbox. An inbox made before inbound mail woke agents is `false` until you turn it on with [Update an inbox](#update-an-inbox); its mail is still stored.

**status** `string`

`active` or `disabled`.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

### Create an inbox

`POST /v1/identities/{id}/emails` — scope `agents:write`

Give **either** an explicit `address` **or** a `domain_id` — with `domain_id` the localpart is derived from the agent's name (lowercased, hyphenated, capped at 32 characters, then suffixed `-2`, `-3`, … against what is taken).

**owning\_agent\_id** `string` *required*

The agent inbound mail is for (`agt_…`).

**wake** `boolean` (default: true)

Whether mail wakes that agent. `false` stores mail without starting a session.

**address** `string`

A full address to claim. The localpart must match `[a-z0-9._-]{2,64}`. Mutually exclusive with `domain_id`.

**domain\_id** `string`

Host on this domain and auto-derive the localpart. Mutually exclusive with `address`.

No domain of your own yet? Every organization can mint one free **system domain** — a subdomain of the platform's shared mail domain, named after your organization — with `POST /v1/domains` `{ "kind": "system" }` (CLI: `naive identity domain connect`, no `--domain`). Its DNS is published for you, so it is ready for inboxes without a registrar; pass its `id` as `domain_id`, or an address on it. See [Domains](/docs/api/domains).

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/identities/idn_01H.../emails \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "domain_id": "dom_01H9DM...", "owning_agent_id": "agt_01H..." }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "eml_01H9EM...",
  "object": "email_inbox",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H...",
  "domain_id": "dom_01H9DM...",
  "address": "ava-sales@mail.acme.dev",
  "localpart": "ava-sales",
  "owning_agent_id": "agt_01H...",
  "wake": true,
  "status": "active",
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:00Z"
}
```

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) for a malformed localpart, or for supplying both `address` and `domain_id`; `not_found` (404) for an unknown identity, domain, or agent; `name_conflict` (409, `param: "address"`) when the address is already an inbox in this organization; `job_not_ready` (409, retryable) while the domain is not yet `active`. A domain error names the field you sent — `address` or `domain_id`.

### List inboxes

`GET /v1/identities/{id}/emails` — scope `agents:read`. Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination) of inbox objects; accepts `limit`.

### Update an inbox

`PATCH /v1/identities/{id}/emails/{eid}` — scope `agents:write`. Turns the wake on or off: whether mail to the address starts a session for its agent. Audited as `email.updated`. Answers the inbox.

**wake** `boolean` *required*

`true` to wake the agent on each message that passes the guards; `false` to store mail only.

### Delete an inbox

`DELETE /v1/identities/{id}/emails/{eid}` — scope `agents:write`. Mail to the address stops being accepted.

### Send email

`POST /v1/identities/{id}/emails/{eid}/send` — scope `sessions:write`

Gated on the domain's `dns_status`. A send attempted before SPF/DKIM are provisioned is refused with a **retryable** `job_not_ready` — verify the [domain](/docs/api/domains#verify-a-domain) and try again.

**to** `string[]` *required*

Recipient addresses.

**subject** `string` *required*

Subject line.

**text** `string` *required*

Plain-text body.

Answers `202` with a receipt, not a message object — the provider's own message id is deliberately not surfaced. Once the provider accepts it, the message is kept as an [outbound message](#list-sent-messages).

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "email_send",
  "accepted": true,
  "from": "ava-sales@mail.acme.dev",
  "to": ["buyer@example.com"],
  "sent_at": "2026-08-20T17:06:00Z"
}
```

**Errors** — `job_not_ready` (409, retryable) while the domain is unverified; `validation_failed` (400); `insufficient_credits` (402).

## Phone numbers

### The phone number object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `pho_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `phone_number`.

**identity\_id** `string`

The persona that owns the number.

**e164** `string`

The number in E.164 form, e.g. `+14155550123`.

**country** `string`

ISO country code.

**capabilities** `object`

`sms_inbound` is live the moment the number is bought. `sms_outbound` is true **iff** `campaign_status` is `approved`. `voice` is always `false` — voice is not supported, and the field exists so its absence is explicit.

**tier** `string`

`sole_prop` or `standard` — the carrier registration tier.

**brand\_status** `string`

`none`, `pending_verification`, `verified`, or `rejected`.

**campaign\_status** `string`

`none`, `pending`, `approved`, or `rejected`. Gates outbound.

**owning\_agent\_id** `string | null`

The agent inbound texts wake, as this persona, billed to your credits. `null` when none is set (bought without one, or its agent was deleted). The agent must hold the persona. Set or clear it with [Update a number](#update-a-number); texts that arrived with no agent set are never woken.

**provisioned\_at** `string | null`

When the carrier released the number.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

### Provision a number

`POST /v1/identities/{id}/phones` — scope `billing:write`

A number is a purchase, which is why this needs `billing:write` and not `agents:write`. An organization holds at most 3 numbers. Numbers run under the deployment's one shared carrier registration; registering your own brand is not available yet.

**tier** `string` *required*

`sole_prop` or `standard`.

**legal\_name** `string` *required*

The legal name of the deployment's shared carrier registration; any other name is refused before anything is bought.

**country** `string`

ISO country code. Defaults to `US`.

**tax\_id** `string`

`standard` tier only. Checked for presence, then discarded: never stored or sent.

**contact\_phone** `string`

`sole_prop` only. Checked for shape, then discarded: no passcode is sent, and it is never stored.

**e164** `string`

Request a specific number instead of the next available one.

**owning\_agent\_id** `string`

The agent inbound texts wake (`agt_…`). It must hold this persona. Checked before the purchase; if the agent is deleted mid-purchase, the number comes back with `owning_agent_id: null`.

Answers **`202`, not `201`**: the number exists and can receive immediately, but outbound waits on a carrier decision.

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) when a tier-specific field is missing or supplied for the wrong tier, or `owning_agent_id` is not an agent id or names an agent that does not hold this persona, or `legal_name` is not the shared registration's; `forbidden` (403) without `billing:write`; `not_found` (404) when the identity or `owning_agent_id` names nothing in this organization; `state_conflict` (409) when the organization already holds 3 numbers — nothing is bought.

### List numbers

`GET /v1/identities/{id}/phones` — scope `agents:read`. Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination); accepts `limit`.

### Update a number

`PATCH /v1/identities/{id}/phones/{pid}` — scope `agents:write`. Returns the number. Recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `phone.updated`.

**owning\_agent\_id** `string | null` *required*

The agent inbound texts to this number are for (`agt_…`), or `null` to clear it.

The body is strict: any other field is `400` `validation_failed`.

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) for another field, or an `owning_agent_id` that is not an agent id or names an agent that does not hold this persona; `not_found` (404) when this identity holds no such number, or `owning_agent_id` names no agent in this organization.

### Release a number

`DELETE /v1/identities/{id}/phones/{pid}` — scope `billing:write`. The number returns to the carrier and cannot be reclaimed.

### Send SMS

`POST /v1/identities/{id}/phones/{pid}/send` — scope `sessions:write`

**to** `string` *required*

Recipient in E.164 form.

**text** `string` *required*

Message body.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Refused with `compliance_pending` until `campaign_status` is `approved`. That is a **carrier rule**, not a platform one — no scope or plan bypasses it, and inbound keeps working the whole time.
>
> **Not available yet:** a text has no price, so after that check every send is refused `501 feature_not_configured` — this route, the CLI, the SDK and the agent's `phone.send` tool alike.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "sms_send",
  "accepted": true,
  "from": "+14155550123",
  "to": "+14155550188",
  "sent_at": "2026-08-20T17:07:00Z"
}
```

## List inbound messages

`GET /v1/identities/{id}/messages` — scope `agents:write`. It holds strangers' words and addresses, so a hosted app's own read-only key can't reach it.

Everything that arrived for this persona, both channels unless one is named.

**channel** `string`

`email` or `sms`. Omit for both.

**limit** `integer`

Page size. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `inb_01H...`).

**channel** `string`

`email` or `sms`.

**endpoint\_id** `string`

The `eml_`/`pho_` endpoint it arrived at.

**from** `string`

Sender address or number.

**to** `string`

The endpoint address or number.

**subject** `string | null`

Email subject; `null` for SMS.

**text** `string`

Plain-text body.

**auth** `object`

SPF/DKIM/DMARC results for mail, carrier origin for SMS — kept for the audit of why the message was accepted.

**session\_id** `string | null`

The session this message woke, or `null`: a guard held it (`guard_reason`), the endpoint has no owning agent, or the agent couldn't start (it doesn't hold the persona, or the balance is too low). A wake that couldn't start is retried for 15 minutes, so this can still fill in.

**guard\_reason** `string | null`

The [wake guard](/docs/identity/inbound#safety-inbound-is-untrusted) that held the message, or `null`. A held message is stored and never wakes an agent.

| Value | Held because |
| - | - |
| `sender_rate_limit` | more than 5 an hour from one sender to this inbox or number |
| `endpoint_rate_limit` | more than 20 an hour to this inbox or number, all senders together |
| `thread_turn_cap` | an 11th turn from one sender in one mail thread within a day |
| `auto_reply` | the mail is marked automatic |
| `own_persona` | it came from one of your own personas |

**received\_at** `string`

Arrival timestamp.

**read\_at** `string | null`

When it was marked read; `null` while unread.

Inbound arrives at the platform's own receivers — see [Inbound receivers](/docs/api/webhooks#inbound-receivers) for how a message becomes a message object.

## Mark a message read

`POST /v1/identities/{id}/messages/{mid}/read` — scope `agents:write`

**read** `boolean` *required*

`true` to mark it read, `false` to put it back to unread.

Returns the message. Marking a read message read again keeps the time it was first read.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/identities/idn_01H.../messages/inb_01H.../read \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "read": true }'
```

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) when `read` is missing or not a boolean; `not_found` (404) when this identity holds no such message.

## List sent messages

`GET /v1/identities/{id}/sent` — scope `agents:write`

Everything the persona sent, newest first: through [Send email](#send-email) and through its agent's own `email.send` tool alike. Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination); accepts `limit`.

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `out_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `outbound_message`.

**channel** `string`

`email`. Texts are not kept yet.

**endpoint\_id** `string`

The `eml_` inbox it was sent from.

**from** `string`

The sending address.

**to** `string[]`

Recipient addresses.

**subject** `string | null`

Subject line.

**text** `string`

Plain-text body.

**sent\_by\_agent\_id** `string | null`

The agent that sent it with its tool; `null` for a send through the API.

**actor** `object | null`

The key or person that sent it through the API; `null` when an agent sent it.

**sent\_at** `string`

When the provider accepted it.

> [card] [Identities](/docs/api/identities)
>
> The persona these endpoints hang off.


# Mini apps
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/mini-apps

The company's mini apps: pages its template declares, read with live numbers.

A mini app is a small app of the dashboard, made of the platform's blocks: what waits on you, what
the agents are doing, the board, the week ahead, posts, spend. A template declares its mini apps as
data, each with a name, an icon and one or more pages. A company with no template has none. Every
number on a page is read by the platform when you ask for it. None is stored in the mini app.

## List the mini apps

`GET /v1/mini-apps` — scope `sessions:read`

The mini apps in the template's order, each with its pages and what it reads: every source bound on any of its pages, `media_library` for the library block, and `posts_waiting` where it lists posts waiting on a person (who can decide them from it). `reads` is derived from the declaration by the platform, never written by the template.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "mini_app",
      "slug": "channel",
      "name": "Channel",
      "icon": "play",
      "pages": [
        { "slug": "posts", "title": "Posts" },
        { "slug": "schedule", "title": "Schedule" },
        { "slug": "analytics", "title": "Analytics" }
      ],
      "reads": ["post_views", "posts", "posts_waiting", "schedule", "spend_total"]
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Read a page

`GET /v1/mini-apps/{slug}?page={page}` — scopes `sessions:read`, `agents:read` and `files:read`

A page shows agents, the board, routines, the setup's answers, social handles and media, so a key
needs the scopes that guard those on their own routes. Spend also needs `billing:read`.

One page, read now on the company's clock: the one `page` names, else the first. The answer is the
mini app's summary plus `networks` (the template's networks, each `{ platform, connected }`, where
`connected` says whether a persona is connected to it and is `null` when that could not be read),
`page` (the slug that was read),
`as_of`, `timezone` and `spec`. `spec` is a flat map of elements under one `Page`: each element is
`{ type, props, children? }`, and each data slot is the source it names plus what was read, such as
`{ "$source": "spend_total", "days": 14, "value": 4120000 }`. Money is integer micro-USD.

A block that could not be read is an `Unread` element in its place, with the reason:

```json theme={"system"}
{ "type": "Unread", "props": { "of": "Metric", "label": "Spent", "reason": "the company's spend is shown to the people who can read billing" } }
```

Spend is read only for a caller holding `billing:read`. An unknown mini app or page is `not_found`.


# Mobile devices
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/mobile-devices

Cloud Android phones and iPhones you look at, tap, type into, install apps on, and destroy. The third member of the computer suite.

> [!NOTE]
>
> See [Computers](/docs/api/computers) for the Linux sandbox and [Browser sessions](/docs/api/browser-sessions) for the managed browser. A mobile device is a sibling of both: its own resource, with its own lifecycle. It needs no computer.

A **mobile device** is a cloud phone — an Android phone or an iPhone: a screen, touch input and an app lifecycle. It is usually ready in under a minute (a few minutes with `apps` at create; an iPhone up to about three), driven through a small set of actions, watched live from the dashboard, and ends when you delete it or when its own timers fire. There is **no pause**: idle cost is controlled by `idle_timeout_minutes` and `max_duration_minutes`, both set at create; the platform checks them every minute.

## The mobile device object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `mob_...`).

**object** `string`

Always `mobile_device`.

**name** `string`

Human-readable name. The one field you can change after create.

**platform** `string`

`android` or `ios`.

**os\_version** `string | null`

`13`, `14` or `15` on Android; `null` on iOS, which has no version to choose.

**model** `string`

`phone`. `tablet` and `watch` are reserved and refused today.

**jurisdiction** `string`

`us`, `eu` or `as` — where the device runs (the US, Germany or Singapore) and where its traffic comes from: a residential IP in that country, with the phone's GPS, timezone, locale and carrier matched to it. It is the one placement control; a region is never a parameter.

**status** `string`

`creating`, `ready`, `terminated` or `failed`. See [Truth](#truth-who-says-what-the-status-is).

**idle\_timeout\_minutes** `integer`

Minutes without an action after which the platform ends the device (1–180, default 10). Checked once a minute.

**max\_duration\_minutes** `integer`

Hard ceiling on the device's life (1–1440, default 120).

**apps** `string[]`

The apps asked for at create, installed from the platform's app catalogue when the device starts (an install the catalogue fails is not reported here; take a screenshot or call `install_app` to check): package names on Android (`com.spotify.music`), App Store bundle ids on iOS (`com.burbn.instagram`). There is no upload route; to add one to a running device, use [`install_app`](#act-on-the-device).

**termination\_reason** `string | null`

`null` while alive; then `requested`, `idle_timeout`, `max_duration`, `unfunded` (stopped by the platform because the balance or plan no longer covered it) or `unknown`.

**error** `string | null`

One sentence when provisioning failed, else `null`.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

**terminated\_at** `string | null`

When it ended, or `null` while alive.

**session\_id** `string | null`

The agent session whose [`mobile` tool](/docs/capabilities/tools#the-mobile-tool) opened it, the session it was created for (`session_id` at create), or `null`.

## Create a mobile device

`POST /v1/mobile_devices` → `202 Accepted` — scope `computers:write`. The row is recorded before the provider is asked, so a create whose answer is lost is still found and ended, never a device nobody can find; a provision that failed leaves the list. The request then waits up to \~45 seconds for the device to become `ready` and answers with whatever is true at that moment. An Android phone usually takes under a minute (two to three with `apps` at create) and an iPhone up to about three, so expect `creating` and poll `GET /v1/mobile_devices/{id}` until it is `ready`. There is no limit on how many devices an organization runs, only on what it can pay for: a create is admitted when the prepaid balance covers **10 minutes of runway for every live device and the new one, each at its own rate**, plus what the live ones have run so far — one Android phone needs `$0.50`, one iPhone `$0.80`, and a fifth Android phone `$2.50` when four are running, plus the minutes they have accrued. Short of that, the create is `402 insufficient_credits` before anything is provisioned, and the message names the amount needed. When every phone slot on the platform is in use, the create is `429 rate_limited`; try again shortly. A device bills per minute from create to end — `$0.05` on Android, `$0.08` on iOS, its residential network included — booked when it ends ([Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#priced-tools)).

**name** `string`

Defaults to `device`.

**platform** `string`

`android` (the default) or `ios`.

**os\_version** `string`

Android only: `13` | `14` | `15`, defaults to `15`. Omit it for `ios`: an iPhone has no version to choose, and sending one is `400 validation_failed`.

**model** `string`

`phone`, the default and today the only value; `tablet` and `watch` are `400 validation_failed`.

**jurisdiction** `string`

`us` | `eu` | `as`. Defaults to `us`. Sets where the phone runs and the country of the residential IP its traffic exits through.

**idle\_timeout\_minutes** `integer`

1–180. Defaults to `10`.

**max\_duration\_minutes** `integer`

1–1440. Defaults to `120`.

**apps** `string[]`

Up to 10 apps installed from the platform's app catalogue when the device starts: package names on Android (`com.spotify.music`), App Store bundle ids on iOS (`com.burbn.instagram`, `com.openai.chat`). No URLs; no store account is needed. The catalogue carries many but not all store apps (on Android, Wikipedia and DuckDuckGo are not offered; iPhones carry fewer), and there is no route that lists it: an app it lacks is `404`, `param: apps`, before any device starts, so check one with `install_app` on a running device first.

**session\_id** `string`

An agent session of yours. The device is filed under it, and that session's [`mobile` tool](/docs/capabilities/tools#the-mobile-tool) uses it instead of opening its own phone. When the session ends, the device ends with it. A session that has already ended is refused with `409 session_terminal`.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/mobile_devices \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{ "name": "pixel", "os_version": "15", "idle_timeout_minutes": 15 }'
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
const device = await naive.mobileDevices.create({ name: "pixel", os_version: "15", idle_timeout_minutes: 15 });
const iphone = await naive.mobileDevices.create({ name: "iphone", platform: "ios", apps: ["com.burbn.instagram"] });
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "mob_01H8YZ...",
  "object": "mobile_device",
  "name": "pixel",
  "platform": "android",
  "os_version": "15",
  "model": "phone",
  "jurisdiction": "us",
  "status": "ready",
  "idle_timeout_minutes": 15,
  "max_duration_minutes": 120,
  "apps": [],
  "termination_reason": null,
  "error": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-22T10:00:00Z",
  "terminated_at": null,
  "session_id": null
}
```

## Retrieve & list

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/mobile_devices/{id}   # retrieve one -> 200 (reconciled with the provider)
GET /v1/mobile_devices        # list (cursor-paginated), terminated and failed devices excluded -> 200
GET /v1/mobile_devices?session_id=ses_...   # only the phone that agent session opened
```

Both take any authenticated key. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination) for list parameters.

### Truth: who says what the status is

The platform ends a device on its idle and maximum timers, checking once a minute; the provider can also end one on its own (an error, a stopped account) without telling us. `status` on a row is what we last wrote; **`GET /v1/mobile_devices/{id}` asks the provider and rewrites the row** when they disagree, filling `terminated_at` and `termination_reason`. The **list reads rows only** — a provider call per row is not a read — so a list can lag until a detail is opened. Neither read wakes or bills anything: a device bills while it is alive whether or not you look at it.

## Rename

`PATCH /v1/mobile_devices/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `computers:write`. The body is strict: any field other than `name` is `400` `validation_failed` naming it. Recorded in the [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) as `mobile_device.updated`.

**name** `string` *required*

1–200 characters.

## Act on the device

`POST /v1/mobile_devices/{id}/act` → `200 OK` — scope `computers:write`. One action per call; the device must be `ready`, otherwise `409` `computer_unavailable`. Not written to the audit log: an action is work, as `exec` on a computer is.

| `type` | Fields | What it does |
| - | - | - |
