```json Response theme={"system"}
  "budget_micro_usd": 2000000,
  "consumed_micro_usd": 0,
  "token_usage": { "input": 0, "cache_write": 0, "cache_read": 0, "output": 0, "reasoning": 0 },
  "pending_actions": [],
  "output_schema": null,
  "structured_output": null,
  "last_seq": 0,
  "metadata": {},
  "started_at": null,
  "ended_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:05:00Z"
}
```

## Retrieve a session

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}` → `200 OK` with the current status, `stop_reason`, and usage.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ses_01H9AB...", "status": "idle", "stop_reason": "end_turn", "consumed_micro_usd": 41870, "last_seq": 142 }
```

## List sessions

`GET /v1/sessions` → `200 OK`, cursor-paginated. Filter with `?agent_id=`, `?deployment_id=`, and `?status=`. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

`?handoff_from=ses_…` lists the top-level sessions that root [handed off](#hand-off-to-other-agents) — the room's member work — newest first. A thread the root delegated to is not a handoff; those are `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/threads`. `?handoff_key=room:ses_…` lists the top-level sessions handed off under that exact key — the room's seated members, whoever seated them — newest first.

## Hand off to other agents

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/handoffs` → `200 OK`. Scope `sessions:write`. The session `{id}` — top-level and not yet ended — hands `message` to one or more agents of your organization, each started as a **top-level session of its own** marked `metadata.handoff: { from_session, from_agent, key, depth }`. Who may be reached is the sender's agent's `handoffs` policy, exactly as it governs the model's own `send_to_agent`; the receiver's budget is capped at its agent's per-task cap.

**agents** `string[]` *required*

One to six targets, each an `agt_` id or an agent name. Duplicates collapse to one.

**message** `string` *required*

The task. The receiver sees it prefixed with the sending agent and session, so it can tell a handoff from a person.

**handoff\_key** `string`

De-duplicates per target: a target still working under this key answers `already_running` with that session instead of starting another. Under a room's key (`room:<sender id>`) the words are delivered into that session for you, and it takes no [send](#send-input) of yours — it answers into the room; under any other key, send follow-ups to it yourself.

**budget\_micro\_usd** `integer`

Per-receiver cap in micro-USD; clamped to the target agent's `max_task_micro_usd`.

A refused target is a **row, not an error**: one target the policy does not allow does not stop the others.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "handoff_batch",
  "handoffs": [
    { "object": "handoff", "agent_id": "agt_01H9AB...", "session_id": "ses_01H9AC...", "status": "queued", "handoff_key": "trailer-cut" }
  ],
  "refusals": [
    { "object": "handoff_refusal", "agent": "producer", "code": "forbidden", "message": "lead may not hand off to producer" }
  ]
}
```

Only the sender's own faults answer with the [error envelope](/docs/api/errors): a sender that is a thread or a member's session in a room (`403 forbidden`), has ended (`409 session_terminal`), or is not yours (`404 not_found`). A chain of handoffs is at most four deep.

## Send input

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages` → `202 Accepted`. Sends input to a session and produces [events](/docs/api/events). The reply is the **acceptance**, not a session snapshot: the turn has not run yet.

**message** `string` *required*

The message text to send. It must contain some text: an empty or whitespace-only message is `400 validation_failed` naming `message`, and nothing is sent or billed. The same holds for the first `message` on create and a `message` on interrupt.

**interrupt** `boolean`

When `true`, steer a `running` session in one call: the model call the current turn has out is stopped at once and the new message is applied by the next turn. A stopped call is billed for what it used: its input plus the output streamed so far. This is the common case. Defaults to `false`.

**queue** `boolean`

When `true`, a send to a `running` session is accepted and held: the current turn finishes on its own and the message becomes the input of the turn that follows. On a session that is not running it is an ordinary send. Cannot be combined with `interrupt`. Defaults to `false`.

**model** `string`

A model id from [`GET /v1/models`](/docs/api/models). The session runs on it from this message's turn on, and later turns keep it until another send picks again. The send is quoted on it, so an unknown id is `400 validation_failed` and a model that does not serve the session's completion window is `400 window_unavailable`. The agent itself is not changed — update the agent too if new sessions should start on it.

**mode** `string`

`plan` or `build`. `plan` runs the session read-only from this message's turn on: it can research, ask and write a plan, and builds only after a person approves it. `build` leaves plan mode. A session whose harness cannot hold a call for approval refuses `plan` with `400 validation_failed` naming `mode`. Only a person sets it: a send an agent makes through the control-plane tools is `403 forbidden` naming `mode`. See [Plan mode](/docs/concepts/session-operations#plan-mode).

**idempotency\_key** `string`

Accepted and ignored. De-duplicate a retried send with the `Idempotency-Key`**header** — see [Idempotency](/docs/api/overview#idempotency); this body field does nothing.

Without `interrupt` or `queue`, sending to a `running` session returns `409` with code `session_running` — interrupt first, set `interrupt: true` to steer it, or `queue: true` to wait for it.

A member's session in a room — one [handed off](#hand-off-to-other-agents) under the key `room:<id>` — answers into that room, so a send to it (and an interrupt that carries a `message`) returns `403 forbidden`. Speak in the room instead; stopping it, approving its calls and answering its questions work as on any session.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../messages \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "message": "Actually, refund order #4822 instead", "interrupt": true }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "status": "running", "accepted_seq": 143 }
```

`accepted_seq` is the session's event high-water mark at the moment the send was accepted: **every event this turn produces has `seq > accepted_seq`**. That is what to wait on — poll `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events?after_seq=143`, or wait for the session's `last_seq` to pass it. Do not wait on `status` alone: the send returns before the first event is committed, so a status read taken immediately after can still describe the previous turn.

**A session started for a board card says when that card has moved on.** A session the [board](/docs/team/board) (or a schedule) started for a card can still be messaged after the card is closed or another session has been started on it. The send goes through as usual and the session acts on it, but it no longer holds that card. The reply then adds a `hint` naming the card: that it is `done`, or which session holds it now, so you can send your guidance there or put it on the card. Any other send has no `hint`.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...", "status": "running", "accepted_seq": 143, "hint": "Card crd_01H9CD..., which this session was started for, is now held by session ses_01H9EF...: send guidance for that card there instead." }
```

**A channel's session runs nothing.** A top-level session whose `metadata.room` is its own agent's id is a channel's transcript. A send to it — and the first `message` when it is created — is recorded on its log as the person's message (`message.completed` with `role: "user"`, under the `Idempotency-Key`), and no turn follows. Nothing is quoted, `interrupt` and `queue` change nothing, and `status` stays as it was. To ask a member, [hand off](#hand-off-to-other-agents) from it.

## Interrupt a session

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/interrupt` → `200 OK`. Stops the current turn at once (the model call in flight is aborted and billed for its input plus the output streamed so far), preserving history and the sandbox, and returns the session `idle` with `stop_reason: "interrupted"`. A live session that is not running (`idle`, or parked on an approval or a question) has no turn to stop: the interrupt changes nothing and answers the session as it was, its `stop_reason` (`end_turn`, a pending approval, …) intact. A session that has ended (`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`) is refused with `409 session_terminal`. An optional `message` is applied as the next input. Unlike [cancel](#cancel-a-session), the session stays resumable.

**message** `string`

Optional input to apply after interrupting.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../interrupt \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ses_01H9AB...", "status": "idle", "stop_reason": "interrupted" }
```

## Respond to a tool confirmation

When a tool with `permission: "ask"` runs, the session goes idle with `stop_reason: "awaiting_approval"` and the blocking calls appear in `pending_actions`. Resolve each with:

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/tool_confirmations` → `202 Accepted`, carrying the full [session object](#the-session-object) with the resolved call removed from `pending_actions`. Like a send, the reply is the acceptance: the tool has not run yet.

**tool\_call\_id** `string` *required*

The id from `pending_actions[].tool_call_id` (also carried on the `tool.confirm`[event](/docs/api/events)).

**decision** `string` *required*

`allow` to run the tool, or `deny` to reject it.

**reason** `string`

On `deny`, fed back to the model as the tool result.

**scope** `string` (default: call)

How far the `allow` reaches. `call` — the default, and what an omitted `scope` means — approves this one call. `session` grants the call's **tool** for the rest of this session: every later call to that tool name runs without a confirmation. `allow` only; `session` with `deny` is rejected with `validation_failed` (400) naming `scope`.

**answers** `object`

A template install's answers as the person edited them, keyed by question `key` (a string, or a list for a multiple choice), at most four — a template asks at most four questions. `allow` only, and only for a call that applies a template: the install runs with these answers and every other argument as proposed. Answers the template's questions refuse, a `deny`, `scope: "session"`, or any other tool are rejected with `validation_failed` (400) naming `answers` or `answers.<key>`.

**shown** `string`

On an `allow` of a `list_as_template` call: the `digest` of the [listing checks](/docs/api/apps) the card showed. It is filed with the approval, and the listing is refused if what it would list has changed since.

An `allow` of a parked `propose_plan` builds the plan at the version the call names. If the plan has
been written since — by the agent, or by you through `PUT /plan` — it is refused with
`version_conflict` (409) naming `tool_call_id`, and the call stays parked: read the plan, then `deny`
with a `reason` so the agent proposes the version that is there now.

A session grant is deliberately narrow. It covers **one tool name**, in **one session**, and it is
never implied — you ask for it per grant. It lives in that session's transcript, so it disappears
when the session ends, is invisible to every other session, and is never written onto the agent. It
does not apply to a parked question, and an explicit `deny` for a particular call still stands even
while its tool is granted.

When the parked call is the platform's tool invoker (`tools_execute`, which runs any catalogue tool
named in its `tool` argument), the grant is for **that target tool**: later `tools_execute` calls
with the same `tool` run without a confirmation, and a different `tool` through the same invoker is
confirmed as usual. The target is read from the parked call — the body carries nothing extra — and a
grant for the invoker with no target grants nothing.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../tool_confirmations \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "tool_call_id": "call_01H...", "decision": "allow" }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ses_01H9AB...", "object": "session", "status": "running", "pending_actions": [] }
```

### Operator actions

An agent may propose a wallet or card action it cannot run — open a persona's wallet, change its
limits, freeze or unfreeze it, add the testnet faucet's test money, retry or refund a card — as a
parked `operator.request`. An `allow` from a signed-in owner or admin **runs it**, once, before the
reply: the persona must be one the session's agent acts as, or the agent must be the company's CEO,
or the allow is refused with `forbidden` (403) and nothing runs. A refusal from the action itself is
the allow's refusal, and the call stays parked. A repeated allow of the same call replays the first
answer. The agent reads what the action answered.

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/operator_preview?tool_call_id=…` → `200`, scope `sessions:read`: what an
approval card shows for one parked `operator.request`, read from the account — the persona by name,
current and new limits, a card's label and what a refund returns — with `runnable` and, when it is
`false`, `why`.

## Answer a question

An agent that needs something from a person parks the turn: the session goes idle with `stop_reason: "awaiting_answer"` and the question appears in `pending_actions` as a row with `kind: "question"`, carrying a `prompt` and one to three `fields`. Answer it with:

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/answers` → `202 Accepted`, carrying the full [session object](#the-session-object) with the answered question removed from `pending_actions`. Scope `sessions:write`.

**tool\_call\_id** `string` *required*

The id from `pending_actions[].tool_call_id` on the row you are answering.

**answers** `object` *required*

One entry per field, keyed by `fields[].key`. A string, or an array of strings for a `choice` field with `multiple: true`. Every field must be answered, except one the question marked `optional: true` — say "no answer" by leaving that key out of the object. A key that is present is validated either way, so `""` and `[]` are `validation_failed`, not a way to skip.

This is a separate route from `tool_confirmations`, not a variant of it. A held tool call is answered with a verb and no payload; a question is answered with a payload and no verb. Posting an answer for a `kind: "tool"` row is rejected with `validation_failed` (400) naming `tool_call_id`, and points you at the other route.

A `choice` field accepts anything the person types unless it sets `other: false`, in which case only its listed `options` are accepted. The values are read back by the model as words, so send the option text and not an index.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../answers \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "tool_call_id": "call_01H...", "answers": { "mailbox": "hello@acme.com", "tone": "warm" } }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ses_01H9AB...", "object": "session", "status": "running", "pending_actions": [] }
```

## Read the plan

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/plan` → `200 OK`. Scope `sessions:read`. The session's living plan: `{ "object": "plan", "markdown": "...", "version": 3, "by": "owner" }`. `version` is `0` and `markdown` empty until one is written; `by` is `agent`, `owner`, or `null` at version `0`.

## Edit the plan

`PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/plan` → `200 OK`, carrying the plan. Scope `sessions:write`. The owner's edit, a compare-and-set.

**markdown** `string` *required*

The whole plan, at most 20,000 characters. `- [ ]` and `- [x]` lines are its to-dos.

**base\_version** `integer` *required*

The `version` you edited from.

The write wakes nothing: the agent reads the edit at its next turn.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PUT https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../plan \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "markdown": "- [ ] Draft the brief\n- [ ] Publish it", "base_version": 3 }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "object": "plan", "markdown": "- [ ] Draft the brief\n- [ ] Publish it", "version": 4, "by": "owner" }
```

**Errors** — `version_conflict` (409) naming `base_version` when the plan moved on since you read it; read it again and edit from there. `forbidden` (403) on a member's session in a room; `session_terminal` (409) on an ended session.

## Raise the budget

`PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/budget` → `200 OK`. Scope `sessions:write`.

A session that hit its cap stops with `stop_reason: "budget_paused"`. Raise the cap and it becomes resumable.

**cap\_micro\_usd** `integer` *required*

The new per-session cap, in micro-USD.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Raise only.** A cap at or below what the session has already consumed is rejected with `validation_failed` (400) — lowering it would be retroactive, charging a limit against spend that already happened.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PATCH https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../budget \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "cap_micro_usd": 5000000 }'
```

Returns the full session object with the new `budget_micro_usd`.

**Errors** — `validation_failed` (400) for a cap that is not a raise, is above the agent's `cap_micro_usd`, or is `null` (a session always carries a cap); `session_terminal` (409) once the session has ended, with the cap unchanged; `not_found` (404). The organization's balance is not checked here: a raise is never refused for credits.

## Cancel a session

`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/cancel` → `200 OK`. Terminally stops the session and moves it to `cancelled`. Any in-flight turn is stopped. Use [interrupt](#interrupt-a-session) instead if you want to keep the session resumable.

On the [event stream](/docs/api/events) a cancel ends like an interrupt: a `session.usage` with the session's totals, then a `session.idle` with `stop_reason: "interrupted"`, and the stream closes. No event is named for the cancel. To tell a cancel from an interrupt, read the session's `status`, which is `cancelled` (terminal) after a cancel and `idle` (resumable) after an interrupt.

Cancel is idempotent. Cancelling a session that is already `cancelled` answers `200` with the session as it is. A session that ended `completed` or `failed` cannot be cancelled and answers `409 session_terminal`.

There is no delete. Cancel is how you tidy up: it ends the session, stops its spend and lets go of the agent's computer, which is kept (delete it under [Computers](/docs/api/computers) to stop its storage). The session's record, cost and events are kept for the life of the organization; no sweep removes them. Events are guaranteed replayable for at least 72 hours (see [Events](/docs/api/events)).

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../cancel \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "ses_01H9AB...", "status": "cancelled" }
```

## Download a workspace

`GET /v1/sessions/{id}/workspaces/{phase}` → `200 OK` with the archived working directory of a session's sandbox, as it was at one boundary of its work: `end` (the session finished, or its idle sandbox was reclaimed), or `card_start` / `card_end` (it moved a board card to doing / done). `start` has none — a fresh sandbox's disk is its base image. The body is a `tar.gz`; its sha-256 is in the `x-workspace-sha256` header, and an unchanged workspace archives to the same hash. `?kind=diff` returns the `git diff HEAD` of the repository in the workspace instead, when there was one. `?card_id=crd_…` picks that card's boundary; without it the newest one of the phase answers. Credential files (`.env*` and the platform's own) and re-derivable caches such as `node_modules` are never archived.

Needs `audit:read`, like [stored proxy calls](/docs/api/proxy): it is captured content. A boundary with nothing stored — or a session in another organization — is `404 not_found`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/sessions/ses_01H9AB.../workspaces/end \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." -o workspace.tar.gz
```

> [card] [Stream events](/docs/api/events)
>
> List and stream a session's events, resumable by `seq`.


# Skills
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/skills

Versioned, org-scoped skills attached to agents.

A **skill** is a reusable, versioned instruction module — a `SKILL.md` document — that agents load on demand. Skills are org-scoped and immutable per version: each push creates a new version identified by its content hash.

## The skill object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `skl_01H...`).

**name** `string`

Unique, human-readable name within the org (e.g. `refund-policy`).

**description** `string | null`

Short description of what the skill does.

**latest\_version** `integer`

The highest version number.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## The skill version object

**id** `string`

The skill this version belongs to (`skl_…`).

**slug** `string`

The skill's slug.

**version** `integer`

Monotonic version number.

**sha256** `string`

SHA-256 of the `SKILL.md` content. Verifies integrity.

**size\_bytes** `integer`

Content size.

**created\_at** `string`

When this version was pushed.

## Create a skill

`POST /v1/skills` → `201 Created` for a new slug, `200 OK` when the slug already exists (the push is applied as a new version of it). A skill is never created empty: the create *is* the first push. Both responses are the [skill version object](#the-skill-version-object).

**content** `string` *required*

The `SKILL.md` text. Version 1 of a new slug.

**slug** `string`

Unique slug within the org — lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Required unless you send `name`.

**name** `string`

The same thing spelled `name`. Send one of `slug` or `name`.

**description** `string`

Short description. Defaults to `null`.

**sha256** `string`

SHA-256 hex digest of `content`. Optional: the server hashes the bytes itself and refuses a digest that does not match.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{ "slug": "refund-policy", "description": "How to process refunds.", "content": "# Refund policy\n...", "sha256": "9f86d0..." }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "skl_01H8XZ...",
  "slug": "refund-policy",
  "version": 1,
  "sha256": "9f86d0...",
  "size_bytes": 1024,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

## Retrieve & list

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/skills/{id}    # retrieve one
GET /v1/skills         # list (cursor-paginated)
```

See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

## Push a new version

`POST /v1/skills/{id}/versions` uploads a new `SKILL.md`. The body is the document text, optionally with its `sha256`; the server rejects the request with `validation_failed` if the hash does not match the content. Pushing bytes identical to the current version mints nothing and answers `200`.

**content** `string` *required*

The full `SKILL.md` text.

**sha256** `string`

SHA-256 hex digest of `content`. Optional: the server hashes the bytes itself and refuses a digest that does not match.

**description** `string`

Replace the skill's description as part of this push.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills/skl_01H8XZ.../versions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "content": "# Refund policy\nConfirm the order first.\n...", "sha256": "b1946ac9..." }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "skl_01H8XZ...",
  "slug": "refund-policy",
  "version": 2,
  "sha256": "b1946ac9...",
  "size_bytes": 2048,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T18:00:00Z"
}
```

## List versions

`GET /v1/skills/{id}/versions` returns version history, newest first. Cursor-paginated.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    { "version": 2, "sha256": "b1946ac9...", "size_bytes": 2048, "created_at": "2026-08-20T18:00:00Z" },
    { "version": 1, "sha256": "9f86d0...", "size_bytes": 1024, "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z" }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

## Retrieve one version

`GET /v1/skills/{id}/versions/{n}` — scope `agents:read`. Returns that immutable version's metadata **with its body**: the [skill version object](#the-skill-version-object) plus a `content` string carrying the raw `SKILL.md`.

This is the second half of progressive disclosure. The list above carries only `version`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, and `created_at`; the text itself costs this extra call, so a runtime pays for it once when the skill is actually used rather than on every turn.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills/refund-policy/versions/2 \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

`{id}` accepts a slug or an id, and `{n}` is the integer version. `not_found` (404) if either does not resolve.

## Delete a skill

`DELETE /v1/skills/{id}` — scope `agents:write`. Removes the skill and its whole version history.

A skill an agent lists — pinned (`refund-policy@3`) or floating (`refund-policy`) — is not deleted. The call answers `409` `state_conflict` and names the agents: `Used by Editor and Writer. Remove it from them first.` So is a skill that a [deployment](/docs/api/deployments) pinned to an older agent version still lists: `A routine of Editor runs an older version that uses it. Delete or update that routine first.`

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "skl_01H9BC...", "object": "skill", "deleted": true }
```

## Pin a version

An [agent](/docs/api/agents)'s `skills[]` accepts two reference forms:

| Reference | Resolution |
| - | - |
| `refund-policy` | Floats to the skill's `latest_version`, resolved **at session start**. |
| `refund-policy@3` | Pinned to the immutable version `3`. Never moves, even after new pushes. |
| `naive/landing-page-copy` | The [platform catalogue](#the-platform-catalogue), floating to its newest published version at session start. |
| `naive/landing-page-copy@1` | The platform catalogue, pinned. |

The `naive/` prefix is the whole difference: a bare slug is always one of **your** skills, a prefixed one is always the platform's, and your `landing-page-copy` and the platform's never collide. Either kind that cannot be resolved fails the agent write with `404 not_found`, `param: "skills"`.

Skill versions are content-addressed and immutable, so pushing a new `SKILL.md` never silently changes an already-pinned agent. Use `GET /v1/skills/{id}/versions` to find the numbers you can pin.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Attach a skill to an agent by slug or id. An unpinned reference (`refund-policy`) resolves to the latest version at session start; a pinned one (`refund-policy@3`) is frozen.

## The platform catalogue

The platform publishes a small catalogue of skills — landing-page copy, client onboarding, SEO briefs, clip selection and the like — that any agent can reference as `naive/<slug>`. It is read-only from the API: versions are published with a platform release, and like your own skills they are content-addressed, so a published version never changes.

```http theme={"system"}
GET /v1/skills/catalog                          # list, newest version per slug
GET /v1/skills/catalog/{slug}                   # one slug, its newest version
GET /v1/skills/catalog/{slug}/versions/{n}      # one version, with its content
```

All three accept any authenticated caller — an API key with any scope, or a signed-in session that does not yet belong to an organization — because a catalogue is something to browse before there is anything to attach it to.

### The skill catalogue entry object

**object** `string` *required*

`skill_catalog_entry`

**slug** `string` *required*

The handle you reference as `naive/<slug>`.

**version** `integer` *required*

The version described; the number to pin.

**name** `string` *required*

Display name.

**description** `string` *required*

One line on what the skill is for.

**tags** `string[]` *required*

Families the skill belongs to, e.g. `agency`, `seo`, `media`.

**content\_hash** `string` *required*

SHA-256 of `content`, lowercase hex.

**published\_at** `string` *required*

When this version was published.

**content** `string`

The raw `SKILL.md`. **Only** on the version read; the list never carries it.

### List the catalogue

`GET /v1/skills/catalog` — the newest version of every slug, alphabetical, cursor-paginated (the cursor is a slug). `?tag=` narrows to one family and `?search=` is free text over `slug`, `name` and `description`; the two compose.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills/catalog?tag=seo" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY"
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "skill_catalog_entry",
      "slug": "seo-content-brief",
      "version": 1,
      "name": "SEO content brief",
      "description": "Intent, target query, outline, entities to cover, internal links — before a word of the draft.",
      "tags": ["media", "seo", "content"],
      "content_hash": "3f1a…",
      "published_at": "2026-09-08T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

### Resolve one `naive/<slug>`

`GET /v1/skills/catalog/{slug}` — the **newest** version of that slug, without `content`. This is the route that answers "does `naive/short-video-hooks` exist, and at what version?" — `GET /v1/skills/{ref}` is *your* skills and answers `404` for a `naive/` name, which is not the same claim. A slug nothing published answers `404 not_found`, `param: "slug"`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills/catalog/seo-content-brief \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY"
```

### Read a catalogue version

`GET /v1/skills/catalog/{slug}/versions/{n}` — the entry **with** `content`. An unknown slug or version answers `404 not_found`, `param: "slug"`.

```bash theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/skills/catalog/seo-content-brief/versions/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $NAIVE_API_KEY"
```


# Social
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/social

Identity-scoped social account setup, media publishing, analytics, and comments.

Every route is nested under an identity. `{identity}` accepts an `idn_…` id or the identity's name.

## Activate

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/social/activate` — scope `billing:write`

Creates the identity's social workspace. The operation is idempotent: a later call returns the
existing workspace.

## Read status

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social` — scope `agents:read`

Returns `activated` and the provider's current connected accounts. Before activation it returns
`activated: false` and an empty account list.

## Open the account portal

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/social/portal` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "redirect_url": "https://app.example.com/social/done",
  "platforms": ["linkedin", "x"]
}
```

Both fields are optional: `redirect_url` defaults to the persona's own studio screen on deployments
that configure one. The response contains a hosted `url` the account owner visits to authorize
one or more networks. The URL is short-lived provider state; do not store it as an account.

## List accounts

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social/accounts` — scope `agents:read`

Returns a [paginated list](/docs/api/pagination). This is a live reconciliation read, not a mirror of an
OAuth token or cached account table.

## Upload media

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/social/uploads` — scope `sessions:write`

Pass `{ "url": "https://…" }`. The provider fetches the public image, video, or document and
returns a `social_upload`. Naive Managed Agents stores neither the source bytes nor a second upload record.

## Create or schedule a post

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/social/posts` — scope `sessions:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "content": "We shipped it.",
  "platforms": ["linkedin", "x"],
  "media_urls": ["https://cdn.example.com/launch.jpg"],
  "scheduled_at": "2026-09-01T14:00:00Z"
}
```

Omit `scheduled_at` to queue the post immediately. `title` is optional and defaults to the first 100
characters. `media_urls` accepts up to ten public URLs, and `file_ids` up to ten stored `fil_`
ids — each resolves to a short-lived signed URL fetched once, so a [stored file](/docs/api/files) posts
without ever needing a public address.

Which targets are legal depends on whether the post carries media. `bluesky`, `facebook`,
`linkedin`, `mastodon`, `threads`, and `x` take a post either way. `instagram`, `tiktok`, and
`youtube` publish media, not text, so naming one requires at least one `media_urls` or `file_ids`
entry — a text-only post to them is refused `validation_failed` on `platforms`, and the message
says which platform and what is missing. `pinterest` and `reddit` are connectable but not yet
postable: each needs a per-post destination (a board, a subreddit) this body has no field for, and
a post naming one is refused with that reason rather than accepted and ignored.

`visibility` is optional and says who may see the published post: `public`, `unlisted`, or
`private`. Only `mastodon` and `youtube` accept it — they are the two networks whose contract
carries all three — and naming any other platform alongside a `visibility` is refused
`validation_failed` on `visibility`, with the network named. Omit the field and nothing is sent
upstream: the post publishes at the connected account's own default, which on a video channel is
normally public. Managed Agents chooses no default of its own, so no existing integration changes behaviour.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "content": "The one-minute version.",
  "platforms": ["youtube"],
  "file_ids": ["fil_262tzfys51n955rn6d1wdchyg8"],
  "visibility": "unlisted"
}
```

### AI-generated posts

Labelling is opt-in: set `ai_generated: true` to label a post. The post then carries the network's
own AI-content label where the network has one — TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, X and Pinterest — and
its caption ends with an `#AIgenerated` line on every network, kept inside the network's length limit
(a caption that already carries the `#AIgenerated` tag is left as written; a phrase such as
"AI-generated" in the text does not count). Nothing labels a post on its own: without
`ai_generated: true` it is posted unlabelled, including one that attaches a file rendered as a
[character](/docs/api/characters).

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "content": "Monday fit check",
  "platforms": ["tiktok", "instagram"],
  "file_ids": ["fil_262tzfys51n955rn6d1wdchyg9"],
  "ai_generated": true
}
```

One non-X post costs 13,000 µUSD. A post including X costs 32,500 µUSD, or 273,000 µUSD when its
text contains an HTTP(S) link. One multi-network post pays the base once. The balance is checked
before publishing and the debit appears under the `social` component.

## Read a post

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social/posts/{post}` — scope `agents:read`

The response reports `scheduled`, `processing`, `posted`, `failed`, or `deleted` state. A post id
owned by another identity returns `not_found`.

## Analytics, comments, and deletion

* `GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social/accounts/{account}/analytics`
* `GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social/posts/{post}/analytics`
* `GET /v1/identities/{identity}/social/posts/{post}/comments`
* `DELETE /v1/identities/{identity}/social/posts/{post}`

All four verify the remote resource belongs to the identity's workspace before returning data or
mutating it. Analytics payloads remain provider-shaped under `data`; comments use Managed Agents' ordinary
pagination envelope.

## List the company's posts

`GET /v1/posts` — scope `sessions:read`

Every post the company files, across personas and sessions, in one list. A post an agent filed is
held for a person to allow before it goes out; it is listed here as `pending` until someone decides.

| Query | |
| - | - |
| `status` | `pending`, `scheduled`, `posted` or `failed`. Omit for all. |
| `identity_id` | Only this persona's posts. |
| `agent_id` | Only posts this agent filed. |
| `limit` / `after` | [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination). |
| `reconcile` | `false` lists only what is stored and asks the network nothing. Default `true`. |

`scheduled` lists the soonest first; everything else lists newest first. Before a list that can show
sent posts, up to five posts that are due and not yet confirmed are checked with the network first,
each at most once every five minutes.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "post",
  "id": "ses_01H9AB...:tc_9f2c1a7e...",
  "status": "pending",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H9AB...",
  "agent_id": "agt_01H9AB...",
  "session_id": "ses_01H9AB...",
  "tool_call_id": "tc_9f2c1a7e...",
  "content": "Three ways to fold a fitted sheet",
  "platforms": ["youtube"],
  "file_ids": ["fil_01H9AB..."],
  "media_urls": [],
  "visibility": "unlisted",
  "scheduled_at": "2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z",
  "posted_at": null,
  "url": null,
  "error": null,
  "metrics": null,
  "measured_at": null,
  "duplicate_of": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-25T17:02:11.000Z"
}
```

* A `pending` post has no network id yet: its `id` is the session and the approval it waits on.
  Allow or deny it with [`POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/tool_confirmations`](/docs/api/sessions) and its
  `tool_call_id`. What an agent filed is exactly what goes out — to change it, deny with a reason and
  the agent files it again.
* `posted` carries the permalink in `url` and, once an agent has read them, the latest numbers in
  `metrics` (`views`, `likes`, `comments`, …) with the time they were read in `measured_at`. Numbers
  are read at most once a day per post.
* `failed` carries the network's reason in `error`. A post that reached some networks before it
  failed keeps its link and its network ids for those. If the network later sends it after all, it
  reads `posted`.
* `duplicate_of` is set on a `pending` post that would publish a stored file the persona already
  has on the same network, or that an earlier approval is waiting to publish, in this session or
  another: `{ id, status, platform, at, agent_id, session_id }`. An agent's post of a file that is
  already out, scheduled or being sent on that network is refused rather than published twice —
  even when two approvals land at the same moment. Another persona posting the same file is not a
  repeat.


# Social data
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/social-data

Search a catalogue of read-only tools for public social media data, read one's input schema, and run it — priced per run, no connected account.

Three routes over one catalogue of read-only tools for public posts, profiles, comments, followers, hashtags and trends on about 21 networks. The same catalogue an agent reads with its `data_*` [tools](/docs/capabilities/tools) in the `social` domain; the guide is [Social data](/docs/capabilities/social-data). These routes are the [data routes](/docs/api/data)' `social` domain.

## The social data tool object

**object** `string`

Always `social_data_tool`.

**id** `string`

Opaque. Pass it back to [describe](#describe-a-tool) or [run](#run-a-tool) unchanged; it has no prefix and is not a stored object.

**name** `string`

What the tool does, briefly.

**description** `string`

What it returns. On [describe](#describe-a-tool), the long form.

**platforms** `string[]`

The networks it reads: `x`, `instagram`, `tiktok`, `facebook`, `reddit`, `youtube`, `snapchat`, `linkedin`, `threads`, `telegram`, `douyin`, `kuaishou`, `xiaohongshu`, `weibo`, `bilibili`, `zhihu`, `wechat`, `lemon8`, `pipixia`, `toutiao`, `xigua`.

**price** `object`

What a run costs **you**: `basis` (`per_call`, `per_result` or `varies`), `micro_usd` (integer; for `varies`, the highest case) and `text` (`"$0.003 per call"`).

## Search tools

`GET /v1/social_data/tools` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. Free.

**query** `string` *required*

What you need, as a short noun phrase (1–200 characters): `tiktok video comments`, `instagram profile`.

**platform** `string`

Only tools for this network (one of `platforms` above).

**limit** `integer`

1–20, default 8.

Answers `{ data: social_data_tool[] }`, best match first. There is no cursor: the ranking is the page.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/social_data/tools?query=instagram%20profile&platform=instagram&limit=3" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const { data } = await client.socialData.searchTools({ query: "instagram profile", platform: "instagram", limit: 3 });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive social-data search "instagram profile" --platform instagram --limit 3
```

## Describe a tool

`GET /v1/social_data/tools/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. Free.

Answers the [tool](#the-social-data-tool-object) plus:

**input** `object`

A JSON Schema per input location — `path`, `query`, `body` — each present only when the tool takes it. A [run](#run-a-tool) sends parameters in the same three places.

**notes** `string[]`

Usage notes: quirks, limits, the parameter that controls volume.

An `id` that is not a social data tool is `404 not_found`.

## Run a tool

`POST /v1/social_data/runs` → `200 OK` — scope `sessions:write`. Priced. [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) optional: a retry under the same key replays the first answer and is billed once.

**tool\_id** `string` *required*

An `id` from search.

**query** `object`

Query parameters, as `input.query` describes.

**path** `object`

Path parameters, as `input.path` describes.

**body** `object`

Body fields, as `input.body` describes.

The request returns when the run ends — usually seconds, at most about two minutes.

**object** `string`

Always `social_data_run`.

**tool\_id** `string`

The tool that ran.

**status** `string`

`succeeded` or `failed`. A failed run is still a `200`: it happened, and `error` says why.

**data** `any`

The network's data, unchanged. `null` when failed.

**error** `string | null`

Why it failed, in words that say what to change — often the parameter the network refused.

**cost\_micro\_usd** `integer`

What this run debited, on the `search` tier. Normally `0` for a failed run, and then no ledger entry is written; a stopped per-result run debits what it gathered.

**created\_at** `string`

ISO 8601.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/social_data/runs \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "tool_id": "<tool_id>", "query": { "username": "nasa" } }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
const run = await client.socialData.run({ tool_id, query: { username: "nasa" } });
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive social-data run <tool_id> --query username=nasa
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "social_data_run",
  "tool_id": "<tool_id>",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "data": { "username": "nasa", "follower_count": 98000000 },
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": 3900,
  "created_at": "2026-10-02T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

### Errors

| Status | `code` | When |
| - | - | - |
| 400 | `validation_failed` | A missing `tool_id`, a parameter location that is not an object, or input the service refused before running. Nothing is billed. |
| 402 | `insufficient_credits` | The prepaid balance is below the tool's listed price for one call (or for 25 results on a per-result tool, the most one run returns). Checked before the run starts. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The `tool_id` is not a social data tool. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | Too many runs at once; retry shortly. |
| 501 | `feature_not_configured` | Social data is not enabled on this deployment. |
| 502 | `provider_error` | The service did not answer, or the run passed two minutes and was stopped. Nothing is billed. |

## Pricing

Search and describe are free. A run is the tool's `price`, booked once on the `search` component; a failed or stopped run is normally free (a stopped per-result run costs what it gathered). See [Pricing](/docs/platform/pricing#priced-tools).


# Storage
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/storage

Object storage on a fullstack app: buckets, objects, signed URLs.

A `fullstack` [app](/docs/api/apps) has an object store alongside its database: **buckets** you name, holding **objects** by key. Storage is app-scoped and org-level — it belongs to the app, outlives any session, and is reachable by every agent that can reach the app (`allowed_apps` on the `apps` tool). A `frontend_only` app has no storage and answers `501 feature_not_configured`; a backend still provisioning answers a retryable `job_not_ready`.

This is not the [files](/docs/api/files) API. Files are what your agents produce; storage is what your app serves.

`{id}` in every route below is what the [database](/docs/api/database) routes take: an `app_` id, the app's **name**, or the word **`default`**, which resolves the organization's only `fullstack` app. With two or more `fullstack` apps `default` is `409 ambiguous_app`; with none, `404 not_found`.

## Shapes

**bucket** `object`

`{ object: "bucket", name, public, created_at }`. A name is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$`. `public` is recorded on the bucket; every read through Naive Managed Agents is authorized by your key or a signed URL either way.

**storage\_object** `object`

`{ object: "storage_object", bucket, key, size_bytes, content_type, etag, updated_at }`. `etag` is the store's hash without quotes, or `null` when it reports none.

**signed\_url** `object`

`{ object: "signed_url", url, method, expires_at }`. `method` is `PUT` or `GET`. A `GET` link is on the API's own host (`GET /v1/storage/links/{token}`, no key needed): it carries its grant and answers `302` to the store, so follow redirects (`curl -L`). A `PUT` link is the store's own address: send the bytes straight to it. Either is dead after `expires_at`.

## Buckets

* `GET /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets` — scope `agents:read`. `{ object: "list", data: bucket[] }` — the buckets the app's store holds, including ones your own code created there. A bucket whose name falls outside the grammar above is the store's alone: it is neither listed here nor tracked by Managed Agents.
* `POST /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets` — scope `agents:write`. Body `{ name, public? }` (default private) → `201 bucket`. An existing name is `409 name_conflict`.
* `DELETE /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}` — scope `agents:write`. A non-empty bucket is refused with `400 validation_failed` (param `force`); `?force=true` empties it first.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/apps/app_01H.../storage/buckets \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "name": "avatars", "public": true }'
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
await naive.storage.buckets.create("avatars", { public: true });
```

## Objects

* `GET /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}/objects?prefix=&limit=&after=` — scope `agents:read`. A [page](/docs/api/pagination) of `storage_object`, keys under `prefix`.
* `PUT /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key}` — scope `agents:write`. The raw body is the object, up to 50 MiB; `Content-Type` is required and stored → `storage_object`. Anything larger goes through an [upload URL](#signed-urls).
* `GET /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key}` — scope `agents:read`. The bytes, with the stored `Content-Type` — authorized by your key like every other read. `?signed=true` returns a one-hour `signed_url` (GET) instead of the bytes.
* `DELETE /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key}` — scope `agents:write`. Idempotent `204`.

A key may contain `/` — `users/alice.json` is one object with a two-segment key. Encode each segment as you would any path segment; an empty segment or `..` is `400 validation_failed` (param `key`).

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL -X PUT https://api.vetta.sh/v1/apps/app_01H.../storage/buckets/avatars/objects/users/alice.json \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data-binary '{ "name": "Alice" }'
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={"system"}
await naive.storage.upload("avatars", "users/alice.json", { name: "Alice" });
const { bytes, contentType } = await naive.storage.download("avatars", "users/alice.json");
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "storage_object",
  "bucket": "avatars",
  "key": "users/alice.json",
  "size_bytes": 18,
  "content_type": "application/json",
  "etag": "9a0364b9e99bb480dd25e1f0284c8555",
  "updated_at": "2026-09-06T18:00:00Z"
}
```

## Signed URLs

`POST /v1/apps/{id}/storage/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key}/upload-url` — scope `agents:write`

**content\_type** `string` *required*

The type the upload will carry.

**expires\_seconds** `integer`

60–3600, default 900.

Returns a `signed_url` with `method: "PUT"`. `PUT` the bytes to `url` with that `Content-Type` before `expires_at`; the object then appears in the bucket like one uploaded inline. The download counterpart is `GET .../objects/{key}?signed=true`, above.

## From an agent

An agent with the [`apps` tool](/docs/capabilities/tools) reaches the same store through five actions, gated by the tool's `allowed_apps`. When the organization has exactly one fullstack app, `app` may be omitted; several is `409 ambiguous_app`, none is `404 not_found`.

| Action | Arguments | Returns |
| - | - | - |
| `storage_list` | `bucket`, `prefix?`, `after?` | `{ objects, has_more, next_cursor }` — pass `next_cursor` back as `after` for the next 100. |
| `storage_put` | `bucket`, `key`, `file_id` | The `storage_object` written from an existing `fil_` — its bytes and `content_type` become the object. |
| `storage_get` | `bucket`, `key` | `{ object: storage_object, file_id }` — the bytes land in a **new** [file](/docs/api/files) the agent reads like any other. |
| `storage_remove` | `bucket`, `key` | `{ removed: { bucket, key } }`. |
| `storage_signed_url` | `bucket`, `key`, `content_type?`, `expires_seconds?` | A `signed_url` (`PUT` with `content_type`, otherwise `GET`) to hand to a browser or a script. |

Bytes never sit in a tool result: `storage_put` reads a `fil_` the agent already has and `storage_get` returns one it did not, so the [files](/docs/api/files) API is the way in and out.

## Auditing and billing

Bucket creation and deletion, object uploads, downloads and deletions are [audit](/docs/api/audit-logs) rows (`app.bucket_created`, `app.bucket_deleted`, `app.storage_put`, `app.storage_get`, `app.storage_deleted`) carrying the bucket and key — never the bytes. Creating or deleting a bucket also reaches [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) subscribers as `app.storage.bucket.created` / `app.storage.bucket.deleted` with `{ app_id, bucket }`, once the bucket and its audit row exist; object reads and writes are audit rows only, never [events](/docs/api/events). Storage bills on the `storage` [line item](/docs/api/credits) per bucket per day once a rate is published; **no rate is published today, so storage carries no charge** — and no line appears on the ledger.

## Errors

| status | code | when |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | `validation_failed` | a bad bucket name or key, a missing `Content-Type`, an inline `PUT` over 50 MiB, or a non-empty bucket deleted without `force` |
| `404` | `not_found` | no such app, bucket or object |
| `409` | `name_conflict` | the bucket already exists |
| `409` | `ambiguous_app` | `default` and the organization holds several `fullstack` apps; name one |
| `501` | `feature_not_configured` | a `frontend_only` app |


# Trading
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/trading

A brokerage account an identity connects over OAuth, read and traded through — paper or live.

Every route is nested under an identity. `{identity}` accepts an `idn_…` id or the identity's name.
An identity may connect one brokerage account per env: `paper` (simulated money) and `live`. A
connection is addressed by `(identity, env)` — it has no id of its own. Amounts are integer
micro-USD (`1 USD = 1000000`); quantities are decimal strings (`"0.0125"`), because fractional shares
and coins need them. See [Trading](/docs/identity/trading) for the model and the agent tools. Reads need the `agents:read`
scope and writes need the `billing:write` scope; on a `live` account, connecting, completing, placing, canceling and closing
also need a live `sk_live_` key.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Naive Managed Agents is not a broker, a dealer or an investment adviser, and holds no customer money. The account, its orders and its fills are the brokerage's. Nothing Naive or an agent says about a symbol is investment advice.

> [!NOTE]
>
> On a deployment with no brokerage app configured, connecting and every read or write at the brokerage answer `501 feature_not_configured`, and so does listing connections; disconnecting still works.

## The connection object

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "trading_connection",
  "identity_id": "idn_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "env": "paper",
  "status": "active",
  "account_number": "PA3XXXXXXX",
  "scope": "account:write trading data",
  "status_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2026-10-07T10:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-07T10:00:04Z"
}
```

`status` is one of `pending` (an authorization was started), `active`, `expired` (the brokerage
revoked access — connect again) or `failed`, with `status_reason` saying why. Reconnecting an
`active` env keeps it `active` until the new authorization lands; a declined re-authorization leaves
it `active` and only records the reason. This object never carries a token: Naive keeps one sealed
access token per identity and env, and no response returns it.

## Connect

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/connect` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "env": "paper" }
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "trading_connect",
  "authorize_url": "https://…/oauth/authorize?…",
  "env": "paper",
  "disclosure": "By allowing Naïve to access your brokerage account, you are granting Naïve access to your account information and authorization to place transactions in your account at your direction. …"
}
```

Show `disclosure` to the person **before** they open `authorize_url`. The link works once and expires
after 15 minutes. When they approve, the brokerage sends their browser to
`GET /v1/trading/oauth/callback`, which stores nothing: it forwards the brokerage's answer to the
dashboard's `/trading/complete` page. There, the signed-in person finishes the connection with
`POST /v1/trading/oauth/complete`, and lands on the identity's page with `?trading=connected` — or
`?trading=failed`, with the reason on the connection. Not offered over [MCP](/docs/api/mcp): a model never
hands a person a link that binds their brokerage to an identity.

## Complete a connection

`POST /v1/trading/oauth/complete` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "state": "…", "code": "…" }
```

The dashboard calls this for you; you only call it if you serve your own return page. Send what the
brokerage returned: `state`, plus `code` — or `error` when the person declined. A `state` is accepted
once, and only from a key in the organization that started the connect, so a link that reaches
someone else can never put their brokerage account on your identity. An unknown, used or foreign
`state` is `not_found`. Answers the `trading_connection`: `active` with its `account_number`, or
`failed` with `status_reason` (an already `active` connection stays `active` and only records the
reason).

## List connections

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/connections` — scope `agents:read`

`{ "object": "list", "data": [ trading_connection, … ] }` — at most one per env.

## Disconnect

`DELETE /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/connections/{env}` — scope `billing:write`

Deletes the connection and its sealed token. Answers
`{ "object": "trading_connection", "identity_id": "…", "env": "paper", "deleted": true }`, or
`404 not_found` when that env is not connected. To also revoke Naive's access at the brokerage, do so
in the brokerage's own settings.

## Choosing the env

Every read and write takes `env` (a query parameter on reads and cancel, a body field on place and
close). Given, it is used. Omitted, the identity's one `active` connection is used; with both
`active` the call answers `400 validation_failed` with `param: "env"`; with none, `409
state_conflict` — connect first.

## Account

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/account?env=` — scope `agents:read`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "trading_account",
  "env": "paper",
  "account_number": "PA3XXXXXXX",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "cash_micro_usd": 100000000000,
  "buying_power_micro_usd": 200000000000,
  "equity_micro_usd": 100000000000
}
```

`status` is the brokerage's own account status, verbatim.

## Positions

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/positions?env=` — scope `agents:read`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "trading_position",
      "symbol": "AAPL",
      "asset_class": "us_equity",
      "side": "long",
      "qty": "2",
      "avg_entry_price_micro_usd": 180000000,
      "current_price_micro_usd": 190060000,
      "market_value_micro_usd": 380120000,
      "unrealized_pl_micro_usd": 20120000
    }
  ]
}
```

A crypto position's symbol is written without a slash (`BTCUSD`). `asset_class` is `us_equity`,
`crypto` or `us_option`.

## The order object

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "trading_order",
  "id": "61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d",
  "client_order_id": "req_2c8f…",
  "symbol": "AAPL",
  "asset_class": "us_equity",
  "side": "buy",
  "type": "limit",
  "time_in_force": "day",
  "qty": "1",
  "notional_micro_usd": null,
  "filled_qty": "0",
  "filled_avg_price_micro_usd": null,
  "limit_price_micro_usd": 180250000,
  "stop_price_micro_usd": null,
  "extended_hours": false,
  "status": "new",
  "created_at": "2026-10-07T14:30:00Z",
  "filled_at": null,
  "canceled_at": null
}
```

`id` is the brokerage's order id. `status` is the brokerage's own (`new`, `partially_filled`,
`filled`, `canceled`, …), verbatim. An order Naive cannot represent — a kind placed elsewhere that
this API does not offer — is left out of lists, and reading it by id answers `validation_failed`.

## List orders

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/orders?env=&status=&limit=` — scope `agents:read`

`status` is `open` (default), `closed` or `all`; `limit` 1–500 (default 50). Answers
`{ "object": "list", "data": [ trading_order, … ] }`, unpaged.

## Read an order

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/orders/{order_id}?env=` — scope `agents:read`

## Quotes

`GET /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/quotes?symbols=&asset_class=&env=` — scope `agents:read`

`symbols` is 1–100, comma-separated, of one `asset_class`: `us_equity` (default) or `crypto`. Crypto
symbols are slashed: `BTC/USD`.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "trading_quote",
      "symbol": "AAPL",
      "asset_class": "us_equity",
      "bid_price_micro_usd": 190050000,
      "ask_price_micro_usd": 190070000,
      "bid_size": "100",
      "ask_size": "200",
      "quoted_at": "2026-10-07T14:30:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

A price finer than a micro-dollar is rounded half-up.

## Place an order

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/orders` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "env": "paper",
  "symbol": "AAPL",
  "side": "buy",
  "type": "limit",
  "time_in_force": "day",
  "qty": "1",
  "limit_price_micro_usd": 180250000
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| - | - |
| `symbol` | Required. Option symbols are accepted as they are. |
| `side` | `buy` or `sell`. |
| `type` | `market`, `limit`, `stop` or `stop_limit`. Required — there is no default. |
| `time_in_force` | `day`, `gtc`, `ioc`, `fok`, `opg` or `cls`. Required. |
| `qty` / `notional_micro_usd` | Exactly one. |
| `limit_price_micro_usd` | Required on `limit` and `stop_limit`, refused on the others. |
| `stop_price_micro_usd` | Required on `stop` and `stop_limit`, refused on the others. |
| `extended_hours` | Optional; allow a fill outside regular hours. |
| `client_order_id` | Optional, up to 128 characters. |

Answers `201` with the `trading_order`. The request's `Idempotency-Key` becomes the order's
`client_order_id` unless the body names one, so a retry with the same key cannot place twice; a
request with neither carries no key. A call with this route is the caller's own decision — it is not
an approval card; an [agent's order](/docs/identity/trading#agent-tools) asks a person by default, and on
`live` always. Venue rules — a minimum notional, which
`time_in_force` a coin accepts — are the brokerage's: its refusal comes back as `validation_failed`
or `forbidden` with its reason.

## Cancel an order

`DELETE /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/orders/{order_id}?env=` — scope `billing:write`

Answers `{ "id": "…", "object": "trading_order", "deleted": true }`. The brokerage cancels
asynchronously: read the order for its final status.

## Close a position

`POST /v1/identities/{identity}/trading/positions/{symbol}/close` — scope `billing:write`

```json theme={"system"}
{ "env": "paper", "percentage": "50" }
```

At most one of `qty` or `percentage` (a decimal string, greater than 0 and at most 100); neither closes
the whole position. Answers the closing `trading_order`. Use the position's own symbol (`BTCUSD`).

## Errors

All codes are the [standard ones](/docs/api/errors).

| Code | When |
| - | - |
| `feature_not_configured` (501) | This deployment has no brokerage app. |
| `state_conflict` (409) | No `active` connection for that identity and env — connect first; the brokerage revoked access ("reconnect required"), which marks the connection `expired`; or the connection changed (a disconnect or a newer connect) while an authorization was being completed — connect again. |
| `validation_failed` (400) | A malformed body, both envs connected with no `env`, or the brokerage refused the request (its reason, shortened). |
| `forbidden` (403) | The key lacks `billing:write`; a `live` connect, completion, order, cancel or close was made without a live `sk_live_` key; or the brokerage refused on an account rule. The connection stays `active`. |
| `not_found` (404) | No such identity in this organization, no such order at the brokerage, or an authorization `state` that is unknown, already used, or from another organization. |
| `rate_limited` (429) / `provider_error` (502) | The brokerage is busy or did not answer, or the stored credential could not be used here (nothing was sent, and the connection is left as it is); retry later. |

## Audit

Connect started, connected, disconnected, order placed, order canceled and position closed each
write an [audit log](/docs/api/audit-logs) entry (`trading_connection.connect_started`,
`trading_connection.connected`, `trading_connection.disconnected`, `trading_order.placed`,
`trading_order.canceled`, `trading_position.closed`). Each names the env; an order entry also names the
symbol, side, type and size, and a close names the symbol and the amount. No entry carries a token, an
envelope or an authorization `state`.


# Vaults
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/vaults

Write-only credential storage, injected at the network boundary — values are never returned.

> [!NOTE]
>
> See the [Credential vault](/docs/identity/vault) guide for the injection model.

A vault holds credentials an agent needs but must never see. Secret values are **write-only**: they are accepted on create, injected at runtime, and **never returned** by any read.

## The vault object

**id** `string`

Unique id (e.g. `vlt_01H...`).

**object** `string`

Always `vault`.

**identity\_id** `string | null`

The [identity](/docs/api/identities) the vault belongs to, or `null` when it was created without one.

**display\_name** `string`

Human-readable name.

**credential\_count** `integer`

How many credentials it holds. The metadata itself comes from `GET /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials` — a vault read never embeds it.

**created\_at** `string`

Creation timestamp.

## Create a vault

`POST /v1/vaults` — scope `admin`

**display\_name** `string` *required*

Human-readable name.

**identity\_id** `string`

The identity that owns the vault, by `idn_` id or by name. Defaults to `null` (org-wide). One that is not an identity in your organization answers `404 not_found`.

## Add a credential

`POST /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials`

**kind** `string` *required*

`static_bearer` or `mcp_oauth`. **`env_var` is not available: it is refused with `501 feature_not_configured`** —
substituting it needs an egress boundary on the sandbox's network path, and storing a secret under a
guarantee that cannot be kept is worse than refusing it. Use an MCP kind, which is injected before the
sandbox sees the value.

**key** `string` *required*

The reference name — for `env_var`, the environment variable name (e.g. `PAYMENTS_API_KEY`).

**host** `string`

Only read for `env_var` (not available) — the one exact destination host the value would be substituted for.

**mcp\_server\_url** `string`

Required for `static_bearer` and `mcp_oauth` — the server URL the token is matched to.

**agent\_id** `string`

The one agent the token may be injected into. An id that names no agent answers `404 not_found`. Omitted, any agent that declares `mcp_server_url` receives it. Fixed at create, like every other field: to re-bind, create a new credential and delete the old one.

**value** `string` *required*

The secret. **Write-only** — accepted here and never returned by any endpoint.

**expires\_at** `string`

Optional expiry, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset. It must be in the future: a past one answers `400 validation_failed`. It is returned in UTC.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/vaults/vlt_01H.../credentials \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "kind": "mcp_oauth",
    "key": "Payments MCP",
    "mcp_server_url": "https://mcp.example.com/sse",
    "value": "••••••••"
  }'
```

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "vcr_01H9CD...",
  "object": "vault_credential",
  "vault_id": "vlt_01H...",
  "kind": "mcp_oauth",
  "key": "Payments MCP",
  "host": null,
  "mcp_server_url": "https://mcp.example.com/sse",
  "agent_id": null,
  "placeholder_ref": "vetta_ref_9f2c...",
  "expires_at": null,
  "last_injected_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Reads never include secret values. `GET` on a credential returns only metadata — `kind`, `key`, `host`, `mcp_server_url`, `agent_id`, `placeholder_ref`, `expires_at`, `last_injected_at`, `created_at`. There is no reveal route and no update route: rotation is create-new then delete-old.

## How injection works

* **`env_var`** — *not available on this deployment.* The design is an opaque placeholder in the sandbox with the real value substituted at the [egress boundary](/docs/computer/networking#egress-pinning-coming-soon); that boundary does not exist yet, so the route refuses the kind rather than storing a secret it cannot protect.
* **`static_bearer` / `mcp_oauth`** — injected server-side when the agent connects to the matching [MCP server](/docs/capabilities/tools#mcp-connector) URL. Matching is by URL: a credential is injected when its `mcp_server_url` equals one of the agent version's `mcp_servers[].url`. A credential with an `agent_id` is injected into that agent's sessions only. A credential for this platform's own `/v1/mcp` is never injected: bound to an agent under the key `ceo_<agent id>` in the vault named "Orchestrator control plane", it records that agent as your organization's CEO (`ceo_agent_id`), which gets a short-lived credential for each turn holding only what the people driving it may do. Only that one agent gets it: if you bound this URL to an agent under another key or vault name, bind it again as `ceo_<agent id>` in "Orchestrator control plane" (a company with exactly one such agent had it recorded for it when this shipped). There is no per-session credential selection.
* **A bound agent is an admin's to change.** Once a credential is bound to an agent, `PATCH`, rollback and `DELETE` on that agent need the `admin` scope. Without it they answer `403 forbidden`. A session, schedule or team roster pinned to a version older than the binding runs without the credential, unless that version is still the agent's current one.

At rest, each value is protected with envelope encryption: a per-record data key (AES-256-GCM) wrapped by a managed key service and bound to the organization and identity.

## Scopes

| Route | Scope |
| - | - |
| `POST /v1/vaults` | `admin` |
| `GET /v1/vaults` · `GET /v1/vaults/{id}` | `agents:read` |
| `DELETE /v1/vaults/{id}` | `admin` |
| `POST /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials` | `admin` |
| `GET /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials` | `agents:read` |
| `DELETE /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials/{cid}` | `admin` |

Writing a secret is an `admin` act; listing what exists is not. That split lets an agent-facing key confirm a credential is present without ever being able to add or remove one.

## Retrieve a vault

`GET /v1/vaults/{id}` — scope `agents:read`. Returns the vault object with `credential_count`. Metadata only, like every other read here — no secret value is reachable through this or any route.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "vlt_01H...",
  "object": "vault",
  "identity_id": "idn_01H...",
  "display_name": "payments",
  "credential_count": 3,
  "created_at": "2026-08-20T17:00:00Z"
}
```

## List vaults & credentials

```bash theme={"system"}
GET /v1/vaults                      # list vaults (cursor-paginated)
GET /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials     # list credential metadata (cursor-paginated)
```

Both accept `limit` and `after`. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

## Delete

```bash theme={"system"}
DELETE /v1/vaults/{id}                       # delete the vault
DELETE /v1/vaults/{id}/credentials/{cid}     # remove one credential
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deleting a vault **soft-deletes the record and hard-deletes its secrets**. The credential values are destroyed, not archived — this cannot be undone, and any agent that was relying on injection from this vault starts failing at the egress boundary on its next call.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{ "id": "vlt_01H...", "object": "vault", "deleted": true }
```

### Rotating a credential

There is no update route for a credential, and that is the contract rather than an omission. Rotate by **adding the new secret and then deleting the old one** — two records, two ids. That keeps `last_injected_at` attributable to exactly one secret, so an audit can still answer which value was in use at the moment of a given call.

> [card] [Back to core resources](/docs/api/agents)
>
> The Phase 1 resource set.


# Video
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/video

Generate video over REST — a queued job you read back, with the finished file on it.

A video renders for minutes, so `POST /v1/media/videos` does not wait: it answers `202` with a **media job** in `queued`, and you read the job back until it is `completed` or `failed`. The finished clip is a [file](/docs/api/files). Images are the synchronous case — see [Images](/docs/api/images). The same job is what an agent's [`generate_video`](#in-a-session) tool submits; the [catalogue](/docs/api/media) is shared, and it is its own — a video model is never an agent's [`model`](/docs/concepts/model-router).

## The media job object

**id** `string`

`med_…`.

**object** `string`

Always `media_job`.

**kind** `string`

`video`. Other async media kinds share the object and the routes below.

**status** `string`

`queued` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`.

**model** `string | null`

The model rendering it.

**input** `object`

The request as accepted.

**result** `object | null`

On `completed`: `{ files: [{ file_id, content_type, width, height, duration_seconds }] }`. Dimensions are `null` where the model did not report them.

**error** `object | null`

On `failed`: `{ code, message }` — the reason, safe to repeat, so a refusal and an outage read differently.

**cost\_micro\_usd** `integer | null`

What was debited, in integer micro-USD, once the job finished: `null` while it runs, `0` on a failure — a job that fails is not billed.

**session\_id** `string | null`

The session whose agent submitted it; `null` for a job submitted through this API.

**created\_at** `string`

Submission time.

**completed\_at** `string | null`

When it reached a terminal status.

## Generate a video

`POST /v1/media/videos` → `202 Accepted` — scope `agents:write`, [`Idempotency-Key`](/docs/api/overview#idempotency) **required**.

**model** `string`

A model id from [`GET /v1/media/models?kind=video`](/docs/api/media#search-models). Omitted, the first of the platform's video defaults — the standard video model, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-max`, `minimax/hailuo-3`, `bytedance/seedance-2.5`, then `alibaba/wan-3.0/text-to-video` — that this deploy's catalogue publishes (not every deploy publishes the first; the job's `model` names the one that ran); for an edit (`video_url`), only one the catalogue says takes a video. Otherwise the request is refused and you name one.

**prompt** `string` *required*

What to render.

**image\_urls** `string[]`

One image, used as the **first frame** the video animates from: a stored image's `fil_` id — say a still [rendered as a character](/docs/api/characters#rendering-as-a-character) — or a public `http(s)` URL. A `fil_` this organization does not hold is `not_found`; one that is not an image, a private or loopback host, and a `data:` or `file:` URL are `validation_failed`. The job's `input` keeps the `fil_` you sent.

**character** `string`

Put a trained [character](/docs/api/characters) on video, by `chr_` id or name. It must be `ready`, and `image_urls` must be one `fil_` still this organization rendered as that character — anything else is `validation_failed` — because the face on screen is the still's. Only a model whose catalogue entry says it animates a still is used; a named one that does not is `validation_failed`. The character is recorded on the job, never sent to the model.

**seconds** `integer`

Target duration, 1–60. Models honour it as they can — each renders a set of lengths of its own, and clamps to what it supports.

**aspect\_ratio** `string`

Such as `16:9` or `9:16`. On a model that publishes the ratios it takes, one it does not is clamped to the nearest it does. Anything that is not `W:H` in whole numbers, or is wider than `8:1` or taller than `1:8` (no model takes more), is refused with `validation_failed` on `aspect_ratio` before anything renders or is billed.

**seed** `integer`

Repeat an earlier result, on models that honour a seed.

**The default model, the standard video model,** renders 5 to 15 seconds (a shorter or longer `seconds` is clamped into that) at 768p, always with **audio generated with the picture** — speech written into the prompt is spoken. It starts from a first frame or from the prompt alone, and edits no clip: an edit (`video_url`) goes to the next default that takes one. It is priced **$0.036 per generated second**, so a 5-second clip costs $0.18 and a 10-second one $0.36. Where it is not published, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-max` is next: 5 to 20 seconds at 720p with audio, at `21:9`, `2:1`, `16:9`, `4:3`, `1:1`, `3:4` or `9:16`, **$0.0425 per second until 7 November 2026 (00:00 UTC), then \$0.17 per second**. The price is the one in force when the job is submitted.

That is the whole request. A model priced per generated second renders at its own listed resolution, 720p for most. Not on it today: a `resolution` or `size`, a **last** frame, style or subject reference images beyond the first frame, an audio on/off switch, a completion callback URL, and any per-model or per-provider passthrough. A body that carries one of them is `validation_failed`, not quietly dropped. Completion is read by polling the job or, for an agent's job, from the session's events; a job submitted here does not fire a [webhook](/docs/api/webhooks) — [clip jobs](/docs/api/clips) do, video jobs do not yet.

```bash cURL theme={"system"}
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/media/videos \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "idempotency-key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1", "prompt": "waves at dusk, slow pan", "seconds": 4 }'
```

```ts SDK theme={"system"}
let job = await client.media.videos.generate({ model: "heygen/heygen-video-1", prompt: "waves at dusk", seconds: 4 });
while (job.status === "queued" || job.status === "processing") {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5_000));
  job = await client.media.get(job.id);
}
```

```bash CLI theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind video --model heygen/heygen-video-1 --prompt "waves at dusk" --seconds 4
naive media show med_01J...
```

```json 202 Accepted theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01J...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "video",
  "status": "queued",
  "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1",
  "input": { "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1", "prompt": "waves at dusk, slow pan", "seconds": 4 },
  "result": null,
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": null,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": null
}
```

## Retrieve a job

`GET /v1/media/{id}` → `200 OK` — scope `agents:read`. Poll it; a job left rendering for over thirty minutes is failed and not billed. Any `med_` reads here, a [clip job](/docs/api/clips) included — the same object `GET /v1/media/clips/{id}` answers.

```json Response theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01J...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "video",
  "status": "completed",
  "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1",
  "input": { "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1", "prompt": "waves at dusk, slow pan", "seconds": 4 },
  "result": {
    "files": [
      { "file_id": "fil_01J...", "content_type": "video/mp4", "width": null, "height": null, "duration_seconds": null }
    ]
  },
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": 412000,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-09-06T12:03:41.000Z"
}
```

Read the clip with [`GET /v1/files/{file_id}?download=true`](/docs/api/files#retrieve-a-file). The file carries `source.type = video_generation` and `source.job_id` = this job.

A job an agent submitted with `generate_video` carries its `session_id`, and that session's [event stream](/docs/api/events#event-types) announces it: `media.job.queued`, then `media.job.completed` or `media.job.failed`. A job submitted here has no session, so poll it.

## List jobs

`GET /v1/media` → `200 OK`, cursor-paginated — scope `agents:read`. See [Pagination](/docs/api/pagination).

**kind** `string`

`video` (or another async kind).

**status** `string`

`queued`, `processing`, `completed` or `failed`.

**session\_id** `string`

Jobs an agent submitted from one session.

**limit** `number`

Page size, 1–100.
