```
error: subscription_required: this organization has no active plan. Start or renew it with `POST /v1/credits/subscription` and follow `action_url`; the organization can be used again as soon as the payment is confirmed. (req_9k2m4p7q1w8x3v6z0b5n2c4t8r)
fix it with: naive plan subscribe
```

The first line is unchanged and still leads with the `code`, so `case` statements that branch on it keep working; the remedy is a second line on stderr. Exit code is `1` — see [exit codes](/docs/cli/sessions#run-exit-codes).

## The balance

What the plan does *not* cover: every token an agent spends is debited from the prepaid balance below. `insufficient_credits` (402) means top up; `subscription_required` (402) means the plan above.

### show

```bash theme={"system"}
naive credits show
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "credit_balance",
  "balance_micro_usd": 79416537,
  "mode": "test"
}
```

`mode` is `test` for an `sk_test_…` credential and `live` for `sk_live_…`. A test-mode balance is not real money.

### topup

```bash theme={"system"}
naive credits topup --usd 50
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--usd` | Amount as a decimal-dollar string (required). |

> [!WARNING]
>
> `topup` opens a hosted checkout and credits **nothing** by itself. Only the verified payment callback moves money, so the balance does not change the moment this command returns. Poll `naive credits show` if you need to wait for it to land.

### ledger

```bash theme={"system"}
naive credits ledger --limit 2
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "led_35cwx4557pj3sr9wrsgbfnx7f3",
      "type": "debit",
      "amount_micro_usd": -124,
      "balance_after_micro_usd": 79416537,
      "actor": { "type": "key", "id": "key_5d50bxwbje7b5n4a8gpkpfak38" },
      "session_id": "ses_xq5542edbac2dssv3gm6atdcr8",
      "agent_id": "agt_kt88353jaw132sjakt4sytz4a6",
      "deployment_id": null,
      "line_items": [
        { "tier": "input", "amount_micro_usd": -114 },
        { "tier": "cache_write", "amount_micro_usd": 0 },
        { "tier": "cache_read", "amount_micro_usd": 0 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "led_..."
}
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--type` | `debit` \| `credit`. |
| `--session` | Attribute to one session. |
| `--agent` | Attribute to one agent. |
| `--deployment` | Attribute to one deployment. |
| `--from` / `--to` | ISO-8601 date bounds. |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

Each entry carries full attribution and a `line_items` breakdown by pricing tier, so a charge can always be traced to the run that caused it.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive credits ledger --agent agt_kt88353jaw132sjakt4sytz4a6 --from 2026-08-01 --human
```

### spend

```bash theme={"system"}
naive credits spend --from 2026-08-01
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "spent_micro_usd": 41873200,
  "by_tier": { "input": 30112000, "output": 9861200, "computer": 1900000 },
  "by_agent": [{ "agent_id": "agt_kt88353jaw132sjakt4sytz4a6", "spent_micro_usd": 41873200 }],
  "by_session": [{ "session_id": "ses_xq5542edbac2dssv3gm6atdcr8", "spent_micro_usd": 12004100 }]
}
```

What every matching charge spent, summed by the server: the total, by tier, and the 50 dearest agents and sessions. It takes the ledger's `--session`, `--agent`, `--deployment`, `--from` and `--to`. `--days 14` (alone) adds the company's spend per day, on `--timezone` or the company's clock. Use it for a total: adding up a page of `ledger` misses every charge past that page.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Money is exact.** `--usd` takes a decimal-dollar string and is converted client-side to integer micro-USD. JSON output amounts are integer `*_micro_usd` (`1 USD = 1_000_000` micro-USD) so a script's arithmetic never rounds; `--human` renders dollars for reading.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A misspelled filter cannot silently widen a money query. `naive credits ledger --sesion ses_…` exits `2` and lists the flags the command does take, rather than answering with the whole org's ledger.


# naive board
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/board

Read and move cards on a team's shared board from a terminal.

The [team board](/docs/team/board) is the durable half of a [team](/docs/team/overview): a coordinator's transcript scrolls away, the card that says who holds what does not. These commands read and move cards on it.

`<board>` is a `brd_` id, or the `agt_` id — or the name — of the agent that owns the board. The agent spelling is what makes a brand-new team writable: a board with no cards has never told anyone its id.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive board create <board>` | Ensure the agent's board, and print it. |
| `naive board show <board>` | The whole board, in column order. |
| `naive board get <board>` | The board itself: its id, its owner, and its per-column counts. |
| `naive board card <board> <card-id>` | One card, in full. |
| `naive board add <board>` | Add a card. |
| `naive board assign <board> <card-id> <name>` | Hand a card to a teammate, which starts them on it. |
| `naive board move <board> <card-id>` | Retitle, move, assign or block a card. |
| `naive board comments <board> <card-id>` | Read a card's comments, oldest first. |
| `naive board comment <board> <card-id>` | Comment on a card. |
| `naive board done <board> <card-id>` | Mark a card `done`, with the note a `done` needs. |

## create

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board create research-lead
```

Prints the board object: its `brd_` id, the agent that owns it, and how many cards stand in each of the four columns. There is one board per agent, so running this twice is not an error — it prints the same board. You do not have to run it at all: the first `naive board add` mints the board too.

## show

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board show research-lead
naive board show research-lead --status blocked
naive board show research-lead --limit 20
```

Cards come back in column order — `todo`, `doing`, `blocked`, `done` — then oldest first. `--status` narrows to one column.

**The default is the whole board.** The command walks every page, so `--status done` answers for the board and not for a first page of it — which matters because the cards are sorted by column *before* they are paginated: a single page is the first columns and nothing after them, so a truncated read empties the last column rather than the end of a list.

`--limit` (1–100) and `--after` are there for a caller that wants one page at a time. Naming either takes exactly that page and prints `has_more` with the `next_cursor` to pass to the next `--after`.

With `--human` each row shows the card's id, status, title, `assignee`, `blocked_by` and `woken_session_id` — the `ses_` id of the session the board started for the assignee, or `-` if nothing has been woken for it yet. `--json` prints every card in full, including `reported_status`: the terminal state the owner was last told about, or `null` while the report is still owed.

## add

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board add research-lead \
  --title "Verify the Q3 numbers" \
  --assignee fact-checker \
  --status todo
```

Only `--title` is required; a card defaults to `todo`, unassigned and unblocked. `--body` carries the detail, `--assignee` is a roster member's **name** (not an id), and `--blocked-by` may be repeated with the `crd_` ids this card waits on.

`--key` (up to 128 characters) makes the add idempotent: the same key on the same board always answers the same card, so a seed script can be re-run without doubling the board. The first run mints the card; a repeat prints the card that already exists. Without a key every `add` is a new card.

Adding with `--assignee` is a hand-over too — see `assign` for what that starts.

## assign

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board assign research-lead crd_8k12… fact-checker
naive board assign --none research-lead crd_8k12…
```

Hands the card to a roster member by **name**. This is how work starts: a `todo` card with an assignee and no open blocker starts a session of that teammate at once (a busy teammate takes it after its current card), and the card records it as `woken_session_id`. If that session ends without the card reaching `done`, the board parks the card as `blocked` so the hand-over is never silently lost.

`--none` takes the card back and starts nobody. A name and `--none` together exit `2`.

## move

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board move research-lead crd_8k12… --status doing --assignee web-researcher
naive board move research-lead crd_8k12… --title "Verify the Q4 numbers"
```

Pass only what changes. `--assignee ""` unclaims the card; omitting a flag leaves that field alone.

`move` is the whole `PATCH`, so it also carries `--title` and `--body`. That is not a stretch of the name: it has always carried `--assignee` and `--blocked-by`, neither of which is a move across columns either, and there is one route here — a second editing verb over the same `PATCH` would leave you guessing which to reach for. `assign` and `done` sit beside it not as edits but as the two things a person says to a board.

`--status done` is refused with `missing_note` unless the card already carries a note: use `done --note`.

## get

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board get research-lead
```

The board object — its `brd_` id, the agent that owns it, and how many cards stand in each of the four columns. `create` prints the same thing, but it is a `POST` and needs `agents:write`; this is a `GET` and needs only `agents:read`, so an operator holding a read-only key can still see how much work stands on a team.

`get` takes a board. `card` takes a card. They are told apart by their names, not by how many arguments you passed.

## card

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board card research-lead crd_8k12…
```

One card, in full. `show` lists the board; this reads a single card by its `crd_` id.

## comments

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board comments research-lead crd_8k12…
```

The card's comments, oldest first — the hand-off notes a team leaves each other. `show` lists cards without them, so this is the only way to read a card's conversation from a terminal.

## comment

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board comment research-lead crd_8k12… --body "The Q3 figure is stale."
```

There is no `--author`. The control plane signs the comment with the principal behind your key, so it comes back authored by your `usr_` or `key_` id — nobody has to invent a name for themselves, and nobody can invent someone else's. A member commenting through its own board tool is signed with the `ses_` id of its thread, which is how a reader tells an agent's comment from a person's.

## done

```bash theme={"system"}
naive board done research-lead crd_8k12… --note "Figures verified; report is in /q3/summary.md"
```

Marks the card `done`, which is the documented terminal state. A `done` needs a note — the sentence that tells the owner what was finished and where it is — and `--note` is that note; it lands as the card's `note`, beside the brief, which is left alone. Without one the control plane refuses with `409 state_conflict` (`missing_note`), and the terminal prints that message; a card whose note already says enough may be closed without `--note`. **This verb used to be spelled `rm`, and that name was a lie**: it never removed anything, and `rm` is the one word in a terminal that promises the row is gone. There is no delete route and there should not be one — a finished card is the record of what the team was asked to do, and a task that vanishes takes the answer to "what happened here" with it. So the verb was renamed to what it does. `naive board rm` is no longer a command and exits `2`.


# naive browser
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/browser

Drive a computer's browser from the terminal, and manage the saved logins that outlive a session.

Two spellings, one surface. `naive computer browser <id> <verb>` drives the browser on a
[computer](/docs/cli/computer); `naive browser …` holds what outlives the session — saved logins and who
may reopen them. Options, guards and lifetime: the [Browser](/docs/computer/browser) guide.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive computer browser <id> goto <url>` | Navigate. |
| `naive computer browser <id> click <selector>` | Click a CSS selector. |
| `naive computer browser <id> type <selector> <text>` | Type into a CSS selector. Credential-shaped text is refused. |
| `naive computer browser <id> act <instruction>` | Do something described in words; `--var k=v` fills `%k%`. |
| `naive computer browser <id> extract [instruction]` | Read the page, a selector, or data shaped to `--schema`. |
| `naive computer browser <id> observe <instruction>` | List the elements that match a description. |
| `naive computer browser <id> links` | List the page's links. |
| `naive computer browser <id> screenshot` | Capture a PNG; prints the `fil_` id. |
| `naive computer browser <id> status` | The open session, or `not_found`. |
| `naive computer browser <id> close` | Close the session. Idempotent. |
| `naive computer browser <id> save-context` | Save the open session's login under a name. |
| `naive browser login <id>` | Sign in from the identity's saved credential. |
| `naive browser signup <id>` | Register with a generated password and save it. |
| `naive browser credential save` | Seal a login credential into an identity's vault. |
| `naive browser context grant <name>` | Let an agent or role reopen a saved login. |
| `naive browser context revoke <name>` | Delete a saved login and its grants. |

## Attach a browser

`naive computer create` takes the full option object; `--browser` attaches one on the open web and `--allowed-domains` attaches and scopes it.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer create --name box --allowed-domains "app.example.com,*.example.com" \
  --timeout-minutes 20 --region eu-central --allow-writes --viewport 1280x720
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--allowed-domains` | Comma-separated domains, or `*`. Optional — the open web by default. |
| `--timeout-minutes` | 1–360, default 15. |
| `--region` | `us-west` (default), `us-east`, `eu-central`, `ap-southeast`. |
| `--viewport` | `<width>x<height>` in pixels. |
| `--os` | `windows`, `mac`, `linux`, `mobile`, `tablet`. |
| `--keep-alive`, `--block-ads`, `--stealth`, `--proxy` | Switches; all default off. `--proxy` needs a bounded allow-list, not `*`. |
| `--no-solve-captchas` | CAPTCHA solving is on by default; this turns it off. |
| `--allow-writes` | Permit write-looking `act`, `click` and `type`. |
| `--allow-extract` | Permit `extract`, `observe` and `screenshot` on a reopened saved login. |
| `--context-name` | Reopen a saved login by name. Needs a grant. |
| `--persist-context` | Write cookies back to `--context-name` at close. |
| `--human-login` | Start a human-first login; holds the saved login for 15 minutes until `save-context`. |

## Drive it

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer browser cmp_01H... goto https://app.example.com/
naive computer browser cmp_01H... act "search for %term%" --var term=naive
naive computer browser cmp_01H... extract "the product names and prices" --schema '{"type":"object"}'
naive computer browser cmp_01H... extract --selector "table.prices"
naive computer browser cmp_01H... links --contains docs --limit 20
naive computer browser cmp_01H... screenshot
naive computer browser cmp_01H... close
```

Every verb prints one `browser_action` (JSON by default, `--human` for a table). `--var` repeats;
its values are sent once and never appear in the result. `extract` takes `--selector` and
`--schema` (a JSON object); `links` takes `--contains` and `--limit`.

## Saved logins

Save a credential first — the password comes from **stdin**, so it is never in your shell history
or the process list. `--password` exists for CI, and `--username` sets the name typed into the login form when it is not the email (it defaults to `--email`).

```bash theme={"system"}
printf '%s' "$FIGMA_PASSWORD" | naive browser credential save \
  --identity idn_01H... --service figma.com --email ada@example.com
```

Then sign in on a computer, save the login, and grant it:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive browser login cmp_01H... --service figma.com --url https://figma.com/login --identity idn_01H...
naive computer browser cmp_01H... save-context --name figma --identity idn_01H... --service figma.com
naive browser context grant figma --identity idn_01H... --agent agt_01H...
naive browser context grant figma --identity idn_01H... --role member
naive browser context revoke figma --identity idn_01H...
```

`grant` takes exactly one of `--agent <agt_…>` or `--role <owner|admin|member>`. `grant` and
`revoke` answer a signed-in dashboard session only; with an API key they exit with `forbidden`.

`signup` registers a new account with a generated password and seals it into the identity's vault:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive browser signup cmp_01H... --service figma.com --url https://figma.com/signup \
  --identity idn_01H... --email ada@example.com
```


# naive identity card
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/cards

Buy prepaid virtual cards for a persona, reveal their credentials, and log spend.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Not available yet.** Card issuing is not configured on the hosted service yet, so quoting, issuing, retrying and revealing a card answer `501 feature_not_configured` ("card issuing is not configured") and no credit moves. The reference below describes the surface for when issuing is turned on; do not build on it yet.

Cards belong to a [persona](/docs/cli/identity), so every command takes `--identity`. Reached as `naive identity card <command>` — three words, where `card` is a sub-group rather than a positional argument. See [Cards](/docs/identity/cards) for the model and the [Cards API](/docs/api/cards) for the wire shapes.

`--usd` takes a decimal such as `50` or `12.99`; the CLI converts once to the integer micro-USD the API speaks (`50` → `50000000`).

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity card list` | List the persona's cards (never a credential). |
| `naive identity card quote` | Price a load before buying. |
| `naive identity card issue` | Buy a prepaid card (debits credits); `--wait` for it to settle. |
| `naive identity card show` | Read one card. |
| `naive identity card reveal` | Reveal a card's number and PIN — audited; needs `--i-understand-this-is-audited`. |
| `naive identity card retry` | Re-run issuance for a failed card. |
| `naive identity card cancel` | Mark an active card cancelled. |
| `naive identity card refund` | Return the credits of a failed card. |
| `naive identity card transactions` | List a card's logged spend. |
| `naive identity card spend` | Log a spend against a card. |

`--identity` takes either an `idn_` id or the persona's name; the API resolves both. On a deployment with no card issuer bound, `quote`, `issue`, `retry` and `reveal` answer `501 feature_not_configured`. There is no assign/unassign: an agent whose session selects the persona holds its cards.

## list / quote / issue

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity card list --identity ava --status active
naive identity card quote --identity ava --usd 50
naive identity card issue --identity ava --label Ads --usd 50 --wait
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--status` | Filter `list`: `pending_payment`, `issuing`, `active`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `refunded`. |
| `--usd` | The load (required on `quote` and `issue`); the quote reports the allowed range and the price. |
| `--label` | A name for the card (required on `issue`). |
| `--wait` | On `issue`: poll the card once a second (up to 30 s) until it leaves `pending_payment` / `issuing`. |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

`issue` debits the quoted price from the organization's credits before anything is ordered; a short balance answers `402 insufficient_credits`. Without `--wait` the card is printed as issued — usually `issuing` — and `show` reads it again.

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "vcd_01j9x2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0v1w2",
  "object": "card",
  "status": "active",
  "label": "Ads",
  "brand": "Visa",
  "last4": "4242",
  "load_micro_usd": 50000000,
  "spent_micro_usd": 0,
  "…": "…"
}
```

## show / reveal / retry / cancel / refund

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity card show --identity ava --card vcd_…
naive identity card reveal --identity ava --card vcd_… --i-understand-this-is-audited
naive identity card retry --identity ava --card vcd_…
naive identity card cancel --identity ava --card vcd_…
naive identity card refund --identity ava --card vcd_…
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--card` | The `vcd_` id (required). |
| `--i-understand-this-is-audited` | Required on `reveal`; without it the command refuses before any request is made. |

`reveal` is the only command that prints a card number; every call is recorded as `card.credentials_revealed`, and a card that is not `active` answers `404 not_found`. A lifecycle action from the wrong status answers `state_conflict`. A prepaid card cannot be topped up — issue another.

## transactions / spend

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity card transactions --identity ava --card vcd_…
naive identity card spend --identity ava --card vcd_… --usd 12.99 --merchant "Example Ads" --description "Campaign #4"
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--card` | The `vcd_` id (required). |
| `--usd` | The amount spent (required on `spend`). |
| `--merchant` / `--description` | Optional context for the entry. |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

Logging a spend that would exceed the card's load is refused with `validation_failed`.


# naive character
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/character

Train a reusable on-screen persona from reference photos, check on it, list and delete it — then render images as it with naive media generate.

A **character** is a consistent on-screen persona — an AI influencer, a recurring host — trained once from a handful of reference photos and then pinned into every later image, so the same face carries across a whole channel. Training takes a few minutes: `create` answers at once with the character in `training`, and `get` is what you poll until it is `ready`. A character is addressed by its `chr_` id **or** its name. API detail: [Characters](/docs/api/characters).

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive character create --name <name> --image <ref> --consent` | Train a character. Paid; prints it in `training`. |
| `naive character get <id\|name>` | One character, its status advanced from the trainer. |
| `naive character list` | Your characters, newest first, then the prebuilt ones (`"prebuilt": true`). |
| `naive character update <id\|name>` | Change its name, description, persona or looks. Never its face. |
| `naive character delete <id\|name>` | Delete one and free its name. |

## create

```bash theme={"system"}
naive character create --name Ava --consent \
  --description "Late twenties, freckles, copper bob, oversized denim jacket" \
  --persona '{"niche":"Fashion · fit checks","voice":"Dry, quick, never salesy"}' \
  --style-pack "Phone snap" --style-pack "Quiet luxury" \
  --image ./ava-front.jpg --image ./ava-profile.jpg --image fil_01J9B...
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "chr_01J9CD...",
  "object": "character",
  "name": "Ava",
  "description": "Late twenties, freckles, copper bob, oversized denim jacket",
  "status": "training",
  "source_images": ["fil_01J9A...", "fil_01J9C...", "fil_01J9B..."],
  "thumbnail_url": null,
  "reason": null,
  "scope": "organization",
  "persona": { "niche": "Fashion · fit checks", "voice": "Dry, quick, never salesy" },
  "style_pack": ["Phone snap", "Quiet luxury"],
  "sheet": [],
  "metadata": {
    "consent": {
      "attested": true,
      "by": "key_01J8ZX...",
      "at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "statement": "I confirm the person in these photos is me, or has given me permission to create an AI likeness of them, and is not a public figure."
    }
  },
  "created_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-10-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--name` | **Required.** A short name unique among your characters, 1–100 characters. How you address it later. |
| `--description` | Who the character is — looks, age, vibe, wardrobe. Up to 1,024 characters. |
| `--image` | **Required**, repeat for one to sixteen photos of the *same* person. Each is a public `http(s)` URL, a stored `fil_` id, or a local `png`/`jpg`/`jpeg`/`webp`/`gif`/`heic` file — uploaded to [Files](/docs/cli/files) first and sent as its `fil_`. More, varied angles train a stronger likeness. |
| `--persona` | Who they are, as a JSON object of up to five lines of 500 characters: `niche`, `bio`, `voice`, `wardrobe`, `hooks` — read by your agents when they write as the character. |
| `--style-pack` | Repeat, one look name each (as [`--style`](/docs/cli/media#generate) takes them, up to 12): the looks the character is usually drawn in. |
| `--consent` | **Required.** You confirm the person in the photos is you, or has given you permission to create an AI likeness of them, and is not a public figure. Without it nothing is sent. The character keeps who confirmed it and when. |

Photos of a recognizable public figure are refused before anything is billed, with the reason.

A training is billed once, when the trainer accepts the photos; your balance must cover one first, else `insufficient_credits`. The CLI sends the required `Idempotency-Key` for you. Re-running the same command is refused before anything is trained, because the name is taken — delete the character first to train it again. See [Billing](/docs/api/characters#billing).

## get

```bash theme={"system"}
naive character get Ava | jq -r .status
```

Each read advances the status from the trainer: `training`, then `ready` or `failed` (with `reason`). Poll it until it is `ready`:

```bash theme={"system"}
until [ "$(naive character get Ava | jq -r .status)" != training ]; do sleep 20; done
```

## list

```bash theme={"system"}
naive character list --status ready
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--status` | `training`, `ready` or `failed`. |
| `--scope` | `organization` (yours) or `platform` (prebuilt: ready now, with a `persona` and the `style_pack` looks they are usually drawn in; they cannot be deleted). |
| `--limit` | Page size, 1–100. |
| `--after` | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |

## update

```bash theme={"system"}
naive character update Ava --persona '{"wardrobe":"Linen shirts and old denim"}'
```

Takes `--name`, `--description`, `--persona` and `--style-pack`. A persona is merged line by line, so the lines you leave out stay. A prebuilt character is refused.

## delete

```bash theme={"system"}
naive character delete Ava
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "id": "chr_01J9CD...", "object": "character", "deleted": true }
```

A soft delete: the character can no longer be rendered as, and its name is free for a new one. Images it already rendered keep their `source.character_id`.

## Rendering as a character

`--character` on [`naive media generate`](/docs/cli/media#generate) renders an image as a `ready` character. With `--image-url` naming a still of that character (its `fil_` id), it re-poses that still on the same set instead:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind image --character Ava \
  --prompt "Ava waves at the camera on a rooftop at golden hour" --aspect-ratio 9:16
```

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind image --character Ava --image-url fil_01J9... \
  --prompt "closer, she leans on the railing and laughs" --aspect-ratio 9:16
```

A character carries into video through that still: pass `--character` and the still's `fil_` id as the video's `--image-url` first frame. The first frame must be a still rendered as that character, or the call is refused, and only a model that animates a still is used:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind video --character Ava --image-url fil_01J9... --prompt "she waves, the camera pushes in slowly"
```

An agent does the same with the [`create_character` family of tools](/docs/capabilities/tools#characters); a character made here is one its sessions can render as.


# naive identity domain & email
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/comms

Connect sending domains and run a persona's inboxes.

Two sub-groups of [`naive identity`](/docs/cli/identity): **domains** are org-level (a domain is shared), **email inboxes** belong to a persona.

## naive identity domain

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity domain connect` | Register a domain for sending and receiving. |
| `naive identity domain quote` | Price a domain before buying it. |
| `naive identity domain purchase` | Buy a domain with credits, up to a maximum price. |
| `naive identity domain list` | List domains. |
| `naive identity domain show` | Show one domain. |
| `naive identity domain verify` | Re-check DNS and advance the status. |
| `naive identity domain records` | Print the DNS records you must publish. |
| `naive identity domain rm` | Remove a domain. |

Domains are **org-level** — there is no `--identity` flag on this sub-group.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity domain list --limit 2
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dom_8e9f4apc0281smp2hk7bww0x1j",
      "object": "domain",
      "name": "acme-mail.com",
      "kind": "external",
      "status": "active",
      "dns_status": "provisioned",
      "inbound_status": "failed",
      "app_connect_status": "pending",
      "records": [
        { "type": "TXT", "host": "…._domainkey", "value": "p=MIGfMA0…", "priority": null, "managed": true }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

The three status fields move independently, and that is the point — a domain can be sending (`dns_status: provisioned`) while inbound is still broken (`inbound_status: failed`). Read all three before assuming a domain is healthy.

| Command | Flags |
| - | - |
| `connect` | `--domain`, `--name`, `--kind`, `--receive` |
| `quote` | `--domain` |
| `purchase` | `--domain`, `--max-price-micro-usd` (required), `--receive` |
| `list` | `--limit`, `--after` |
| `show` / `verify` / `records` / `rm` | `--domain` |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity domain connect --domain acme-mail.com --kind external --receive
naive identity domain records --domain dom_...     # publish these, then:
naive identity domain verify --domain dom_...
```

`verify` is idempotent — run it as often as you like while DNS propagates.

## naive identity email

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity email provision` | Create an inbox on an active domain. |
| `naive identity email list` | List a persona's inboxes. |
| `naive identity email send` | Send mail as the persona. |
| `naive identity email messages` | List messages on a channel. |
| `naive identity email read` | Mark an arrived message read, or unread with `--unread`. |
| `naive identity email sent` | List what the persona sent, newest first. |
| `naive identity email update` | Turn whether mail wakes the inbox's agent on or off (`--wake on\|off`). |
| `naive identity email rm` | Remove an inbox. |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity email list --identity idn_6sc5s97c5jt1ds84qngajv659p
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "data": [], "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null }
```

| Command | Flags |
| - | - |
| `provision` | `--identity`, `--address`, `--domain`, `--agent` |
| `list` | `--identity`, `--limit` |
| `send` | `--identity`, `--inbox`, `--to`, `--subject`, `--text` (`--message` synonym) |
| `messages` | `--identity`, `--channel`, `--limit` |
| `read` | `--identity`, `--message`, `--unread` |
| `sent` | `--identity`, `--limit` |
| `rm` | `--identity`, `--inbox` |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity email provision --identity idn_... --address ava@acme-mail.com --agent agt_...
naive identity email send --identity idn_... --inbox eml_... \
  --to customer@example.com --subject "Your refund" --text "Processed today."
naive identity email messages --identity idn_... --channel email
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Outbound email depends on a configured comms provider.** Where one is not configured the send surface answers `501 feature_not_configured` and holds no rows to read. This is a deployment state, not a bug in your call — a persona read stays healthy either way, so `identity show` succeeding tells you nothing about whether `email send` will.
>
> Check by attempting one send in a test org rather than assuming; a `501` here is a platform configuration answer and no retry will change it.

Inbound continues to work whenever the domain's `inbound_status` is healthy, independently of the outbound path.


# naive computer
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/computer

Provision and control sandboxes.

Manage [computers](/docs/capabilities/computer) — disposable Linux sandboxes with an optional browser.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive computer create` | Create a computer. |
| `naive computer list` | List computers. |
| `naive computer show <id>` | Show a computer. |
| `naive computer exec <id>` | Run a shell command. |
| `naive computer pause <id>` | Pause the sandbox; it bills nothing while paused. Pausing a computer you created does not refund the rest of its paid 10-minute block, and any `exec` or `fs` call on it resumes it, so billing restarts. |
| `naive computer resume <id>` | Wake the sandbox. |
| `naive computer snapshot <id>` | Capture state to boot from later. |
| `naive computer snapshots` | List the organization's snapshots, newest first (`--limit`, `--after`). |
| `naive computer delete-snapshot <snapshot-id>` | Delete a snapshot. Refused while a live computer was restored from it. |
| `naive computer build-3d <id> <script.py> --engine <cad\|blender>` | Build, check and render a 3D model from a script. |
| `naive computer delete <id>` | Destroy the sandbox. |

## create

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer create --name box --vcpu 2 --memory-mb 4096 --browser --allowed-domains "*.example.com"
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--name` | Human-readable name. Optional; defaults to `computer`, and names need not be unique — commands take the `cmp_` id. |
| `--vcpu` | Provisioned vCPU, 1–16 (default 2). |
| `--memory-mb` | Provisioned memory in MiB, 128–65536 (default 4096). |
| `--disk-gb` | Root disk size in GiB (up to 100). |
| `--mode` | **Not accepted** — passing it is an unknown-flag error. Every computer is a micro-VM; an `isolate` mode is coming soon. |
| `--size` | Optional preset (`small` \| `medium` \| `large`). **Not available yet** — no preset is defined, so passing it is an error; set `--vcpu`, `--memory-mb` and `--disk-gb`. |
| `--browser` | Attach a managed browser. |
| `--allowed-domains` | Optional with `--browser`; comma-separated globs, or `*`. Absent, the open web. |
| `--snapshot <id>` | Boot from a snapshot. |

## exec, pause, resume, snapshot

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer exec cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7 -- "ls -la ~"
naive computer pause cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7
naive computer resume cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7
naive computer snapshot cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7
```

Snapshots take no `--name`: the call returns a `snapshot_id`, and that id is the handle you pass to
`naive computer create --snapshot`. Passing `--name` is a hard error, not an ignored flag.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer snapshots
naive computer delete-snapshot snp_0368aa449de84e308959ca72744a3bd5
```

> [!TIP]
>
> Computers pause automatically when the agent sleeps between turns, so you rarely pause manually. See [Runtime & durability](/docs/concepts/runtime).

## build-3d

Runs a [build123d](https://github.com/gumyr/build123d) (`cad`, millimetres) or Blender (`blender`, metres) script in the computer, checks the result, renders previews and publishes the exports as files. Same body and answer as [`POST /v1/computers/{id}/build-3d`](/docs/api/computers#build-a-3d-model).

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer build-3d cmp_01J... bracket.py --engine cad --name bracket --export step,stl --views iso,top --out ./bracket
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "ok": true,
  "files": [
    { "file_id": "fil_01J...", "name": "bracket.step", "content_type": "model/step", "bytes": 48211 },
    { "file_id": "fil_01K...", "name": "bracket.stl", "content_type": "model/stl", "bytes": 120884 }
  ],
  "previews": ["fil_01L...", "fil_01M..."],
  "checks": { "valid_solid": true, "watertight": true, "bbox_mm": [60, 40, 12], "volume_cm3": 14.2, "triangles": 2416 },
  "error": null,
  "log_tail": "",
  "compute_seconds": 6.4
}
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--engine` | **Required.** `cad` (the script assigns `result`, a build123d shape) or `blender` (the script builds the scene). |
| `--name` | Base name of the outputs, `[a-z0-9_-]`, up to 64. Defaults to the script's file name. |
| `--export` | Comma-separated: `step`, `stl`, `3mf`, `glb`, `obj`, `blend`. Default `step,stl` for `cad`, `glb` for `blender`. |
| `--views` | Comma-separated preview angles, up to 4: `iso`, `front`, `top`, `side`. Default `iso`. |
| `--size` | Preview size in pixels, 256–1024. Default 768. |
| `--timeout` | Seconds the script may run, 10–300. Default 120. |
| `--out` | Download the exports and previews into this directory. |

A script that fails answers `ok: false` with `error: { message, line }` and exits `1`. For `cad`, STEP, STL and 3MF are published only when the solid is valid and watertight. There is no fee of its own: the build is billed as the computer's running seconds.

## fs

One command covers the whole filesystem surface. The **operation comes first**, then the computer:
`naive computer fs <read|write|list|mkdir|remove> <computer-id> --path <path>`.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer fs list cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7 --path /home/naive
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "name": "notes.txt",
      "path": "/home/naive/notes.txt",
      "type": "file",
      "size_bytes": 6,
      "mode": 33188,
      "modified_at": "2026-11-05T14:02:10.000Z"
    },
    {
      "name": "project",
      "path": "/home/naive/project",
      "type": "directory",
      "size_bytes": 4096,
      "mode": 16877,
      "modified_at": "2026-11-05T13:58:41.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

`type` is `file`, `directory`, `symlink` or `other`; `mode` is the POSIX mode as an integer (`33188` is `0o100644`); `modified_at` is `null` when the filesystem does not report a time.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive computer fs read cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7 --path /home/naive/notes.txt
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "path": "/home/naive/notes.txt",
  "encoding": "text",
  "content": "hello\n"
}
```

`write` takes `--content`, and `--encoding base64` carries bytes that are not text. `remove` and
`mkdir` take only `--path`. Passing the computer id where the operation belongs is a usage error, not
a request:

```
usage: fs op must be read|write|list|mkdir|remove, got "cmp_01a02ad8ba0f7bd59115bfd513fc6ed7"
```


# naive data
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/data

Search the data catalogue in any of 18 domains, read a tool's input schema, and run it from the terminal.

The three [data routes](/docs/api/data) from the terminal. Search and describe are free; a run is priced at the tool's listed price. [`naive social-data`](/docs/cli/social-data) is the same catalogue's `social` domain.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive data search "<query>"` | Find tools. `--domain <domain>`, `--platform <network>`, `--limit <1-20>`. |
| `naive data describe <tool_id>` | A tool's input schema, price and notes. |
| `naive data run <tool_id>` | Run it; prints the run with its `data` and `cost_micro_usd`. |

`--domain` is one of `social`, `search`, `people`, `companies`, `compliance`, `funding`, `seo`, `finance`, `crypto`, `news`, `legal`, `weather`, `jobs`, `real_estate`, `reviews`, `trade`, `shopping`, `travel` ([what each covers](/docs/capabilities/data#domains)); any other value exits 2 before a request is sent. `--platform` narrows to one social network.

## run

Parameters go where the tool's `describe` output says:

| Flag | Goes to | Example |
| - | - | - |
| `--query key=value` | `query` (repeatable) | `--query symbol=AAPL` |
| `--path key=value` | `path` (repeatable) | `--path id=1234` |
| `--body '<json object>'` | `body` | `--body '{"location":"Austin, TX","maxItems":5}'` |

`key=value` is always text — a ZIP code stays a string. Use `key:=value` for a JSON value: `--query limit:=5`, `--query verified:=true`.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive data search "insider trades" --domain finance
naive data describe <tool_id>
naive data run <tool_id> --query symbol=AAPL
```

A failed run exits 0 and prints `status: "failed"` with its `error` and, normally, `cost_micro_usd: 0`. A refusal before the run (a balance below the tool's listed price, an unknown tool) exits non-zero with the error envelope.


# naive db
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/database

Work with a fullstack app's managed database from the terminal: SQL, tables, migrations.

Every `fullstack` [app](/docs/cli/apps) comes with a managed Postgres database. These commands reach it
without a connection string. API detail: [Database](/docs/api/database).

Every command takes an optional `--app <id-or-name>`. **Omit it when the organization has one
`fullstack` app** — that app is resolved for you. With several, the command fails with
`ambiguous_app` and lists the candidates; name one. With none, `not_found`: make one with
`naive app create <name> --type fullstack`.

`query` and `migrate` require the `agents:write` scope; `tables` and `migrations` require `agents:read`.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive db query "<sql>"` | Run SQL and print the rows. |
| `naive db tables` | List the database's tables with row and size estimates. |
| `naive db migrate <file.sql>` | Apply a SQL file as a named migration, once. |
| `naive db migrations` | List the migrations that have been applied. |

## query

```bash theme={"system"}
naive db query "select count(*) from todos"
naive db query "insert into todos (title) values ('ship it')" --app storefront
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "object": "app_db_result", "rows": [{ "count": 3 }], "row_count": 1 }
```

## tables

```bash theme={"system"}
naive db tables
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "data": [{ "object": "db_table", "name": "todos", "schema": "public", "rows": 3, "size_bytes": 16384 }] }
```

## migrate

```bash theme={"system"}
naive db migrate sql/0001_todos.sql
naive db migrate sql/0001_todos.sql --name todos --app storefront
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--name` | The migration's name. Defaults to the file's base name without its extension (`0001_todos`). |
| `--app` | The app whose database to migrate. |

A migration is applied **once per name**: re-running the command with the same file is a no-op that
prints the existing ledger row, and re-running it with a *changed* file under the same name fails
with `version_conflict` — write a new file instead. Names are lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`.

For an app a project declares, put the files in the declaration instead — `apps[].migrations` in
[`naive.config`](/docs/cli/naive#config-surface) applies them on every `naive up`.

## migrations

```bash theme={"system"}
naive db migrations
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "dbm_01H...",
      "object": "db_migration",
      "name": "0001_todos",
      "sha256": "9f86d081…",
      "applied_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z",
      "statements": 1
    }
  ]
}
```


# naive deploy & webhook
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/deployments

Schedule agents with cron and subscribe to events.

Manage [deployments](/docs/capabilities/deployments) (scheduled agents) and [webhooks](/docs/capabilities/webhooks) (event subscriptions).

## Deployments

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive deploy create` | Create a scheduled deployment. |
| `naive deploy list` | List deployments. |
| `naive deploy show <id>` | Show a deployment. |
| `naive deploy update <id>` | Change the schedule, prompt, budget, window, persona, or pinned version. |
| `naive deploy run <id>` | Fire once, now. |
| `naive deploy runs <id>` | List past runs. |
| `naive deploy pause <id>` | Pause the schedule. |
| `naive deploy resume <id>` | Resume the schedule. |
| `naive deploy delete <id>` | Delete the deployment. |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive deploy create --agent agt_01j8rk2vq6m4zx9kp7n3c5hwae \
  --cron "0 9 * * *" \
  --budget-usd 5 \
  --window priority \
  --agent-version 4 \
  --identity ava-sales \
  --prompt "Summarize what changed in main overnight."
naive deploy runs dep_01j8rs4vm6k2xq9zn3c7h5wtpb --human
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--agent` | Agent to run (required). |
| `--cron` | Cron expression (required), evaluated in `--timezone` — the organization's timezone when omitted, not UTC. |
| `--budget-usd` | Per-run budget ceiling (required). Decimal-dollar string → `cap_micro_usd` on the wire. |
| `--agent-version` | Pin runs to a specific agent version. Optional; defaults to the agent's `current_version`. |
| `--prompt` | Instruction sent to each scheduled session. |
| `--window` | Completion window for scheduled runs: `immediate` \| `priority` \| `loose`. |
| `--timezone` | IANA timezone the cron expression is evaluated in. Defaults to the organization's timezone. |
| `--on-idle` | An `https://` URL on a public host that is POSTed the `session.idle` webhook when a scheduled run goes idle. Setting it creates a signed [webhook endpoint](/docs/cli/webhook) listed by `naive webhook list`; rotate it to get the signing secret. |
| `--identity` | The [persona](/docs/identity/personas) each fire speaks as — an `idn_` id or its name. The agent must already hold a grant to it. Without one a scheduled run speaks as no persona. |

`update` takes the same flags as `create` except `--agent`; only the flags you pass are changed.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Pin `--agent-version` for a staged rollout or rollback: scheduled runs stay on that immutable config until you re-pin, instead of jumping to `current_version` on the next fire.

## Webhooks

Full reference: [`naive webhook`](/docs/cli/webhook).

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive webhook add` | Subscribe an endpoint to events. |
| `naive webhook list` | List webhooks. |
| `naive webhook show <id>` | Show a webhook endpoint. |
| `naive webhook update <id>` | Change `--url`/`--events`, or `--disable` / `--enable` the endpoint. |
| `naive webhook rotate <id>` | Rotate the signing secret with an overlap window. |
| `naive webhook deliveries <id>` | List delivery attempts (status, response code, retries). |
| `naive webhook delivery <id> <delivery>` | Show one delivery attempt. |
| `naive webhook redeliver <id> <delivery>` | Manually resend a past delivery. |
| `naive webhook rm <id>` | Remove a webhook. |
| `naive webhook test <id>` | Send a test delivery. |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive webhook add \
  --url https://example.com/hooks/naive \
  --events session.idle,message.completed,budget.exceeded
```

### Pause & update

Webhooks toggle with `enable`/`disable` (a config flag on the endpoint), distinct from deployment schedule `pause`/`resume`:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive webhook update whk_01H... --disable          # stop delivering; keep the endpoint
naive webhook update whk_01H... --enable
naive webhook update whk_01H... --events session.idle,session.usage
```

### Rotate the signing secret

```bash theme={"system"}
naive webhook rotate whk_01H... --overlap-hours 24
```

Returns a **new** secret (shown once). During the overlap window both the old and new secrets sign each delivery via a multi-signature `Vetta-Signature: v1=…,v1=…` header, so your verifier keeps accepting deliveries with zero drops. Update your stored secret, then let the old one expire. The SDK `unwrap` helper validates either signature automatically.

### Delivery log & redelivery

```bash theme={"system"}
naive webhook deliveries whk_01H... --human
naive webhook redeliver whk_01H... whd_01H...
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "whd_01H...",
  "event_id": "evt_01H...",
  "event_type": "session.idle",
  "status": "failed",
  "attempts": 3,
  "response_status": 500,
  "delivered_at": null,
  "next_retry_at": "2026-08-20T18:10:00Z"
}
```

See [Webhooks](/docs/capabilities/webhooks) for the signature scheme, retry/auto-disable policy, and payload shapes.


# naive file
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/files

Upload inputs for a session and download published outputs.

Manage [files](/docs/capabilities/files) — inputs you hand to a session, and outputs an agent publishes with `publish_file`. Files are org-scoped objects with a `fil_` id.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The group is **`file`**, singular — matching `agent`, `session`, and `webhook`. The delete verb is **`rm`**. Unknown commands are a hard error, so `naive files delete` exits `2` rather than deleting anything.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive file upload` | Upload a local file; returns a `fil_` id. |
| `naive file list` | List files in the org. |
| `naive file show <id>` | Show a file's metadata. |
| `naive file download <id>` | Write the file's bytes to stdout, unchanged. |
| `naive file publish <id>` | Promote a file to the `published` scope. |
| `naive file rm <id>…` | Delete a file, or up to 100 in one request. |
| `naive file update <id>` | Set a file's title, description or tags. |
| `naive file import <url>` | Fetch a public URL into the library, server-side. |
| `naive file move <id>…` | Put files in a folder, or rename, merge or empty a whole folder. |
| `naive file folders` | List every folder. |

## upload

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file upload --file ./contracts/order-4821.pdf
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--file` | Path to the local file (required). |
| `--name` | Override the stored name. Defaults to the basename. |
| `--scope` | File scope, e.g. `published`. |
| `--session` | Attach the upload to a session. |
| `--title` | A human title for the library. |
| `--description` | A longer, searchable description. |
| `--tag` | A label; repeat the flag or comma-separate (`--tag launch,web`). |
| `--folder` | Put the file in this folder. |

## list

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file list --limit 2
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "fil_h361txkmkapcpavpwfetebat9x",
      "object": "file",
      "name": "report.md",
      "content_type": "text/markdown",
      "size_bytes": 24,
      "scope": "published",
      "session_id": null,
      "sha256": "88cd3bcda30fee16ca4d9d7a7d43aa06123b0ca56409159e4b3364f229a9ae27",
      "created_at": "2026-08-22T23:56:39.813Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "fil_m7fjsd5hg5mt09sgaaya5m0hcb"
}
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--scope` | Filter by scope. |
| `--session` | Only files belonging to one session — this is how you list what a run produced. |
| `--kind` | `image`, `video`, `audio`, `document` or `other` — derived from the content type. Several, comma-separated: `--kind image,video`. |
| `--exclude-kind` | Leave these kinds out, comma-separated. |
| `--agent` | Only files an agent's sessions made (`agt_…`). |
| `--character` | Only what was rendered as one [character](/docs/cli/character) (`chr_…`): its stills and the clips made from them. |
| `--ids` | Exactly these files, comma-separated `fil_` ids. |
| `--order` | `desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc`. |
| `--source` | Provenance: `upload`, `url_import`, `image_generation`, `video_generation`, `video_clipping`, `screenshot` or `speech_generation`. |
| `--tag` | Only files carrying this tag. |
| `--search` | Case-insensitive match on the title, name or description. |
| `--folder` | Only files in this folder. Case does not matter. |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file list --kind image --tag launch --search hero
```

Every picture and clip one agent made, oldest first: `naive file list --kind image,video --agent agt_… --order asc`.

A `--kind`, `--exclude-kind`, `--source` or `--order` outside its list exits `2` before any request is sent. `sha256` is the content hash, so you can verify a download without a second request.

## update

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file update fil_... --title "Launch hero (final)" --tag launch --tag approved
naive file update fil_... --description ""     # an empty value clears the field
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--title` | Set the title; `""` clears it. |
| `--description` | Set the description; `""` clears it. |
| `--tag` | Replace the tags; repeat or comma-separate. |
| `--folder` | Move the file to this folder; `""` takes it out of its folder. |

Only the flags you pass change. The bytes, name and scope never do.

## import

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file import https://cdn.example.com/hero.png --title "Launch hero" --tag launch
```

The API fetches the URL itself — nothing is read from your machine — and stores a `published` file with `source.type: "url_import"`. Only public `http(s)` URLs are accepted, up to 25 MiB. The CLI sends an `Idempotency-Key` so a retried command returns the same file.

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--name` | The stored file name; the URL's last segment by default. |
| `--title` | A human title. |
| `--description` | A longer, searchable description. |
| `--tag` | Labels; repeat or comma-separate. |
| `--folder` | Put the file in this folder. |

## Folders

A folder is a name on a file. A file is in one folder or none, and folders do not nest. A name is 1–64 characters with no `/`. If a folder with the same name in another case exists, the file takes that folder's spelling. A file an agent writes with no folder lands in the folder of the last file its session filed.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file move fil_... fil_... --folder Launch        # put files in a folder
naive file move --from Launch --folder "Launch 2026"   # rename; a name in use merges the two
naive file move --from Launch --folder ""              # empty the folder; the files stay
naive file folders                                     # every folder, newest first
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--folder` | The folder to move to (required); `""` takes the files out of any folder. |
| `--from` | Move every file in this folder, instead of naming ids. |

Name up to 100 file ids, or `--from`, not both. `move` answers `{ object: "file_move", folder, file_ids }`. `folders` takes no flags and answers each folder's `name`, `file_count`, `newest_at`, `cover_file_ids` and `agent_id`. No file is ever deleted by a folder change.

## download

`download` writes the contents to **stdout**; there is no `--out` flag. Redirect it:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file download fil_h361txkmkapcpavpwfetebat9x > ./out/report.md
```

## publish & rm

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file publish fil_...     # promote to the published scope
naive file rm fil_...          # delete
naive file rm fil_... fil_...  # delete several in one request (POST /v1/files/delete), up to 100
```

`show`, `download`, `publish`, and `rm` take the file id as a positional argument and accept no flags. `rm` also takes several ids.

## What a run produced

There is no `naive session files` command. List a session's files by filtering this group:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive file list --session ses_xq5542edbac2dssv3gm6atdcr8
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Sessions are never deleted, but files that were never published live only on the agent's computer and go when the agent is deleted. Publish anything you need to keep — see [Files](/docs/capabilities/files).


# naive identity
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/identity

Personas, the agents that hold them, and OAuth connections.

A **persona** is a durable identity an agent can act as — with its own inboxes, phone numbers, connections, and [vault](/docs/cli/vault). Agents hold personas through a *grant*, not as a field on the agent.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity create` | Create a persona. |
| `naive identity list` | List personas. |
| `naive identity show <id>` | Show one persona. |
| `naive identity update <id>` | Update name or description. |
| `naive identity delete <id>` | Delete a persona. |
| `naive identity agents <id>` | List agents granted this persona. |
| `naive identity attach` | Grant a persona to an agent. |
| `naive identity detach` | Revoke the grant. |
| `naive identity connect` | Start an OAuth connection for a persona. |
| `naive identity disconnect` | Revoke a connection. |

Sub-groups have their own pages: [`identity domain` and `identity email`](/docs/cli/comms), [`identity phone`](/docs/cli/phone), and `identity connections` below.

## create, list, show, update, delete

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity create --name "Ava Sales" --description "Outbound SDR persona"
naive identity list --limit 2
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "idn_6sc5s97c5jt1ds84qngajv659p",
      "object": "identity",
      "name": "Ava Sales",
      "description": "Outbound SDR persona",
      "emails": [],
      "phones": [],
      "domains": [],
      "connections": [],
      "metadata": {},
      "created_at": "2026-08-22T23:47:54.081Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-08-22T23:47:54.081Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "idn_sxassvr215v63cx94nfx9nn3gx"
}
```

`create` and `update` take `--name` and `--description`. `show` and `delete` take the id positionally and accept no flags. The `emails`, `phones`, `domains`, and `connections` arrays are the persona's attached channels — populated by the sub-groups.

## Granting a persona to an agent

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity attach --agent agt_kt88353jaw132sjakt4sytz4a6 --identity idn_6sc5s97c5jt1ds84qngajv659p
naive identity detach --agent agt_... --identity idn_...
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--agent` | Agent id (required). |
| `--identity` | Persona id (required). |

The grant is a two-sided edge, so both sides are named on the command that makes it, and you can read it from either end:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity agents idn_...   # agents that hold this persona
naive agent identities agt_...  # personas this agent holds
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "data": [], "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null }
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> `--identity` on `naive agent create` is **not** supported and exits `2` with an explanation. A persona is granted with `naive identity attach`, never set as a field on the agent. `naive session create --identity …` *is* supported — that selects which already-granted persona a run acts as.

## Connections

An OAuth connection lets a persona act in a third-party tool.

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity connections apps` | Search the app catalogue. |
| `naive identity connections app` | Show one app: auth methods, default tools, what connecting will ask for. |
| `naive identity connect` | Start an OAuth flow for a persona. |
| `naive identity connections list` | List a persona's connections. |
| `naive identity connections show` | Show one connection. |
| `naive identity connections configs` | List the org's auth configs. |
| `naive identity connections config-add` | Register an auth config for a connector. |
| `naive identity connections config-rm` | Remove an auth config. |
| `naive identity disconnect` | Revoke a connection. |

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity connections configs
```

```json theme={"system"}
{ "data": [], "has_more": false, "next_cursor": null }
```

An **auth config** is org-level: it holds the OAuth client for one app, and every persona connects through it. **There is no list of supported apps** — `--connector` takes an app id out of the catalogue, so start by searching it:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity connections apps --search helpdesk
naive identity connections app zendesk
```

`app` is worth reading before `config-add`: it prints which auth methods work (`managed_oauth` needs no credentials of your own), the operations that get pinned by default, and any value connecting will still ask for — an account subdomain, a region. `--auth` takes one of `managed_oauth`, `oauth`, `api_key`; anything else exits `2` and lists the valid values. Register the config once, then connect each persona:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity connections config-add --connector zendesk --auth managed_oauth
naive identity connect --identity idn_... --auth-config ac_... --field subdomain=acme
naive identity connections show ca_...
naive identity connections list --identity idn_...
naive identity disconnect --connection ca_...
```

`connect` answers with a `connect_link`. Hand it to the person who owns the account; the connection stays `initiated` until they finish authorizing, and `connections show` is the poll that reconciles it — there is no webhook for this yet.

| Command | Flags |
| - | - |
| `connections apps` | `--search`, `--limit`, `--after` |
| `connections app` | `--app` (or a positional app id) |
| `connect` | `--identity`, `--auth-config`, `--field` (repeatable, `name=value`) |
| `connections list` | `--identity` |
| `connections show` | `--connection` |
| `connections config-add` | `--connector`, `--auth`, `--scope` (repeatable), `--tool` (repeatable), `--client-id` |
| `connections config-rm` | `--auth-config` |
| `disconnect` | `--connection` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `configs` returning an empty list means no app has been registered for this org yet — `connect` has nothing to connect *through* until `config-add` runs.


# naive keys
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/keys

Create, list, rotate, and revoke scoped API keys.

API keys are how CI and services authenticate. Each key carries an explicit scope list, so a deploy key need not be an admin key.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive keys create` | Mint a scoped key. The secret is shown once. |
| `naive keys list` | List keys — metadata only, never secrets. |
| `naive keys rotate <key-id>` | Mint a replacement secret for a key. |
| `naive keys revoke <key-id>` | Revoke a key immediately. |

## create

```bash theme={"system"}
naive keys create --name ci --scopes agents:write,sessions:write,billing:read
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--name` | Human-readable label (required). |
| `--scopes` | Comma-separated scope list (required). |

`--scopes` is validated client-side against the shared scope enum, so an unknown scope fails before the request is sent.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The `secret` in the `create` and `rotate` replies exists nowhere else. It is not stored in retrievable form and no route returns it again. Capture it now or mint another key.

## list

```bash theme={"system"}
naive keys list --limit 2
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "key_gwpjrs1egky00g6vw5gjczj6fs",
      "object": "api_key",
      "name": "ci",
      "prefix": "sk_test_pdme",
      "scopes": ["agents:write", "agents:read", "sessions:write", "billing:read"],
      "created_by": { "type": "key", "id": "key_66nnedy98yfx3ygzssfv99p7tf" },
      "last_used_at": null,
      "created_at": "2026-08-22T23:56:53.464Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "key_m3jjzgc4zsffsnqhvwwf28m9d1"
}
```

`prefix` is the 12-character display prefix — the same value `naive whoami` reports as `key_prefix`, and the only part of a secret that is ever readable. `last_used_at` is `null` for a key that has never authenticated a request, which makes unused keys easy to find:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive keys list --limit 100 | jq -r '.data[] | select(.last_used_at == null) | .id'
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--limit` | Page size. |
| `--after` | Cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`. |

## rotate & revoke

```bash theme={"system"}
naive keys rotate key_gwpjrs1egky00g6vw5gjczj6fs
naive keys revoke key_gwpjrs1egky00g6vw5gjczj6fs
```

Neither takes a flag; both take the key id as a positional argument.

`rotate` returns a new secret, once. `revoke` takes effect immediately — in-flight requests holding the old secret start failing with `401`. Both actions are recorded in the [audit log](/docs/cli/audit) as `api_key.rotated` and `api_key.revoked`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Test-mode keys (`sk_test_…`) run against the no-real-money seam: sessions execute and the ledger moves, but no charge reaches a payment processor. Check `mode` in [`naive whoami`](/docs/cli/auth#whoami) if you are unsure which you hold.


# naive identity legal
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/legal

Verify a persona's people and form a company from the command line.

Legal resources belong to a [persona](/docs/cli/identity), so every command takes `--identity`. Reached as `naive identity legal <command>` — three words, where `legal` is a sub-group rather than a positional argument. See [Legal](/docs/identity/legal) for the model and the [Legal API](/docs/api/legal) for the wire shapes.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive identity legal verifications` | List the persona's verification cases. |
| `naive identity legal verify` | Start a verification case for one or more members. |
| `naive identity legal verification` | Read one case with its members. |
| `naive identity legal complete` | Complete a member with the token from the hosted page. |
| `naive identity legal resend` | Mint a fresh hosted link for a member. |
| `naive identity legal companies` | List the persona's companies. |
| `naive identity legal form` | Form a company from a verified case (debits credits). |
| `naive identity legal company` | Read one company. |
| `naive identity legal submit` | File a paid company. |
| `naive identity legal documents` | List a company's documents. |
| `naive identity legal document` | Mint a short-lived link to one document. |
| `naive identity legal naics` | Search industry (NAICS) codes. |
| `naive identity legal states` | List the states a company can be formed in, with fees. |

`--identity` takes either an `idn_` id or the persona's name; the API resolves both. On a deployment with no legal provider bound, every command answers `501 feature_not_configured`.

## verify

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity legal verify --identity ava --members '[{"first_name":"Ava","last_name":"Stone","email":"ava@example.com","role":"primary","is_responsible_party":true,"ownership_percent":100}]'
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--members` | JSON array of members (required). Exactly one `primary`, exactly one responsible party, ownership summing to 100. |

The members are validated locally before the request; a malformed list exits `2`. Prints the case; the primary member's `link_url` is set on this response only.

## verifications / verification / complete / resend

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity legal verifications --identity ava --limit 20
naive identity legal verification --identity ava --verification lgv_…
naive identity legal complete --identity ava --verification lgv_… --member lgm_… --token <token>
naive identity legal resend --identity ava --verification lgv_… --member lgm_…
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--verification` | The `lgv_` id (required on the single-case commands). |
| `--member` | The `lgm_` id (required on `complete` and `resend`). |
| `--token` | The token the hosted page returns (required on `complete`). |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

## form

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity legal form --identity ava --company '{"verification_id":"lgv_…","state":"WY","name_options":["Acme Labs"],"naics_code":"541511","description":"Software consulting","mailing_address":{"line1":"1 Main St","line2":null,"city":"Cheyenne","state":"WY","postal_code":"82001","country":"US"}}'
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--company` | JSON body of the formation (required); validated locally. A bad field exits `2` naming it (`usage: --company: state — …`). |

The fee is debited from the organization's credits before anything is filed; a short balance answers `402 insufficient_credits` — the code is the first line on stderr and the exit code is `1`, as for every API refusal.

## companies / company / submit / documents / document

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity legal companies --identity ava
naive identity legal company --identity ava --company lgc_…
naive identity legal submit --identity ava --company lgc_…
naive identity legal documents --identity ava --company lgc_…
naive identity legal document --identity ava --company lgc_… --document lgd_…
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--company` | The `lgc_` id (required). |
| `--document` | The `lgd_` id (required on `document`). |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |

## naics / states

```bash theme={"system"}
naive identity legal naics --q software
naive identity legal states
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--q` | Search text for `naics`. |
| `--limit` / `--after` | Pagination. |


# MCP sessions
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/mcp-sessions

Mint, inspect, and immediately revoke bounded MCP credentials.

The `mcp` group manages [MCP sessions](/docs/api/mcp-sessions). Signed in as a person, `naive mcp create --name my-agent` connects your own agent. Naming `--scopes` and `--tools` makes a session for a system, and needs `admin`.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive mcp create \
  --name release-agent \
  --scopes agents:read,sessions:write \
  --tools agents_list,sessions_create \
  --expires-in 3600
```

Add `--identity idn_...` to label the session with a persona (recorded, not enforced yet). The create reply prints the bearer once;
store it immediately.

```bash theme={"system"}
naive mcp list --limit 20
naive mcp show mcs_...
naive mcp revoke mcs_...
```

`list` and `show` return only metadata and the non-sensitive prefix. `revoke` is one-way and is
enforced on the credential's next request.


# naive media
Source: https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/media

Generate images and video from the terminal, search the generation models and the stock photo library, cut a long video into short clips, transcribe a recording, turn text into speech, generate a sound effect, and answer a spoken turn with one.

`naive media generate` renders: an image comes back at once as [files](/docs/cli/files); a video is a **media job** you read back with `naive media show`. A recurring on-screen persona is a [character](/docs/cli/character), trained once and rendered as with `--character`. `naive media models` is how you learn a legal `--model`, for `generate` or to pin with [`naive agent tools`](/docs/cli/agents#tools).

`naive media edit` submits a Mira edit (`POST /v1/media/edits`) and `naive media edit` with `--wait` follows `GET /v1/media/edits/{id}`. `naive media clip <url>` turns a long video into short, scored, captioned clips as a job you poll with `naive media clip show`. `naive media models` is how you learn a legal `--model` to pin with [`naive agent tools`](/docs/cli/agents#tools), and what a session's `generate_image` / `generate_video` will accept. `naive media stock` searches the [stock photo library](/docs/api/images) for a licensed photo, free. `naive media transcribe`, `naive media speak`, `naive media sound-effect`, `naive media music` and `naive media converse` are the [audio](/docs/api/audio) routes from the terminal.

There is **no fixed list** of models. The catalogue is read from the provider on every call, so a model published today is callable today — and a model that never existed can never be offered.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `naive media generate --kind <image\|video> --prompt <text>` | Render an image (synchronous) or queue a video. |
| `naive media mesh [prompt] --image <fil_\|url>...` | Queue a 3D model from a description or 1–4 photos. |
| `naive media show <id>` | One media job. |
| `naive media list` | Media jobs, newest first. |
| `naive media models --kind <image\|video\|stt\|tts\|s2s>` | Search the models this deploy can render, transcribe or speak with. |
| `naive media stock "<query>"` | Search the stock photo library. Free; the call is booked at `$0`. |
| `naive media clip <url>` | Submit a video-clipping job; prints the queued `media_job`. |
| `naive media clip show <id>` | Read a clipping job back, with its clips once completed. |
| `naive media clips` | List clipping jobs, newest first. |
| `naive media skills build <url…>` | Build an org skill from 1–3 public reel links; prints the queued build. |
| `naive media skills revise <id> --feedback <text>` | Run the next round of a build. |
| `naive media skills get <id>` | Read a build back; reading moves it forward. |
| `naive media skills list` | List builds, newest first. |
| `naive media transcribe <file\|url>` | Transcribe a local file, a stored `fil_` or a public URL. |
| `naive media transcription <id>` | Re-read a transcription job. |
| `naive media speak "<text>"` | Turn text into a stored audio file. |
| `naive media edit "<prompt>" --video <fil_\|url>` | Submit a Mira edit (`POST /v1/media/edits`). `--wait` follows `GET /v1/media/edits/{id}`. |
| `naive media sound-effect "<prompt>"` | Generate a sound effect from a description, stored as a file. |
| `naive media music "<prompt>"` | Generate an original song from a description, stored as a file. |
| `naive media converse <file\|url>` | Answer a recorded spoken turn with a spoken reply, stored as a file. |

## generate

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind image --prompt "a paper kite over a grey harbour" --n 2 --aspect-ratio 16:9
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "image_generation",
  "model": "example/sketch",
  "files": [
    { "id": "fil_01J...", "object": "file", "name": "image-fil_01J....png", "content_type": "image/png", "size_bytes": 184233, "scope": "published", "session_id": null, "sha256": "…", "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z" },
    { "id": "fil_01J...", "object": "file", "name": "image-fil_01J....png", "content_type": "image/png", "size_bytes": 179910, "scope": "published", "session_id": null, "sha256": "…", "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z" }
  ],
  "cost_micro_usd": 60000
}
```

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind video --model heygen/heygen-video-1 --prompt "waves at dusk" --seconds 4
```

A video answers with the job in `queued`; `naive media show` it until it is `completed`, then `naive file download` the `result.files[0].file_id`. Or add `--wait` and the command polls for you, printing the finished job and exiting `0` on `completed`, `1` on `failed`:

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media generate --kind video --model heygen/heygen-video-1 --prompt "waves at dusk" --wait \
  | jq -r '.result.files[0].file_id' | xargs naive file download
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--kind` | **Required.** `image` or `video`. |
| `--prompt` | **Required.** What to render. |
| `--model` | A model id from `naive media models`. Optional: an image gets the platform's default image model, a video the first of the platform's video defaults the catalogue publishes — the standard video model, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-max`, `minimax/hailuo-3`, `bytedance/seedance-2.5`, then `alibaba/wan-3.0/text-to-video`. |
| `--image-url` | An image to edit, restyle or animate from — a stored `fil_` id or a public `http(s)` URL. Repeat for several (images only, up to 4). |
| `--character` | Render as a `ready` [character](/docs/cli/character), by `chr_` id or name. On an image it is the reference (not combined with `--image-url`); on `--kind video` it needs `--image-url <fil_>` of a still rendered as that character, which becomes the first frame. |
| `--style` | Images only: draw the image in a named look (`Library`, `Phone snap`, `Quiet luxury`, …; a character's usual looks are its `style_pack`). |
| `--character-strength` | Images only, with `--character`: 0.5 to 1, how strictly the face is held (try `0.85` for close-ups). Leave it out otherwise. |
| `--n` | Images only: how many, 1–4. Each is its own file. |
| `--seconds` | Video only: target duration, 1–60. |
| `--wait` | Video only: poll every 2 seconds until the job is `completed` or `failed` (at most the job's own 30-minute deadline). Exit code follows the outcome. |
| `--aspect-ratio` | Such as `16:9` or `9:16`. |
| `--seed` | Repeat an earlier result. |

The CLI sends the required `Idempotency-Key` for you; re-running the same command renders again.

## mesh

A textured GLB from a description or from one to four photos of the same object — a [media job](/docs/api/meshes) like a video. From a description it can also be rigged with an idle animation. For a part with real dimensions, build it instead: [`naive computer build-3d`](/docs/cli/computer#build-3d).

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media mesh "a weathered bronze lantern" --wait --out lantern.glb
naive media mesh --image fil_01J... --image fil_01K... --no-texture
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `[prompt]` | What to model. Give this or `--image`, not both. |
| `--image` | A photo of the object, a stored `fil_` id or a public `https` URL. Repeat for up to 4 views of the same object. |
| `--no-texture` | Geometry only, untextured; cheaper. |
| `--rig` | A description only: rig the model and give it an idle animation. |
| `--model` | A model id from `GET /v1/media/models?kind=mesh`. Optional: a description and photos each have a default. |
| `--wait` | Poll until the job is `completed` or `failed`, print it, and exit `0` or `1`. A model from a description takes several minutes. |
| `--out` | With `--wait`: save the finished GLB to this path. |

Each job is priced for the exact options it used, and only when it completes; a failed job is free. See [3D assets](/docs/capabilities/3d#pricing).

## show

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media show med_01J...
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "id": "med_01J...",
  "object": "media_job",
  "kind": "video",
  "status": "completed",
  "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1",
  "input": { "model": "heygen/heygen-video-1", "prompt": "waves at dusk", "seconds": 4 },
  "result": { "files": [{ "file_id": "fil_01J...", "content_type": "video/mp4", "width": null, "height": null, "duration_seconds": null }] },
  "error": null,
  "cost_micro_usd": 412000,
  "session_id": null,
  "created_at": "2026-09-06T12:00:00.000Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-09-06T12:03:41.000Z"
}
```

A failed job carries `error: { code, message }` and `cost_micro_usd: 0` — a job that fails is not billed.

## list

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media list --kind video --status processing
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--kind` | `video`, `mesh` or `transcription`. Clipping jobs have their own list, [`naive media clips`](#clips). |
| `--status` | `queued`, `processing`, `completed` or `failed`. |
| `--session` | Jobs one session's agent submitted. Jobs from the API or CLI have `session_id: null`. |
| `--limit` | Page size, 1–100. |
| `--after` | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |

## models

```bash theme={"system"}
naive media models --kind video --search seedance
```

```json theme={"system"}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "media_model",
      "id": "bytedance/seedance-2.5",
      "name": "Seedance 2.5",
      "kind": "video",
      "description": "A text- and image-to-video model for short cinematic clips."
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false,
  "next_cursor": null
}
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--kind` | **Required.** `image`, `video`, `stt`, `tts` or `s2s`. Each is its own capability with its own catalogue, so there is nothing to default to. |
